title: /backfill spawns a non-existent script — command is permanently broken
detail: execute() spawns `npx tsx scripts/backfill-message-activity.ts <guildId> <weeks> [--dry-run]`, but that file does not exist anywhere in the repo (verified via filesystem + grep; the only references to `backfill-message-activity` are this command, the legacy BACKFILL-NOW.sh, and docs). The real backfill entrypoint is `scripts/backfill/run.ts`, which has a completely different CLI (`--channels=...`, `--skip-reactions`, `--resume-only`) and takes no positional guildId/weeks args. As a result every /backfill invocation immediately fails: tsx exits non-zero with a module-not-found error, the `close` handler reports `❌ Backfill Failed` (or the `error` handler logs a spawn failure), and no data is ever backfilled. The heatmap that /backfill is meant to populate stays empty. Staff-facing command that can never succeed.
fix: Point spawn at the actual script and pass the arguments it expects, e.g. `spawn('npx', ['tsx', 'scripts/backfill/run.ts', ...])` adapted to run.ts's flag-based interface (it currently parses `--channels=` etc., not positional guildId/weeks). Either add a thin `scripts/backfill-message-activity.ts` shim that accepts `<guildId> <weeks>` and calls into the run.ts logic, or rewrite the command to invoke run.ts with the flags it supports. Also update BACKFILL-NOW.sh. Add a smoke test that asserts the spawned script path exists.

title: Byte token redemption is non-atomic and has no rollback — a failed grant destroys the token entitlement with nothing in return
detail: handleConfirm() mutates Discord and the DB in this order inside one try/catch with no compensating action: (1) remove the token role (line 314), (2) remove other multiplier roles (lines 321-345), (3) add the multiplier role (line 348), (3.5) refetch + cleanup (lines 357-382), (4) upsertActiveMultiplier writes the DB source-of-truth (lines 385-394). If ANY step after the token removal throws (e.g. roles.add at 348 hits a 50013/permission change, a 429, or the gateway hiccups), control jumps to the catch at 449 which only shows an error embed. The token role is already gone, the multiplier role was never granted, and NO row was written to active_byte_multipliers. The user has permanently spent a finite token entitlement and received zero value, with no automatic recovery path (the scheduler only removes roles; nothing re-grants tokens). Because the multiplier roles ARE the economy (see byteMultiplierStore multiplier_value is never read — XP boost is driven purely by role possession), this is direct, silent value destruction. The DB write should be the authoritative claim and should happen first/atomically, or the whole sequence must be made compensatable.
fix: Make the token claim the atomic gate before any irreversible Discord mutation. Insert into a redeemed-tokens ledger (or upsert active_byte_multipliers) inside a transaction FIRST; only on a successful insert proceed to Discord role changes. On any Discord failure after the token role is removed, re-add the token role in a finally/catch (compensating action) and delete the just-written DB row, so the user keeps their token. Alternatively, add the multiplier role BEFORE removing the token role, so a mid-flight failure leaves the user holding the token (recoverable) rather than holding nothing.

title: Failed remote DB migration is swallowed, then PM2 restarts new code against an un-migrated database
detail: Step 6.5 runs the migration as: ssh_remote "cd ${REMOTE_PATH} && node scripts/migrate-remote.js" || echo "Migration step completed (may have warnings)". Because the failure branch is `echo` (which always exits 0), a non-zero exit from the migration is discarded even under `set -euo pipefail`. Control then proceeds to Step 7 (lines 449-455) which unconditionally runs `pm2 startOrRestart ecosystem.config.cjs`, bringing up the new bot + web code against a database whose schema was NOT migrated (or was left half-migrated). docs/reference/database-schema-safety.md:13 explicitly promises the opposite: 'If a migration fails, the rest of the deploy bails.' This is the single highest-impact ops defect: a migration error produces a green-looking deploy and a running bot that will throw at runtime on missing columns/tables (see src/config/flaggerStore.ts:211 which already handles 'column missing - migration may not have run'). The pre-deploy backup (maybe_backup_remote_db) does not help because the code is still rolled forward on top of the old schema.
fix: Do not swallow the migration exit code. Either remove the `|| echo ...` so `set -e` aborts, or capture status explicitly and abort before the PM2 restart, e.g.: `if ! ssh_remote "cd ${REMOTE_PATH} && node scripts/migrate-remote.js"; then echo 'ERROR: migration failed, aborting deploy (code NOT restarted)'; exit 1; fi`. Keep the lock trap so the lock is released on abort.

title: Byte token redemption is non-atomic: token role is removed before the multiplier is granted/tracked, so a mid-flow failure destroys the entitlement with nothing in return
detail: handleConfirm performs a multi-step Discord+DB sequence with no transaction or rollback: Step 1 removes the token role (line 314-317), Step 3 adds the multiplier role (line 348-351), Step 4 writes the DB tracking row via upsertActiveMultiplier (line 385-394). These are independent awaited Discord REST calls plus a SQLite write. If the bot crashes, the process is killed, or roles.add() throws (rate-limit 429, transient 500, hierarchy change between the pre-flight canManageRole check at line 245 and the actual add) AFTER the token role has already been removed at line 314, the user has permanently lost their byte token (the giveaway/shop entitlement) and received no multiplier. The catch block at line 449 only edits the reply with a generic error; it does NOT re-add the removed token role. Because the token role IS the entitlement (there is no separate balance ledger - see usebyte.ts findMemberByteTokens which reads role presence as the source of truth), this is an irreversible economic loss. Cross-file: usebyte.ts treats role presence as the wallet, while byteTokenHandler.ts mutates that wallet non-transactionally and trusts that every step after the destructive remove() will succeed.
fix: Reorder to grant-then-consume (add multiplier + write DB row FIRST, remove token role LAST), so a failure leaves the user still holding the token. Alternatively, on any failure after the token removal, compensate by re-adding the token role in the catch block. Best: record an intent/ledger row before touching Discord and reconcile on restart.

title: Migration 039 runs on a second DB connection outside the runner's transaction and never records itself (perpetual re-run, broken atomicity)
detail: Unlike every other migration in the project (which is exported as migrateNNN(db: Database) and receives the runner's connection), migrate039FixArtJobUniqueConstraint() takes NO parameter and instead does `import { db } from "../src/db/db.js"` (line 12), operating on the singleton connection opened by src/db/db.ts. The runner in scripts/migrate.ts (lines 195-213) loads the function via name `migrate039FixArtJobUniqueConstraint`, then runs it inside `db.transaction(() => migrateFn(db))` using ITS OWN better-sqlite3 handle (scripts/migrate.ts line 50). Three concrete consequences: (1) Atomicity is broken. All of 039's writes (the renumber UPDATEs on lines 44-48, DROP INDEX line 53, CREATE UNIQUE INDEX lines 56-59) execute on the singleton connection via autocommit, completely outside the runner's transaction. The runner's transaction stays empty (it issues no writes on its own connection), so if 039 throws partway (e.g. the UNIQUE index creation fails because a duplicate slipped through), the renumber UPDATEs are already committed and will NOT roll back. (2) recordMigration is never called (compare every other migration, e.g. 040 line 135, 038 line 33). The runner does not record versions itself (scripts/migrate.ts applyMigration has no recordMigration call), so version "039" is never inserted into schema_migrations and 039 is treated as pending on every single run -- it re-executes each time `migrate.ts` runs and forces a fresh backup every run (scripts/migrate.ts line 253 filters by appliedVersions which never contains 039). (3) Importing src/db/db.ts from inside the migration process triggers that module's large top-level schema bootstrap (tables + addColumnIfMissing + index creation, src/db/db.ts lines 113-419) to run on a SECOND WAL connection to the same file during the migration -- an unexpected, heavy side effect and a second live handle to the DB the runner is migrating.
fix: Refactor 039 to the standard signature: `export function migrate039FixArtJobUniqueConstraint(db: Database): void` and remove the `import { db } from "../src/db/db.js"`. Use the passed-in `db` for all statements so the work runs inside the runner's transaction. Add `recordMigration(db, "039", "fix_art_job_unique_constraint")` at the end (importing it from ./lib/helpers.js) so the migration is recorded and stops re-running.

title: Patreon art-grant backfill iterates role.members without fetching members → silently grants nothing
detail: After login the script does `const guild = client.guilds.cache.get(guildId)` and then iterates `role.members` (line 100) to backfill `patreon_art_granted` ticket quantities. It never calls `guild.members.fetch()`. `role.members` is a live filter over the guild member cache, which is essentially empty for a freshly-connected client (Discord only pushes a small set during READY even with the GuildMembers intent). As a result `role.members.size` is 0 (or near-0) for every tier, the inner loop never runs, and the script prints 'Processing <tier> (0 members)' followed by 'Backfill complete: 0 members, 0 grant records.' — exiting 0 as if it succeeded. Because this is the one-time economy backfill that must run after migration 062 and before enabling `patreon_art_rewards_enabled`, entitled Patreon supporters silently never get their headshot/fullbody/emoji ticket grants backfilled, and the silent success makes the gap easy to miss. The sibling scripts backfill-user-cache.ts and backfill-user-cache.mjs prove the intended pattern: they `await guild.members.fetch()` before reading members.
fix: Fetch members before reading role membership: replace `const guild = client.guilds.cache.get(guildId)` with `const guild = await client.guilds.fetch(guildId); await guild.members.fetch();` (or call `guild.members.fetch()` immediately after the cache.get null-check). This populates the cache so `role.members` is correctly populated for every tier.

title: Copy-swap re-runs strftime('%s', created_at) on already-INTEGER epoch values, corrupting every timestamp
detail: needsMigration() returns true if ANY of {CHECK present, created_at!=INTEGER, FK!=CASCADE, missing idx_review_action_app_time} holds (line 86). Unlike migration 028 (which early-returns the moment created_at is already INTEGER), this script has NO such guard: if the table is otherwise fully correct (created_at already INTEGER Unix epoch) but merely lacks the idx_review_action_app_time index or has a non-CASCADE FK, runMigration() still executes the full copy-swap. The INSERT...SELECT then applies CAST(strftime('%s', created_at) AS INTEGER) to the already-INTEGER epoch column (lines 128-135). I verified in better-sqlite3 that strftime('%s', 1700000000) does NOT return NULL — it treats the integer as a date-ish numeric and returns garbage (e.g. 1700000000 -> 1780244213, ~year 2026), so COALESCE keeps the corrupted value. Result: running this 'repair' on a healthy DB that is only missing an index silently rewrites EVERY review_action.created_at to a bogus timestamp, destroying the audit trail's chronology and breaking idx_review_action_app_time ordering / time-range analytics. The transaction's only integrity check is row COUNT (lines 143-145), which still matches, so the corruption passes undetected.
fix: Mirror migration 028's guard: in needsMigration(), if getCreatedAtType()==='INTEGER', do NOT trigger the destructive copy-swap solely for a missing index or FK fix — instead create the index / rebuild only when a real schema (CHECK or TEXT created_at) problem exists, and add the index via a plain CREATE INDEX when that is the only deficiency. Equivalently, in the INSERT...SELECT only apply strftime conversion when the source created_at type is TEXT; when it is already INTEGER, copy created_at verbatim.

title: /gate reset wipes ALL guilds' data, not just the current guild
detail: In executeReset -> 'wipe_tables', the deletes are unscoped: runDelete("DELETE FROM application"), "DELETE FROM application_response", "DELETE FROM review_action", "DELETE FROM modmail_bridge", "DELETE FROM review_card", "DELETE FROM avatar_scan", "DELETE FROM review_claim" all run with no WHERE guild_id clause. These tables carry a guild_id column (confirmed in db schema / migrations / test fixtures: application.guild_id NOT NULL). The very next step, 'wipe_guild_question' (line 397-411), IS correctly scoped with "DELETE FROM guild_question WHERE guild_id = ?", and the confirmation modal customId is guild-scoped (v1:gate:reset:${guildId}). So the intent is clearly a per-guild reset, but the bulk deletes nuke every guild's applications/responses/actions/modmail bridges/claims that share this SQLite file. Any second guild (e.g. a staging/test guild, or future multi-tenant use) loses all of its gate data when a mod in one guild runs reset. The bot uses guild_id pervasively and supports per-guild config, so this is a genuine multi-guild data-loss bug; even in the current single-prod-guild deployment it is a latent footgun that diverges from the scoped questions wipe.
fix: Scope every delete by guild_id, mirroring the questions wipe. e.g. db.prepare('DELETE FROM application WHERE guild_id = ?').run(guildId); for review_action/modmail_bridge/review_card/avatar_scan/review_claim which key off app_id, delete via subquery: DELETE FROM review_action WHERE app_id IN (SELECT id FROM application WHERE guild_id = ?). Run application delete last (or capture app ids first) so the subqueries still resolve, all inside the existing transaction.

title: verified_users row is inserted BEFORE the role grant; grant failure leaves a verified record with no role and the 'already verified' check then lies
detail: The flow inserts into verified_users first (lines 196-198), then attempts member.roles.add (lines 206-217) inside a try/catch that ONLY logs on failure (logger.error at 216) and continues. If the role add fails (missing Manage Roles permission, role above the bot in hierarchy, transient API error, member fetch failure), the user is permanently recorded as verified in the DB but never receives the Thin Line role. The log embed is still sent with 'Role Granted: Failed', but the user is told 'Thank you for your service. You have been given the Thin Line role.' (line 219) regardless. Worse, if they re-run /verify, the existence check at lines 69-81 finds the row and replies 'You're already verified ... You have the Thin Line role.' so they can never recover the role through the command. The write is non-idempotent w.r.t. the actual desired state (DB row + role).
fix: Grant the role first (and treat a failed grant as a hard failure that aborts before the INSERT), or wrap both in a compensating flow: if roles.add throws, do not insert (or delete the just-inserted row) and tell the user verification could not be completed. At minimum, make the success DM and embed conditional on roleGranted, and make the 'already verified' path re-attempt the role grant if the member lacks the role.

title: Game-night and movie-night attendance overwrite each other (UNIQUE constraint missing event_type)
detail: finalizeGameAttendance writes to movie_attendance with `INSERT OR REPLACE ... VALUES (..., 'game', ...)` keyed implicitly on the table's UNIQUE constraint. That constraint is `UNIQUE(guild_id, user_id, event_date)` (migrations/025_role_automation.ts:111) and migration 040 (which added the event_type column) only ALTERs in the column + a NON-unique index `idx_movie_attendance_event_type`; it never rebuilds the unique key to include event_type. event_date is a date-only string `YYYY-MM-DD` (src/commands/event/game.ts:92, src/commands/event/movie.ts:88). Movie night finalize uses the same table with the same date (src/features/movieNight.ts:292-295). Therefore, if a user attends both a movie night and a game night on the same calendar day, whichever event is finalized second silently REPLACES the other event's row, destroying the first event's attendance/qualification record and corrupting tier counts (getUserQualifiedGameCount / getUserTotalEventCount). The same applies to creditHistoricalGameAttendance (lines 744-757) and bumpGameAttendance (lines 816-829) whose `ON CONFLICT(guild_id, user_id, event_date)` cannot even reference event_type because it is not a unique key — at runtime this ON CONFLICT clause resolves against the (guild_id,user_id,event_date) unique index and will collide with a movie record of the same day.
fix: Add event_type to the uniqueness key: create a migration that rebuilds movie_attendance with `UNIQUE(guild_id, user_id, event_date, event_type)` (SQLite requires create-new-table + copy + drop + rename), or add a separate `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... ON movie_attendance(guild_id,user_id,event_date,event_type)` after dropping the old unique index, then update all INSERT OR REPLACE / ON CONFLICT targets accordingly.

title: PM2 self-stop kills the process mid-restore, so file replacement/verify/restart never run
detail: restoreCandidate with pm2Coord=true runs `await execAsync('pm2 stop ' + processName)` (line 506) BEFORE replacing the DB file (line 544) and before restarting PM2 (line 620). The live restore button (src/features/dbRecoveryButtons.ts:193-199) invokes this path with pm2Coord:true and the bot itself is the PM2-managed process (env.PM2_PROCESS_NAME). When PM2 stops that very process, the running Node event loop is terminated, so the awaited execAsync never resolves and steps 4–6 (copyFile of the candidate over the live DB, post-restore verification, `pm2 start`) never execute. Result: the database is NOT restored, PM2 may leave the app stopped, and the Discord reply promising success is never sent. The pre-restore backup is created (step 2) but the actual restore silently no-ops.
fix: Do not stop the running bot from within itself. Either (a) perform the copy + integrity verify FIRST while running, then schedule a detached `pm2 restart` (spawned with detached:true / unref) as the final step, or (b) move restore into an out-of-process CLI/worker (src/ops/dbRecoverCli.ts) that PM2 does not manage, or (c) use better-sqlite3's online backup API to replace data without stopping the process.

title: ensureGateEntry calls .has() on fetchPins().items which is a plain Array, throwing TypeError after a successful pin
detail: In discord.js 14.26.4 (the pinned version, ^14.26.4), MessageManager.fetchPins() returns `{ hasMore: boolean, items: readonly MessagePin[] }` where `items` is a plain readonly Array (typings/index.d.ts lines 6581-6590). The pin-verification block casts `items` to `{ has: (id) => boolean }` and calls `pinnedItems.has(message.id)`. Arrays have `includes`, not `has`, so `pinnedItems.has` is undefined and the call throws `TypeError: pinnedItems.has is not a function`. This runs INSIDE the try at line 596 AFTER message.pin() has already succeeded; the catch at 615 logs and then re-throws (line 623). ensureGateEntry is awaited inside withStep('ensure_entry', ...) in src/commands/gate/gateMain.ts:214, and withStep propagates (cmdWrap.ts:392, 'caught by wrapCommand upstream'). Net effect: every /gate setup (and /update re-ensure at update.ts:427) that successfully pins the panel still surfaces an error card to the staff user, even though the panel was created and pinned correctly. Note the SAME file's findExistingGateEntry (lines 160-167) correctly treats items as an array of {message}, proving the intended shape.
fix: Replace the Collection-style `.has()` access with array semantics consistent with the rest of the file: `const pinnedItems = (pinnedResponse as { items?: ReadonlyArray<{ message?: Message }> }).items; const pinnedMatch = Array.isArray(pinnedItems) ? pinnedItems.some((it) => it?.message?.id === message.id) : false;`. Then the success path returns result without throwing.

title: Reopen within 7 days of a DELETED thread commits open-state then throws, leaving an orphaned 'open' ticket pointing at a dead thread
detail: On close, the default config modmail_delete_on_close (treated as true unless explicitly false in threadClose.ts:365 and :546) DELETES the Discord thread. reopenModmailThread first commits a transaction that flips the ticket to status='open' and re-inserts the open_modmail guard row (lines 89-109), then calls addOpenThread(ticket.thread_id) restoring the in-memory routing set (lines 113-116), and ONLY THEN does `interaction.client.channels.fetch(ticket.thread_id)` (line 120). For a thread that was deleted on close, that fetch rejects with Unknown Channel (10003), which is caught by the outer try/catch (line 150) and returns {success:false}. But the DB transaction and addOpenThread have already taken effect. Result: the ticket is now marked 'open' with a thread_id that no longer exists, the open_modmail guard row blocks the user from ever getting a NEW modmail (openPublicModmailThreadFor short-circuits on the existing guard row), and OPEN_MODMAIL_THREADS/handleInboundDmForModmail will route the applicant's DMs to a dead thread (silently failing). Because delete-on-close is the default, virtually every recently-closed ticket has a deleted thread, so the common `/modmail reopen user:@x` path (closed_at within 7 days -> reopen branch, lines 72-85) reliably lands in this broken state. The staff member is told 'Failed to reopen' while the system is left inconsistent.
fix: Fetch and unarchive/unlock the thread BEFORE mutating the DB and in-memory set, and treat a missing/deleted thread explicitly: if the thread can't be fetched (null or fetch throws), do NOT reopen in place — instead fall through to creating a fresh thread via openPublicModmailThreadFor (as the >7-day branch already does). Alternatively, wrap the unarchive in its own try/catch and roll back (reopenTicket->close, delete the open_modmail row, removeOpenThread) if the thread is gone. Either way, never leave status='open' with a thread_id that fails to resolve.

title: BigInt() called on comma-separated permission NAMES, not numeric bitfields — diff/dangerous-change code throws on real data
detail: Every consumer in this file treats RoleSnapshot.permissions and PermissionOverwriteSnapshot.allow/deny as numeric bitfield strings: `new PermissionsBitField(BigInt(oldRole.permissions))` (256-257), `BigInt(oldOw.allow/deny)` (346-349), `BigInt(bitfield)` in bitfieldToPermissionNames (382), and `BigInt(role.permissions)` in getDangerousChanges (414). But the ONLY producers of those fields are roleToSnapshot/channelToSnapshot in src/features/serverAudit/types.ts (lines 234, 252-253), which store comma-separated permission NAMES: `permissions: role.permissions.join(',')` and `allow/deny: ow.allow.join(',')`. At runtime a snapshot holds e.g. `"Administrator,ManageRoles"` or `"ViewChannel"`. `BigInt("ViewChannel")` throws `SyntaxError: Cannot convert ViewChannel to a BigInt`. Trigger paths: (a) computeSnapshotDiff itself calls getDangerousChanges(diff) at line 247, so it throws whenever diff.rolesAdded is non-empty (any role added since last audit has ≥1 perm) or whenever computeRoleChange runs for a role whose permissions string changed; (b) computeOverwriteModification throws whenever a channel overwrite's allow/deny string changes. Impact: In src/commands/audit/diff.ts the catch at line 141 surfaces `❌ Failed to compute diff: Cannot convert ... to a BigInt` to the user — `/audit diff` is broken for any server with real permission changes. In src/features/serverAuditDocs.ts the whole block is wrapped in a silent try/catch (line 174), so DIFF.md is never written and result.dangerousChangeCount stays 0 — dangerous permission escalations (Admin/ManageRoles/Ban added to a role) are silently never detected or alerted, a security-monitoring failure. The unit test masks this because tests/features/securityDiff.test.ts only ever uses `permissions: "0"` / `""` (BigInt("0")=0n, BigInt("")=0n do not throw) and never diffs two roles that actually differ in a named permission.
fix: Make producers and consumers agree on one format. Simplest: since snapshots already store comma-separated names, replace the BigInt/PermissionsBitField parsing with set-diffing of the name lists, e.g. `const oldSet = new Set(oldRole.permissions ? oldRole.permissions.split(',') : []);` then compute added = newSet items not in oldSet and removed = oldSet items not in newSet. Do the same for allow/deny in computeOverwriteModification and overwritesAdded/removed, and make bitfieldToPermissionNames just `bitfield ? bitfield.split(',') : []`. Alternatively change roleToSnapshot/channelToSnapshot to store the real numeric bitfield (role.permissions.bitfield.toString()) — but that requires re-fetching bitfields in analyze.ts (RoleData.permissions is already names-only), so the split-based fix is safer. Add a test where two roles differ by a named permission to prevent regression.

title: `modmail_delete_on_close` opt-out is silently ignored — threads always deleted on close
detail: Both close paths compute the delete decision as `cfg?.modmail_delete_on_close !== false` (line 365 in `closeModmailThread`, line 546 in `closeModmailForApplication` feeding `archiveOrDeleteThread`). The `GuildConfig` type declares `modmail_delete_on_close?: boolean | null`, but that is a type-level lie. The column is created as `INTEGER DEFAULT 1` (src/lib/config.ts:375, ensureModRolesColumns), the config command stores the boolean via upsert which converts `false`->integer `0` / `true`->`1` (src/lib/config.ts:687; src/commands/config/setFeatures.ts:300-304), and `getConfig` does `SELECT *` and returns the raw row with no boolean coercion (src/lib/config.ts:707-724). So at runtime `cfg.modmail_delete_on_close` is the NUMBER `0` or `1`, never a boolean. `0 !== false` evaluates to `true` (strict inequality: number 0 is not boolean false), so `preferDelete`/`deleteOnClose` is `true` even when an admin explicitly set 'Delete on Close = off' (stored as 0). Impact: every modmail close DELETES the Discord thread regardless of the setting, irreversibly destroying the in-channel thread/history against explicit admin opt-out. The opt-out path (archive+lock, keep thread) is unreachable.
fix: Compare the integer truthiness instead of strict boolean inequality. Either coerce in getConfig (e.g. `modmail_delete_on_close: config.modmail_delete_on_close == null ? null : !!config.modmail_delete_on_close`) or change the consumers to `const preferDelete = cfg?.modmail_delete_on_close !== 0 && cfg?.modmail_delete_on_close !== false;` (default true only when null/undefined). Cleanest: normalize all INTEGER-boolean config columns to real booleans on read in getConfig.

title: Ticket open button has no dedup/cooldown — double-click creates duplicate channels and burns numbers
detail: handleOpenButton defers ephemerally then calls TicketService.create() with no per-user/per-type guard. TicketService.create() (src/features/tickets/service.ts:214-352) never checks for an existing open ticket of the same type for the opener — it unconditionally allocateNextNumber(), creates a Discord channel, posts a greeting with role pings, and inserts a ticket row. The interactionCreate router (src/events/interactionCreate.ts:582-595) routes tk: buttons directly to handleTicketButton with no checkCooldown wrapper (unlike error-card buttons which do gate on a cooldown). Discord button double-clicks are extremely common, and because the first interaction is deferred (not yet replied) the second click is still a valid, separately-dispatched interaction. Two near-simultaneous clicks each create a full ticket channel, each consume a ticket number, and each fire pingRoleIds notifications. Impact: orphan/duplicate ticket channels, wasted ticket numbers, duplicate staff pings, and user confusion about which channel is real.
fix: Add a guard before creation: either (a) a short per-(userId, typeKey) cooldown via checkCooldown around handleOpenButton, and/or (b) in TicketService.create(), SELECT for an existing open ticket WHERE opener_user_id = ? AND type_key = ? AND status = 'open' and short-circuit (reply with a link to the existing channel) instead of opening another. A UNIQUE partial index on (opener_user_id, type_key) WHERE status='open' would make it race-proof.

title: Intended-ephemeral claim feedback becomes a public edit of the review card (flags dropped after deferUpdate)
detail: handleClaimToggle is always entered AFTER the parent handleReviewButton called interaction.deferUpdate() (src/features/review/handlers/buttons.ts:177-181). deferUpdate() sets interaction.deferred = true (discord.js InteractionResponses.deferUpdate -> this.deferred = true), and for a component interaction the response '@original' is the message the button is attached to: the public review card. Every feedback call here uses replyOrEdit(interaction, { content, flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }). But replyOrEdit (src/lib/cmdWrap.ts:503-506) takes the deferred branch and explicitly strips flags (`const { flags, ...editPayload } = withFlags; interaction.editReply(editPayload)`), which PATCHes '@original'. Net effect: messages meant to be private to the clicking moderator -- 'This application is already claimed by another moderator.', 'Cannot claim: application is already X.', 'An unexpected error occurred.', and especially 'This user has been permanently rejected from <server> and cannot reapply.' (lines 91-93) -- are written publicly onto the shared review card, overwriting its content line and exposing internal moderation state to everyone who can see the channel. The success path (lines 146-150) similarly edits the card content rather than sending the intended per-mod confirmation.
fix: After an upstream deferUpdate(), do not use replyOrEdit for per-moderator feedback. Use interaction.followUp({ content, flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }) directly (followUp preserves flags and posts a separate ephemeral message), or have replyOrEdit honor ephemeral by routing to followUp when the interaction was deferred via deferUpdate rather than calling editReply. At minimum, stop stripping flags for genuinely ephemeral content.

title: Unclaim feedback/errors also leak onto the public review card (same deferUpdate + stripped-flags path)
detail: handleUnclaimAction is invoked from handleUnclaimModal (src/features/review/handlers/modals.ts:242-270), which calls interaction.deferUpdate() before delegating. As with claim, interaction.deferred is true, so every replyOrEdit({ ..., flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }) here (NOT_CLAIMED / NOT_OWNER / APP_NOT_FOUND error strings, the unexpected-error string, and the 'Application `CODE` unclaimed successfully.' confirmation at 243-248) is turned into a public editReply on the review card with the ephemeral flag discarded (src/lib/cmdWrap.ts:505). Owner-mismatch and not-claimed messages intended for one mod are shown to the whole channel and clobber the card's content line.
fix: Same as the claim finding: send these as interaction.followUp({ content, flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }) instead of relying on replyOrEdit (which drops flags on the deferred/editReply branch).

title: Failed Discord thread creation leaves an orphan open ticket that permanently blocks future modmail for the user
detail: The race-protection transaction (lines 227-263) atomically commits BOTH a new modmail_ticket row (createTicket, line 241, status defaults to 'open' per db.ts:185) AND a 'pending' open_modmail guard row. If the subsequent Discord thread creation (forum.threads.create line 289 or textChannel.threads.create line 298) throws — e.g. transient 500, rate limit, or perms revoked between the precheck and the call — control jumps to the catch (line 440). The cleanup there (lines 476-479) deletes ONLY the 'pending' open_modmail row; it never deletes the orphan modmail_ticket row. That row remains with status='open', thread_id=NULL. There is a partial unique index idx_modmail_open_unique ON modmail_ticket(guild_id,user_id,status) WHERE status='open' (db.ts:195-198). On the user's NEXT open attempt, the open_modmail fast-path is clear (pending was deleted), so execution re-enters the transaction and createTicket runs INSERT INTO modmail_ticket with default status='open' -> violates the partial unique index -> throws SQLITE_CONSTRAINT. The catch then misclassifies this as isRaceCondition (line 448 matches 'SQLITE_CONSTRAINT'), finds no open_modmail row, and returns the generic 'Failed to create modmail thread' error. Net effect: once thread creation fails, that applicant can never have a modmail thread opened again until someone manually deletes the orphan ticket row from the DB. The stated invariant in the code comment ('if INSERT into open_modmail fails we don't leave orphan tickets') only covers the open_modmail collision, not a post-transaction Discord failure.
fix: In the catch block's cleanup, also remove the just-created ticket when the thread was never created. Either (a) wrap the ticket delete with the pending-row delete in one transaction keyed on ticketId: DELETE FROM modmail_ticket WHERE id = ? AND thread_id IS NULL AND status='open', or (b) defer createTicket until after the Discord thread exists (only the 'pending' open_modmail row needs to be inserted in the locking transaction). Also avoid classifying a modmail_ticket unique-index violation as a 'race' that links to a non-existent open_modmail row.

title: Movie tier count includes game-night attendance (cross-event-type contamination)
detail: getUserQualifiedMovieCount() counts every qualified row in movie_attendance for the user with NO event_type filter (WHERE guild_id=? AND user_id=? AND qualified=1). Game nights (src/features/events/gameNight.ts) persist into the SAME movie_attendance table with event_type='game' (finalizeGameAttendance, lines 247-253). This count is the basis for movie tier-role promotion in updateMovieTierRole (movieNight.ts:391). Result: a user who qualifies only for game nights is granted Movie-Night tier roles (and the reverse: getUserTotalEventCount in gameNight.ts:344 is also unfiltered). The economy/role-reward is inflated and wrong. Note gameNight.ts:331 getUserQualifiedGameCount correctly filters event_type='game', proving the movie side simply forgot the filter.
fix: Add AND event_type = 'movie' to getUserQualifiedMovieCount (and decide intended semantics for getUserTotalEventCount). e.g. SELECT COUNT(*) ... WHERE guild_id=? AND user_id=? AND event_type='movie' AND qualified=1.

title: Movie and game attendance collide on UNIQUE(guild_id,user_id,event_date); same-day REPLACE drops a row
detail: movie_attendance has UNIQUE(guild_id,user_id,event_date) (migrations/025_role_automation.ts:111) and event_type was added later with DEFAULT 'movie' (migration 040). finalizeMovieAttendance writes via INSERT OR REPLACE without specifying event_type (so it defaults to 'movie'), while finalizeGameAttendance (gameNight.ts:247) writes the same key with event_type='game'. The UNIQUE key does NOT include event_type, so if the same user attends both a movie night and a game night on the same calendar date, the second finalize REPLACEs (deletes+reinserts) the first event's row entirely. One event's attendance/qualification is silently lost. The manual-adjust helpers (creditHistoricalAttendance ON CONFLICT, bumpAttendance) have the same key collision.
fix: Include event_type in the uniqueness model: change the constraint to UNIQUE(guild_id,user_id,event_date,event_type) (new migration) and update all ON CONFLICT targets to match; or incorporate event_type into a synthetic key. Until then movie and game nights cannot safely share a date.

title: env.test.ts schema has drifted from src/lib/env.ts and asserts the OPPOSITE of real behavior (false confidence)
detail: This test defines its OWN local `envSchema` (lines 30-38) and never imports the real schema from src/lib/env.ts. Two concrete drifts make the test misleading: (1) NODE_ENV. The local enum is z.enum(["development", "production"]) (line 34). The REAL schema (src/lib/env.ts line 118) is z.enum(["development", "production", "test"]). The test's comments and intent explicitly assert that "test" is REJECTED — line 28 ("no 'staging', 'test', etc."), line 94 ("NODE_ENV must be exactly 'development' or 'production'"), line 96 ("Other values like 'staging', 'test', 'local' are rejected"). The real schema ACCEPTS "test". So the only NODE_ENV-negative test uses "staging" (line 101), which happens to fail in both, hiding the drift. (2) RESET_PASSWORD. The real schema requires RESET_PASSWORD (src/lib/env.ts line 136, .min(1)). The local schema omits it entirely, so the 'complete environment' (line 41) and 'apply default values' (line 61) cases pass here but would FAIL against the real schema. Net impact: a real regression to env validation (e.g., someone removing the RESET_PASSWORD requirement, or restricting NODE_ENV to drop 'test' and breaking the test run-mode at src/lib/env.ts line 32 `process.env.NODE_ENV === "test"`) would not be caught by this suite. The test gives false confidence that env validation is verified.
fix: Import and test the actual schema/env module instead of a hand-maintained copy (e.g., export the zod schema from src/lib/env.ts and import it here, or drive process.env + dynamic import of env.ts). At minimum, sync the local enum to include "test", add RESET_PASSWORD to the local object/required-field tests, and fix the now-incorrect comments at lines 28/94/96.

title: pretty.test.ts exercises ZERO source code — entire suite is tautological, gives false coverage for the audit-logging module
detail: This file purports to test src/logging/pretty.ts (logActionPretty / getActionMeta / the action_log INSERT / embed building). It sets up vi.mock for db, logger, time, loggingStore and features/logger (lines 10-49), but it NEVER imports anything from ../../src/logging/pretty.js. Every single `it(...)` re-declares a local literal and asserts on that literal, e.g.: line 178-182 `const meta = { title:'Application Submitted', color:0x5865f2, emoji:'📝' }; expect(meta.color).toBe(0x5865f2)`; line 266 `const query='INSERT INTO action_log'; expect(query).toContain('action_log')`; line 301-305 `const dbFailed=true; const shouldContinue=!dbFailed; expect(shouldContinue).toBe(false)`; line 287-291 `JSON.stringify({key:'value'})` equality; line 343-347 `appId.slice(-6).toUpperCase()` length. None of these call getActionMeta(), logActionPretty(), or any real symbol. Impact: the suite would stay 100% green if pretty.ts were deleted, if a getActionMeta color/emoji/title were wrong, if the action_log INSERT column list were broken, if the meta-field rendering (modmail_close archive label, role_grant reward-roles pluralization, etc.) regressed, or if the embed/JSON fallback path broke. For a module that is the single source of truth for the moderation audit trail and powers /modstats analytics, this is dangerous false confidence — reviewers will believe the behavior is covered when it is not.
fix: Import the real symbols (import { logActionPretty } from '../../src/logging/pretty.js') and assert on actual behavior: call logActionPretty(mockGuild, params) and verify mockPrepare/mockRun received the expected action_log INSERT with the right bound params; verify getActionMeta is invoked indirectly by checking the embed title/color via the mocked EmbedBuilder; verify the no-channel branch calls the mocked logActionJSON with the correct payload. Delete the literal-only assertions.

title: Linked Roles "security" test suite never imports the module under test — every assertion is tautological
detail: The file's header claims it is "Unit tests for Discord Linked Roles OAuth2 server module" verifying "rate limiting, state validation, and HTML escaping". In reality it never imports src/web/linkedRoles.ts. Every test re-declares the value it then asserts (e.g. lines 26-28 `const RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS = 60*1000; expect(RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS).toBe(60000)`; lines 49-69 reimplement checkRateLimit logic locally; lines 104-138 define a private copy of escapeHtml and test that copy). These assertions pass unconditionally regardless of what the real module does. Concrete impact: this is the only test coverage for an UNAUTHENTICATED, internet-facing HTTP server that performs OAuth2 token exchange, CSRF state validation (validateState), per-IP rate limiting, and HTML escaping of attacker-controlled query params (error/state -> escapeHtml) into HTML responses. A regression in the real escapeHtml (XSS), in validateState (CSRF bypass / replay), in checkRateLimit's `>=` boundary (off-by-one allowing an extra request), or in the redirect_uri/scope construction would be completely invisible to CI because no test exercises the real code. The suite gives false confidence that these security behaviors are pinned when they are not.
fix: Import the real functions from src/web/linkedRoles.ts (export them or extract the pure helpers — escapeHtml, checkRateLimit, generateState, validateState, evictOldestEntries — into a testable module) and assert against those exports. For escapeHtml/validateState/checkRateLimit drive the actual implementation with adversarial inputs (e.g. expired/replayed state tokens, count == maxRequests boundary, `<script>` payloads) instead of local copies.

title: Artist-rotation 'next artist' selection is a check-then-act race (TOCTOU) across /redeemreward issue→confirm and concurrent invocations
detail: getNextArtist(guildId) (redeemreward.ts:192) is a pure SELECT (src/features/artistRotation/queue.ts:264-279) — it does NOT mutate the queue. The selected artistId is baked into the Confirm button customId (redeemreward.ts:283). The queue is only mutated by processAssignment() when Confirm is clicked (src/features/artistRotation/handlers.ts:228). handleConfirm trusts the command-time artistId and never (a) re-checks that this artist is still next, (b) consumes/dedupes confirmId, nor (c) applies any per-button cooldown (the cooldown in src/features/review/handlers/buttonCooldown.ts is review-only). Two realistic triggers: (1) two staff run /redeemreward (no override) before either confirms — getNextArtist returns the SAME artist both times, both confirm, the artist is assigned twice, gets two art jobs (createJob, handlers.ts:258), and processAssignment runs twice; (2) one staff double-clicks the single Confirm button — interactionCreate (src/events/interactionCreate.ts:599-613) dispatches each click as an independent interaction with no in-flight guard, so handleConfirm runs twice, creating two jobs and double-incrementing assignments. processAssignment itself is transactional, but the decision that feeds it is made far earlier, so the transaction does not close the window. Contrast: the byte-token confirm path explicitly added a race mitigation (src/features/byteTokenHandler.ts:353-382) while this path has none.
fix: Make the assignment idempotent and re-validated at confirm time: (a) persist pending redemptions keyed by confirmId and atomically consume the row inside processAssignment's transaction (reject if already consumed); and/or (b) for non-override flows, re-run getNextArtist INSIDE the same db.transaction() as processAssignment and assign whoever is actually next at confirm time rather than trusting the customId; and (c) add a short per-(user,confirmId) cooldown / disable the button immediately on first click (interaction.update removing components) to swallow double-clicks.

title: Byte token double-click TOCTOU: entitlement gated only by eventually-consistent Discord role cache; concurrent confirms re-grant and reset expiry
detail: The sole entitlement check before redeeming is guildMember.roles.cache.has(tokenConfig.tokenRoleId) at line 283. The confirm button is never disabled and the ephemeral message's components are not cleared until the final editReply, so a user can fire two ButtonInteractions on the same button. interactionCreate routes each to a separate concurrent handleUseByteButton invocation (events/interactionCreate.ts:616-629); discord.js does NOT serialize interactions for a user. Both invocations deferUpdate, both fetch the member, both observe the token role still present (it is only removed at line 314, after several awaited REST calls), and both proceed. The CHANGELOG (line 322) and the Step-3.5 cleanup (lines 357-382) only address stacking of DISTINCT multiplier roles — and that cleanup explicitly excludes the role just added (roleId !== tokenConfig.multiplierRoleId at 361), so two same-rarity redemptions both add the same role (idempotent) and both reach upsertActiveMultiplier. The upsert's ON CONFLICT (byteMultiplierStore.ts:66-79) overwrites expires_at with a brand-new full-duration value every time, so the second click silently refreshes/extends the multiplier window for a single token. There is no atomic DB claim of the token. Worse, for the epic/legendary pair that share multiplier role 1405369052829974543 (usebyte.ts:87,96), holding both tokens and redeeming epic then legendary extends the same role's expiry to the longer 72h with the de-stack logic seeing nothing to remove.
fix: Gate redemption on an atomic DB claim, not Discord role state. Before any role mutation, run an INSERT OR IGNORE / UPDATE...WHERE into a per-token redemption ledger keyed by (guild_id, user_id, token_rarity) (or a UNIQUE claim row) and bail if changes===0. Additionally disable the confirm button immediately (interaction.update components disabled) at the very start of handleConfirm before deferring, and key the confirmId so a replayed click is rejected. Make the ON CONFLICT path additive/longest-wins on expires_at rather than blindly overwriting, so a stray second write can't silently shorten or refresh a window.

title: Patreon art entitlements with quantity > 1 are permanently under-granted — the second emoji ticket is lost on first redemption
detail: PATREON_ART_ENTITLEMENTS gives '[Patreon] Legendary Fiona' emoji:2 (line 39 region). handlePatreonArtRewards computes delta = entitlement - alreadyGranted, assigns the ticket ROLE exactly once regardless of delta (comment at 187-188 says 'For delta > 1 ... we assign the role once'), then sets quantity_granted to the full entitlement via the high-water-mark MAX() upsert (lines 96-104). The ticket role is a single binary 'has an emoji ticket' marker. Redemption (src/features/artistRotation/handlers.ts:125-145) removes that role after ONE use and tracks nothing about remaining quantity — there is no redeemed/remaining counter anywhere (confirmed: patreon_art_granted has only quantity_granted, migrations/062, and roles.ts:725-730 only displays it). After the first emoji redemption the role is gone, but getGrantedQuantity returns 2 >= entitlement 2, so the periodic sweep (patreonRoleDedup.ts:149-159 → handlePatreonArtRewards every 10 min) hits 'entitlement <= alreadyGranted' (line 180) and never re-grants. Net result: a Legendary Fiona patron pays for 2 emoji tickets but can only ever redeem 1. The economy under-pays the highest-tier supporter.
fix: Track redemptions, not just grants. Add a redeemed counter (or remaining = quantity_granted - redeemed) to patreon_art_granted; decrement/increment it in the /redeemreward confirm handler. Re-grant the ticket role whenever remaining > 0 and the user lacks it. Alternatively, model quantity>1 entitlements as multiple distinct redeemable units rather than one binary role. Until fixed, no tier should define quantity>1 for a single binary ticket role.

title: replyOrEdit silently drops the ephemeral flag and edits the source message after deferUpdate(), clobbering shared review/confirmation cards
detail: replyOrEdit() decides between editReply/followUp/reply purely on interaction.deferred/replied, but discord.js sets deferred=true for BOTH deferReply() and deferUpdate(). The deferred branch (line 503-506) strips flags (`const { flags, ...editPayload } = withFlags`) and calls editReply(). After a component interaction has called deferUpdate(), editReply() edits the ORIGINAL message the component was attached to — it does NOT create an ephemeral reply. So every caller that does `deferUpdate()` then `replyOrEdit({ content, flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral })` (1) loses ephemerality and (2) overwrites the source message. Concrete, routinely-triggered case: src/features/review/handlers/claimHandlers.ts handleClaimToggle — two mods click Claim at once; the loser hits ClaimError ALREADY_CLAIMED and calls replyOrEdit({content:'This application is already claimed by another moderator.', flags: Ephemeral}) (claimHandlers.ts:62-67). Because handleReviewButton already called deferUpdate() (buttons.ts:177-181), this becomes editReply on the review card: the embed, applicant info, and all action buttons are replaced with the bare public sentence, destroying the shared card for every mod. Same pattern: claimHandlers.ts:74,91,178,190,243 (the 'unclaimed successfully' / 'not owner' / perm-rejected messages all request Ephemeral and all instead wipe the card publicly).
fix: Distinguish deferReply-state from deferUpdate-state. Track how the interaction was acknowledged (e.g., set a flag when deferUpdate is used, or check interaction.isMessageComponent() && deferred) and in that case send feedback via interaction.followUp({ ..., flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }) instead of editReply. Also stop discarding `flags` on the editReply branch when the intent is an ephemeral follow-up. At minimum, callers that did deferUpdate() should use followUp for ephemeral side-messages rather than replyOrEdit.

title: Review modal/button error handlers overwrite the review card with a public plaintext error after deferUpdate()
detail: handleRejectModal (and handleAcceptModal:87-112, handlePermRejectModal:126-151, handleKickModal:165-190, handleVoteOutModal:203-228) all call interaction.deferUpdate() first, then on any thrown error call replyOrEdit(interaction, { content: 'Failed to process ... (trace: X).' }) with no flags. Via the cmdWrap.ts bug above, deferred=true routes this to editReply(), which edits the ORIGINAL review card message — replacing the applicant embed and action buttons with a bare public error string. The same defect exists in handleReviewButton's catch (buttons.ts:200-204) for the already-deferred actions (claim/wrong_password/stale_modmail) and in handleModmailButton's catch (buttons.ts:270-275). Net effect: a transient failure (DB hiccup, Discord 50013, etc.) during a moderation action not only fails the action but visibly destroys the review card for all staff, with the internal trace string leaked publicly into the staff channel.
fix: In these post-deferUpdate catch blocks, send the failure via interaction.followUp({ content, flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }) (the message component interaction still supports followUp after deferUpdate) instead of replyOrEdit/editReply, so the card is preserved and the error stays private to the acting mod.

title: Pulse insights engine runs 18 detectors with ~50 synchronous SQLite queries per request, several non-sargable
detail: getInsights() loops over 18 detector functions sequentially (line 1483). Each detector fires 1-6 synchronous better-sqlite3 queries: e.g. detectMessageAnomaly runs 1 + 4-in-a-loop COUNT(*) over message_activity (lines 827-846), detectCommunicatorRatioDecline runs 2 queries x4 windows = 8 queries (lines 910-926), detectVoiceTrend runs 4, detectAppBacklog/ModWorkloadImbalance/RejectionRateShift each scan review_action via 'app_id IN (SELECT id FROM application WHERE guild_id=?)' semi-joins. Conservatively this is ~40-55 blocking queries on a single SSR request, all on the synchronous DB handle, several aggregating over the million-row message_activity / action_log / review_action tables. Because better-sqlite3 is synchronous (web/src/lib/server/db.ts), the entire Node event loop is blocked for the full duration on every cold cache load, stalling all other concurrent dashboard requests. The page-level cache (CACHE_TTL.medium=60s, pulse/+page.server.ts:37) only masks this between refreshes and per time-window; every distinct window and every 60s expiry pays the full cost.
fix: Collapse the per-window repeated COUNT(*) loops (detectMessageAnomaly, detectCommunicatorRatioDecline, detectVoiceTrend) into single GROUP BY queries that return all buckets at once. Share one pass over message_activity / user_activity / review_action across detectors instead of re-querying per detector (pass a small pre-aggregated context into the detectors). Consider precomputing insights in the existing cron rollup (like observatory does) and reading a rollup table at request time.

title: Migration runner reports success when the child is killed by a signal (result.status null)
detail: spawnSync returns { status, signal }. When the child tsx process is terminated by a signal (e.g. OOM-killer during a large migration, or SIGTERM from pm2/kill_timeout), `result.status` is null and `result.signal` is set. `process.exit(result.status || 0)` then exits 0, reporting success for a migration that never completed. Even when status is a real non-zero, the upstream caller in deploy.sh:435 throws the code away via `|| echo`, but this line independently masks signal kills for ANY caller (deploy-no-tests.sh:25, docs/development-guide.md:175 step 7, manual runs). Combined with the swallowed-exit bug it means a killed migration looks fully successful end to end.
fix: Propagate failure faithfully: `if (result.error) { console.error(result.error); process.exit(1); } process.exit(result.signal ? 1 : (result.status ?? 1));`. Use `?? 1` (not `|| 0`) so a null status fails closed.

title: Wrong/missing DB_PATH silently creates an empty DB, 'backs it up', and migrates the empty file
detail: The DB is opened with `new Database(dbPath, { fileMustExist: false })` (line 50) — the in-file comment at 48-49 even warns 'we'll happily create a fresh DB if the path is wrong. You'll only notice when all your data is mysteriously gone.' createBackup() (line 142) then does `copyFileSync(dbPath, backupPath)` AFTER the connection already created the file, so the backup is of the freshly-created empty DB, not the real data. All pending migrations then 'succeed' against the empty DB and get stamped into schema_migrations. On the server this is reachable: if DB_PATH in the remote .env is wrong, or the deploy extracts into a path where ./data/data.db doesn't yet exist (relative cwd mismatch), the bot boots against an empty database with a clean migration log and no recoverable pre-state. There is no assertion that the DB existed and was non-empty before migrating.
fix: Open with `fileMustExist: true` for the migrate path (or stat the file before opening and abort if it is missing/zero-bytes when not explicitly bootstrapping). Take the backup via the filesystem BEFORE opening the connection, and skip/abort backup if the source does not exist instead of copying a just-created empty file. Gate fresh-DB creation behind an explicit `--init`/`--bootstrap` flag.

title: Parallel '--no-tests' deploy path lacks lock/backup/health-check and duplicates the swallowed-migration bug
detail: deploy-no-tests.sh is a second, fully independent deploy script targeting the same prod host/path/PM2 process as deploy.sh. It (a) repeats the exact swallowed-migration defect at line 25 (`node scripts/migrate-remote.js || echo "Migration step completed (may have warnings)"`), (b) has no deploy lock, so it can race a concurrent deploy.sh run (deploy.sh's mkdir lock at line 83 does not protect against this script, which never acquires it), (c) takes no pre-deploy DB backup, and (d) has only a best-effort `pm2 show | grep` status check with no Discord-ready verification. Two scripts mutating the same server with different safety guarantees is a cross-file hazard: an operator using this 'fast' path silently loses every protection that was added to deploy.sh in the 2026-05-02 hardening pass.
fix: Delete deploy-no-tests.sh and fold its behavior into `deploy.sh --fast` (which already exists, lines 159-162), so there is exactly one hardened deploy path with the lock, backup, and migration-abort logic.

title: redeemreward confirm button has no reentrancy guard: double-click duplicates art jobs and double-rotates the artist queue
detail: handleConfirm() runs the assignment side effects with NO idempotency/lock and only clears the buttons at the very end (interaction.editReply({components:[]}) at lines 282-285). The flow is: deferUpdate -> (await) remove ticket role -> (await) grant artist access / post `$add` -> processAssignment() -> createJob() -> logAssignment() -> editReply(clear buttons). Because the confirmation is a NON-ephemeral reply (src/commands/redeemreward.ts:294-297, no MessageFlags.Ephemeral) and handleConfirm never verifies the clicker is the invoker, the live button can be clicked twice in quick succession (or by two different staff) before the first invocation reaches the final editReply. Each click is a distinct Discord interaction with a distinct interaction.id, so the interactionCreate dedup map (src/events/interactionCreate.ts:69-97, which only de-dupes identical IDs from Discord network re-delivery) does NOT prevent it. The downstream operations are NOT idempotent: processAssignment (src/features/artistRotation/queue.ts:374-427) unconditionally rotates the artist to the end of the queue and increments assignments_count by 1 each call; createJob (src/features/artJobs/store.ts:114-161) always INSERTs a new art_job row with the next sequential job number. The random `confirmId` embedded in the customId is parsed but never recorded or consumed anywhere, so it provides no protection. Result of a double-fire: the artist is rotated twice (losing their fair queue position), assignments_count is over-counted, two art_job rows are created for one commission, two assignment_log rows, and for legacy Ticket Tool channels two `$add` commands are posted. This is a cross-file trust gap: the handler trusts that the queue/job stores enforce single-execution, but they only guarantee per-call atomicity, not idempotency. Note the codebase already solves this exact problem elsewhere (modmail threadOpen.ts uses a 'pending' PRIMARY-KEY lock row; byteTokenHandler.ts has explicit 'Step 3.5 race condition' cleanup and an initiator check), confirming this is an oversight rather than intentional.
fix: Guard the confirmation against re-entry before doing any work. Cheapest robust option: in handleConfirm, immediately after deferUpdate(), do an atomic 'consume' of the confirmation -- e.g. INSERT the confirmId into a small consumed_confirmations table (or art_job/assignment_log keyed by a UNIQUE confirmId) inside a transaction and bail if it already exists (ALREADY_PROCESSED), mirroring the review claimTx pattern. Alternatively, edit the message to remove the buttons (interaction.update / editReply with components:[]) as the FIRST action so a second click can't hit the live component, and add an initiator check like byteTokenHandler (reject if interaction.user.id !== the original invoker). Also make processAssignment + createJob run under a single guard so they cannot both execute twice.

title: Migration 039 never records itself and runs on a different DB connection outside the runner transaction
detail: Of all 70 migrations, 039 is the only one that (a) does NOT call recordMigration(...) and (b) imports the long-lived singleton `db` from ../src/db/db.js (line 12) instead of using the `db` argument the runner passes. The runner (scripts/migrate.ts:209-213) executes `db.transaction(() => migrateFn(db))` and itself NEVER inserts into schema_migrations -- recording is delegated entirely to each migration via recordMigration (see helpers.ts:149). Consequences: (1) Because 039 never writes a schema_migrations row, getAppliedVersions() never sees '039', so scanMigrations keeps it in `pendingMigrations` and it re-runs on EVERY `npm run migrate` / deploy. (2) migrateFn(db) ignores the passed handle; all of 039's writes go through the src/db/db.js singleton connection (a second connection to the same WAL file, opened with different pragmas and a prepare() wrapper). So 039's work happens OUTSIDE the runner's transaction -- if a later statement in that wrapped transaction threw, 039's index/renumber changes would NOT roll back, breaking the atomicity guarantee the runner advertises. The dedup + `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS` + `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` body is itself idempotent so re-running is not catastrophic, but the migration is permanently 'pending', runs un-transactionally, and may touch a different DB path than the one the runner backed up.
fix: Change the signature to `export function migrate039FixArtJobUniqueConstraint(db: Database): void`, drop the `import { db } from "../src/db/db.js"` line so it uses the passed-in handle, and add `recordMigration(db, "039", "fix_art_job_unique_constraint")` at the end (importing it from ./lib/helpers.js), matching every other migration.

title: review_claim.claimed_at is written as an integer into a TEXT column, so normalizeTimestamp always returns null and the dashboard 'claimed at' time is permanently blank
detail: review_claim.claimed_at is declared `TEXT NOT NULL` (src/db/db.ts:129-133 and tests/fixtures/schema.sql:766-770). The production writer reviewActions.ts:110 inserts `nowUtc()` (an integer, e.g. 1748000000) with a comment claiming it is 'matching both table schemas' -- but the column has TEXT affinity, so SQLite coerces the integer to the STRING '1748000000.0' (verified empirically with better-sqlite3). The reader getReviewQueue/getApplicationDetail passes claimed_at through normalizeTimestamp (shared.ts), whose string branch does `value.replace(' ','T') + 'Z'` -> '1748000000.0Z' -> new Date(...) -> NaN -> returns null. Verified: normalizeTimestamp('1748000000.0') === null. Net effect: ReviewQueueItem.claimedAt and ApplicationDetail.claimedAt are ALWAYS null in the dashboard, so reviewers never see when an application was claimed. This is masked by the test suite because the test fixture (tests/utils/dbFixtures.ts:334) inserts claimed_at as `new Date().toISOString()` (a real ISO string that normalizeTimestamp parses fine) -- the fixture does not match how production writes the column, so tests pass while production is broken.
fix: Make normalizeTimestamp recognize numeric strings (e.g. if `/^\d+(\.\d+)?$/.test(value)` treat it as a unix-seconds/ms number and reuse the numeric branch), OR change the writer to store ISO text via tsToIso(nowUtc()) into the TEXT column, OR migrate review_claim.claimed_at to INTEGER and store seconds. The numeric-string guard in normalizeTimestamp is the lowest-risk fix and also hardens every other TEXT-affinity timestamp reader.

title: Byte token confirm is a check-then-act race: entitlement is gated only on the eventually-consistent Discord role cache, with no DB guard, so concurrent confirms can re-grant and reset expiry from a single token
detail: The only guard preventing double-redemption is guildMember.roles.cache.has(tokenConfig.tokenRoleId) at line 283, read from a member fetched per-interaction. The interaction-dedup in interactionCreate.ts (line 69-97, keyed on interaction.id) does NOT help here because two distinct clicks - or two confirmation messages produced by running /usebyte twice - carry distinct interaction IDs. There is no DB-level idempotency: upsertActiveMultiplier (byteMultiplierStore.ts line 66-79) uses ON CONFLICT(guild_id,user_id) DO UPDATE, which unconditionally rewrites expires_at to now+duration on every call. So a user who double-clicks Confirm can have both handlers pass the role.has() check before either removal propagates, and both call upsert; the second call resets the boost expiry to a fresh full duration off a single consumed token. The post-add race cleanup at line 353-382 only removes OTHER multiplier roles, not the duplicate grant of the same role, and does nothing about the duplicated expiry reset. There is no per-user lock around handleConfirm.
fix: Make consumption atomic in SQLite: gate redemption on a conditional write (e.g., an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING into a redemption-claim table keyed by a single-use token instance, or a transaction that both records the spend and refuses if already spent) BEFORE removing the Discord role, and only proceed if changes===1. Add a short per-(guild,user) in-process mutex as defense in depth.

title: Level-reward dedup marker is written before checking whether any reward exists, permanently blocking rewards added to that level later (silent under-grant)
detail: handleLevelRoleAdded writes the permanent dedup row INSERT OR IGNORE INTO level_reward_granted (guild_id,user_id,level) at line 130-133, and only AFTERWARD calls getLevelRewards(guild.id, level) at line 146. When a user reaches a level that currently has zero configured rewards, the function still commits the dedup marker, then returns at line 147-154 because rewards.length===0. The dedup table has UNIQUE(guild_id,user_id,level) and is never cleared (migration 057; only roles.ts:538 deletes from level_rewards config, not from level_reward_granted). Consequently, if staff later add a token/ticket reward for that level (a normal economy operation), every user who already passed that level can NEVER receive it: the dedup INSERT OR IGNORE returns changes===0 and the function short-circuits at line 135-143 before getLevelRewards is ever consulted. Cross-file: the reward catalog (level_rewards, edited via roles.ts) and the dedup ledger (level_reward_granted) are decoupled, and the ordering here makes the ledger record a 'granted' fact that never happened.
fix: Check getLevelRewards FIRST and return early when there are no rewards, WITHOUT writing the dedup row. Only insert the dedup marker once you have a non-empty reward set to grant (ideally insert it inside the same transaction that performs/records the grants). This preserves idempotency while letting newly-added level rewards reach users who level past that tier afterward.

title: Art-ticket redemption (/redeemreward) trusts a stale role snapshot captured at command time and the only spend-guard (Discord ticket-role removal) is non-atomic, allowing double-spend of one ticket across two confirmations
detail: redeemreward.ts builds the confirmation when staff invokes the command, encoding recipientId+artType into the button customId (line 283). The actual debit happens later in handlers.ts handleConfirm: after deferUpdate (line 120) it fetches the member and removes the ticket role only if member.roles.cache.has(ticketRoleId) (line 131-134). There is no DB-backed entitlement for art tickets in the redeem path - the Discord ticket role IS the single-use token (see redeemreward.ts comment line 81-83 'we remove the role so they can't double-dip'). Because the has()-check + remove() is a check-then-act on the eventually-consistent cache with no transactional claim, two confirmations for the same recipient+type (e.g., staff double-clicks, or two staff each run /redeemreward for the same person before either confirms) can both observe the role present, both 'succeed', and produce TWO assignments + TWO art_job rows (createJob, line 258) while only one ticket existed. The branch at line 135-137 ('User did not have ticket role') still proceeds to assign an artist and create a job, so even a redemption against a user with NO ticket is logged as a successful assignment with only a soft warning embed. This is the spend half of the same economy whose grant half is patreon_art_granted; neither side reconciles against the other.
fix: Tie the spend to an atomic DB claim instead of (or in addition to) the Discord role: in handleConfirm, perform a conditional decrement/claim against a per-user art-ticket ledger inside a transaction and abort if nothing was claimed. At minimum, hard-fail (do not create a job or rotate the artist) when the recipient does not actually hold the ticket role, and de-duplicate concurrent confirms with a per-(recipient,artType) guard.

title: Patreon art entitlements with quantity>1 collapse onto a single binary ticket role, so a tier promising 2 emoji tickets only ever yields one redeemable ticket
detail: PATREON_ART_ENTITLEMENTS defines quantity>1 for some tiers (Legendary Fiona emoji: 2, line 38). handlePatreonArtRewards computes delta = entitlement - alreadyGranted (line 182) and then assigns the single ticket role exactly once (assignRole, line 189-195) regardless of delta, while upsertGrant sets quantity_granted to the full entitlement via MAX() (store.ts line 96-103). The DB high-water mark therefore records '2 emoji granted' but the user only ever holds ONE binary emoji ticket role. On the spend side (artistRotation/handlers.ts line 131-134) /redeemreward removes that one role, and because patreon_art_granted already reads 2 the periodic sweep (patreonRoleDedup.ts sweepOnce -> handlePatreonArtRewards every 10 min) sees entitlement(2) <= alreadyGranted(2) and never re-grants, so the second emoji ticket is silently lost. The grant ledger (quantity_granted) and the redeem mechanism (binary role presence) are two different representations that disagree whenever quantity>1. Note: a redemption-counter audit already on file (audit/2026-05-31) corroborates this; reported here as an independently-confirmed economy defect.
fix: Track redeemed vs remaining (e.g., remaining = quantity_granted - redeemed) on patreon_art_granted, decrement remaining in the /redeemreward confirm handler, and re-grant the ticket role whenever remaining>0 and the user lacks it. Alternatively model quantity>1 as multiple distinct redeemable units. Until fixed, no tier should declare quantity>1 against a single binary ticket role.

title: ensurePokeConfigColumns() is never called -> poke config columns missing in prod DB -> /config poke crashes
detail: ensurePokeConfigColumns (config.ts:492) is the ONLY code path that adds guild_config.poke_category_ids_json and poke_excluded_channel_ids_json. There is no migration for them (grep 'poke' across migrations/ = zero hits) and they are absent from tests/fixtures/schema.sql. The startup self-heal runner src/startup/schema.ts wires in 7 other config ensure* functions (lines 67-73) but omits ensurePokeConfigColumns, despite its own comment (schema.ts:11-12) saying new ensure* functions must be appended. git log -S 'ensurePokeConfigColumns' confirms the function was never referenced from index.ts/schema.ts. I opened the live production DB (DB_PATH=./data/data.db, 5GB, actively used) and confirmed both columns are ABSENT. Meanwhile /config poke (config/poke.ts) calls upsertConfig({ poke_category_ids_json: ... }); poke_category_ids_json is in the upsertConfig ALLOWLIST (config.ts:659) so it is NOT filtered out, and upsertConfig builds 'UPDATE guild_config SET poke_category_ids_json = ?' (config.ts:682). Against a table lacking the column this throws SqliteError: no such column: poke_category_ids_json. So setting poke target categories / excluded channels is currently a hard runtime failure in production, caused purely by an ensure function that is dead because nobody wired it in.
fix: Add ensurePokeConfigColumns and ensurePulseConfigColumns to the import block and call list in src/startup/schema.ts:runSchemaSelfHeal() (alongside ensureSkullModeColumns etc.). Alternatively delete the dead ensure functions and add a real numbered migration under migrations/ that ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN the poke/pulse columns, then run npm run migrate on prod. Either way the column-add must actually execute before /config poke is used.

title: ensurePulseConfigColumns() never called and migration 059 not applied -> pulse query SELECT crashes on prod DB
detail: pulse_excluded_category_ids_json is created by two redundant mechanisms: migration 059 (manual-only; migrations are NOT run at startup, only via npm run migrate) and ensurePulseConfigColumns (config.ts:534, never called by schema.ts or anything else). On the production DB, schema_migrations shows only 39 rows with the highest applied = 045, so migration 059 was never applied, and PRAGMA table_info(guild_config) confirms pulse_excluded_category_ids_json is ABSENT. Because the ensure function that would self-heal it is unwired, the column simply does not exist. The web dashboard reads it with an UNGUARDED query: web/src/lib/server/queries/pulse.ts:242 does db.prepare('SELECT pulse_excluded_category_ids_json FROM guild_config WHERE guild_id = ?').get(guildId). The subsequent 'if (!row?.pulse_excluded_category_ids_json)' guard only handles a NULL value, not a missing column, so the prepare/get throws 'no such column' before that guard runs. /config pulse writes via upsertConfig hit the same no-such-column failure as the poke case. This is the same root cause as the poke finding: an ensure helper that is dead because it was never added to the startup runner.
fix: Wire ensurePulseConfigColumns into src/startup/schema.ts:runSchemaSelfHeal(), OR run the existing migration 059 on prod (npm run migrate) and keep migrations as the single source of truth (then delete the dead ensure function). Pick one mechanism; having an unrun migration AND an unwired ensure function is what produced the gap.

title: Migration failure is swallowed by `|| echo`, so the bot restarts against an un-migrated schema
detail: The full deploy runs migrations as: `ssh_remote "cd ${REMOTE_PATH} && node scripts/migrate-remote.js" || echo "Migration step completed (may have warnings)"`. The migration runner scripts/migrate.ts is correctly designed to fail hard: on any migration error it logs and calls `process.exit(1)` (migrate.ts:308-311), and scripts/migrate-remote.js propagates that exit code via `process.exit(result.status || 0)` (migrate-remote.js:24). The `|| echo` in deploy.sh defeats that contract: a non-zero exit (e.g. a migration that throws, a SQLITE_BUSY because the old bot still holds data.db, or migrate-remote.js failing to find tsx) is converted to success. The deploy then proceeds to Step 6.6 (command registration) and Step 7 (`pm2 startOrRestart ecosystem.config.cjs`), starting the NEW code against the OLD schema. Because some migrations are destructive/structural (035_drop_unused_tables DROP TABLE, 028 and 067 DROP TABLE under conditions, 047/053 ADD COLUMN), the new bot can crash-loop on missing columns/tables or read a half-migrated DB. The operator only sees a soothing 'may have warnings' line. This is the central cross-file defect: deploy.sh trusts a wrapper whose carefully-propagated failure signal it then throws away.
fix: Do not swallow the migration exit code. Capture it and abort the deploy before restarting PM2, e.g.: `if ! ssh_remote "cd ${REMOTE_PATH} && node scripts/migrate-remote.js"; then echo 'ERROR: migrations failed, aborting before restart' >&2; exit 1; fi`. The acquire_deploy_lock EXIT trap will still release the lock. If a 'warnings are tolerable' mode is genuinely wanted, gate it behind an explicit flag rather than making it the default.

title: Legacy scripts/deploy.sh ships migrations/ but never runs them, restarting new code on an old schema
detail: scripts/deploy.sh builds a tarball that includes `migrations` and `scripts` (line 108) and on the remote runs only: extract -> `npm ci --omit=dev` -> `pm2 restart` (lines 123-133). There is no `node scripts/migrate-remote.js` / `migrate.ts` step anywhere (grep confirms 0 occurrences of 'migrate'). So anyone running this script (or following the older docs that reference `./deploy.sh`) deploys new code that expects new schema, but the schema is never advanced. The new bot then hits missing columns/tables. This is the inverse-yet-equivalent failure of the root deploy.sh issue and is easy to trigger because two same-named scripts exist (root `deploy.sh` with migrations, `scripts/deploy.sh` without). It also has no deploy lock and no pre-deploy DB backup, unlike the hardened root script.
fix: Either delete scripts/deploy.sh entirely (the hardened root deploy.sh supersedes it) or add the migration step before `pm2 restart` and a pre-deploy backup + lock. At minimum, have it `exec` the root deploy.sh so there is a single source of truth and no path that skips migrations.

title: Documented rollback script deploy-no-tests.sh has no deploy lock and no pre-deploy backup, yet runs migrations
detail: docs/operations/DEPLOY-AGENT.md documents the rollback procedure as `git checkout HEAD~1 && ./deploy-no-tests.sh` (DEPLOY-AGENT.md:79,125,131). deploy-no-tests.sh runs the migration step (line 25, with the same `|| echo` swallow as the root script) and `pm2 startOrRestart` but: (1) it never acquires the DEPLOY_LOCK_DIR mkdir lock that root deploy.sh uses, so it can race a concurrent `./deploy.sh` and both will scp/extract/restart simultaneously, corrupting the extract or the live WAL; (2) it takes no pre-deploy DB backup (no maybe_backup_remote_db, no Litestream check). Worse, in the documented rollback flow the code is rolled back to HEAD~1 but migrations are still applied FORWARD (the runner only goes forward and tracks via schema_migrations), so you end up with old code on a newer-or-equal schema with zero fresh backup right when you are already in an incident. A rollback path is exactly when you most need the lock and the backup.
fix: Make deploy-no-tests.sh call `acquire_deploy_lock` and `maybe_backup_remote_db` (or just `BACKUP_BEFORE_DEPLOY=1 ./deploy.sh --fast`). Update DEPLOY-AGENT.md so the rollback recipe uses the hardened script with a forced backup, and note that migrations are not auto-reverted on a code rollback.

title: Cron-scheduled prod script imports undeclared @xenova/transformers and fetches remote model weights
detail: scripts/embed-incremental.mjs (and embed-all.mjs, embed-gold.mjs) do `import { pipeline, env } from '@xenova/transformers'`, but @xenova/transformers is NOT present in either package.json or package-lock.json (grep across both manifests and both lockfiles: 0 occurrences). The cross-file break: deploy.sh:408 ships the entire `scripts/` dir to the prod host, and scripts/quality-cron.txt:14 schedules `node scripts/embed-incremental.mjs` every 30 minutes on EC2 (/home/ubuntu/pawtropolis-tech). But the production install runs `npm ci --omit=dev` (deploy.sh:341/421/428), which can only ever install what is in the lockfile. Since the package is in NO manifest, npm never provisions it. Two possibilities, both bad: (a) the cron job has been failing every 30 min with MODULE_NOT_FOUND, logging silently to /tmp/quality-embed.log which the file itself says nobody rotates/checks; or (b) someone ran an out-of-band `npm install @xenova/transformers` directly on prod, meaning an unpinned, lockfile-untracked package runs every 30 min outside any reproducible/auditable dependency set. A prior in-repo audit (audit/2026-05-19/deps-ops-findings.md, Finding 1) flagged @xenova/transformers as carrying a HIGH-severity vuln via onnxruntime-web and removed it from package.json, but these importing scripts were left behind.
