Worse, embed-incremental.mjs:18 sets `env.allowLocalModels = false` and line 47 calls `pipeline('feature-extraction', 'Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2')`, which downloads model weights from the HuggingFace CDN at runtime with no integrity/version pinning -- a remote executable-artifact fetch in a scheduled prod job.
fix: Decide intent. If the chat-quality pipeline is live: add @xenova/transformers to package.json dependencies pinned to a specific audited version (or isolate it in a dedicated workspace/package with its own lockfile), commit the lockfile so `npm ci` provisions it deterministically, and pin/vendor the model (set allowLocalModels=true with a checked-in model dir, or pin a model revision) so prod does not pull unverified weights every 30 min. If the pipeline is dead, remove embed-*.mjs and the corresponding quality-cron.txt entry. Either way, stop relying on an out-of-band manual install on prod.

title: PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF is a silent no-op inside the migration runner's transaction
detail: The migration runner (scripts/migrate.ts:209-213) wraps every migration in db.transaction(), so migrate010 always executes inside an open transaction. Migration 010 calls db.pragma("foreign_keys = OFF") at line 97 before the DROP/RENAME table rebuild and db.pragma("foreign_keys = ON") at line 119 after. Per SQLite semantics, PRAGMA foreign_keys is a no-op while a transaction is pending — it can only be toggled when no BEGIN/SAVEPOINT is active. Therefore the intended FK disable never happens; foreign-key enforcement stays ON throughout the table rebuild. The migration happens to still succeed because the only FK involved is guild_question -> guild_config (parent), which the copied rows satisfy, and nothing references guild_question as a parent. But the code's stated safety strategy ('disable foreign keys temporarily to rebuild the table') is silently defeated, and the final pragma at line 119 also does nothing, so FK state after the migration is whatever the runner set (ON), not something this code controls. If a future child table is added that references guild_question, the DROP at line 114 would fail unexpectedly because FKs are actually enforced.
fix: Drop the foreign_keys pragma toggling here (it cannot work inside the runner transaction). For SQLite table rebuilds that truly need FKs off, use the documented 12-step procedure: toggle PRAGMA foreign_keys OUTSIDE any transaction (e.g. have the runner expose a non-transactional path) or use PRAGMA legacy_alter_table plus a foreign_key_check after rebuild. At minimum, remove the misleading OFF/ON calls and add a `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` after the rebuild to assert integrity.

title: Multi-batch message fetch produces non-chronological output (batches interleaved/mis-ordered)
detail: fetchMessagesFromChannel (lines 150-183) fetches messages 100 at a time (newest-first), sorts each batch oldest-first, then prepends each message with messages.unshift(...) (line 167), and finally calls messages.reverse() (line 182). Tracing two batches: batch1 IDs [10,9,8] -> sorted [8,9,10] -> after unshifts messages=[10,9,8]; batch2 (older) IDs [7,6,5] -> sorted [5,6,7] -> after unshifts messages=[7,6,5,10,9,8]; final reverse() yields [8,9,10,5,6,7]. Correct chronological order is [5,6,7,8,9,10]. So any channel/thread with more than 100 messages is archived with the message blocks out of order across every 100-message boundary. The header 'Total messages' count is still correct, so the corruption is silent. For channels under 100 messages (single batch) the output happens to be correct, which masks the bug in light testing.
fix: Drop the per-batch sort + unshift + final reverse entirely. Since Discord returns each batch newest-first and you page with `before: lastId` (strictly older each iteration), simply push each batch's IDs and at the very end build the array oldest-first once. Concretely: collect raw messages into one array via `all.push(...fetched.values())` per batch (newest-first overall), then do `all.sort((a,b) => a.createdTimestamp - b.createdTimestamp)` and map to formatMessage. One global sort by createdTimestamp is unambiguous and removes the interleaving.

title: SQLite datetime strings parsed as local time, producing wrong relative timestamps and day counts
detail: art_job.assigned_at / completed_at are stored as SQLite TEXT via `datetime('now')` (confirmed in src/db/db.ts:353-355 and types.ts:36-39), which yields UTC strings of the form 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (space separator, no timezone). art.ts feeds these directly into `new Date(job.assigned_at).getTime()` (and the same for completed_at) at lines 425, 635, 712, 732, 865, 1038. Per ECMAScript, a date-time string with a space separator and no offset is parsed in the host's LOCAL timezone by V8/Node, not UTC. So on any host not in UTC, every `<t:...:R>` 'Assigned X ago' value rendered by /art jobs, /art view, /art all, and /art getstatus is off by the server's UTC offset. Worse, in handleFinish (lines 635-637) `daysToComplete = Math.floor((Date.now() - assignedAt)/86400000)` can be off by a day, and for a job assigned minutes ago on a host with a positive UTC offset, `assignedAt` (parsed as local) can be GREATER than Date.now(), making the difference negative and rendering '... Completed in -1 days'. The repo already has the correct fix applied in src/ui/reviewCard.ts:110 and src/features/review/card.ts:129 (`trimmed.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z'`), so this column format is known to need normalization before `new Date()`.
fix: Normalize the SQLite datetime string to ISO-UTC before constructing a Date, e.g. a helper `const ms = new Date(job.assigned_at.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z').getTime();` reused at every call site (mirroring reviewCard.ts:110). Also clamp daysToComplete with `Math.max(0, ...)` to avoid negative day counts from clock/parse skew.

title: Mutating staff subcommands never defer and await a network audit-log post before first ack, risking 10062
detail: Slash commands are dispatched by interactionCreate.ts:265 via `executor(interaction)` with NO auto-defer (wrapCommand only catches errors and posts an error card). handleAssign, handleCancel, and handleReassign never call deferReply(); they perform the DB write and then `await logActionPretty(...)` BEFORE the first interaction acknowledgement (handleCancel: audit_log at ~1136 precedes reply at ~1151; handleReassign: audit_log at ~1242 precedes reply at ~1259; handleAssign: audit_log at ~959 precedes reply at ~972). logActionPretty (src/logging/pretty.ts:464,517,635) calls getLoggingChannel(guild) and `channel.send({...})` — a network POST to Discord. If that post is slow (rate limit, transient latency), the total time from interaction receipt can exceed Discord's ~3s response window, so the subsequent interaction.reply() fails with 10062 (Unknown interaction). The DB mutation (cancel/reassign/create) has already committed, but the staff member sees 'This interaction failed' and wrapCommand then also tries (and fails) to post an error card. By contrast the read-only subcommands (handleJobs, handleAll, handleLeaderboard, handleGetStatus) all correctly deferReply() first.
fix: Call `await interaction.deferReply()` at the top of handleAssign/handleCancel/handleReassign (before the DB work / audit log), and replace the final `interaction.reply(...)` with `interaction.editReply(...)`. Alternatively, reorder so the user is acked first and the audit-log post is fire-and-forget after replying.

title: Backfill cooldown is consumed before validation and before the (failing) spawn, locking the guild out for 30 minutes
detail: checkCooldown('backfill', guildId, COOLDOWNS.BACKFILL_MS) records the cooldown timestamp as a side effect on the *allowed* path (see rateLimiter.ts:77 — it sets `now` whenever it returns allowed:true, even if the caller never proceeds). It is called before the weeks/date validation and before the child process is spawned. Combined with the broken-script bug above, a single attempt fails instantly yet still burns the full 30-minute BACKFILL_MS cooldown for the entire guild, so staff cannot retry for half an hour after every failed run. Even independent of the missing-script bug, if spawn errors or validation rejects the input, the cooldown has already been consumed.
fix: Move checkCooldown after input validation, and ideally only record the cooldown once the child process has actually been spawned successfully (e.g. inside backfillProcess.on('spawn'), or call clearCooldown('backfill', guildId) in the 'error' handler and on validation failure).

title: Resume path bypasses cooldown with no concurrency guard — concurrent resumes double-flag members and double-count stats
detail: runMembersAudit (and the parallel runNsfwAudit) are launched fire-and-forget from buttonRouter.handleAuditButton, which explicitly skips the per-guild cooldown for action === 'resume' (buttonRouter.ts:128). getActiveSession returns the same in_progress session for every clicker, and nothing marks the session as 'running' or takes a lock. If two staff click Resume on the same prompt (or the same user double-clicks before the message updates), two runners execute against the same sessionId concurrently. markUserScanned uses INSERT OR IGNORE so the scanned-set dedups, but both runners load `alreadyScanned` at start, so members not yet recorded get analyzed by BOTH runners: upsertManualFlag/upsertNsfwFlag fire twice, two flag embeds are sent to the channel, and updateProgress overwrites flagged_count from two racing counters (last-writer-wins, can under- or over-count). For NSFW this also doubles paid Google Vision API calls. Same shape in nsfw.ts:144-243.
fix: Add a lightweight in-process lock keyed by `${guildId}:${auditType}` (or sessionId) that rejects a second concurrent runner, and/or transition the session to a distinct 'running' status when a runner picks it up and refuse to resume a session already being processed. Re-applying the cooldown on resume (with clear-on-complete) would also prevent the double-click case.

title: Permission cache is never invalidated on role change (invalidatePermissionCache is dead-wired)
detail: filterCommandsByPermission caches the visible-command list under key `${guildId}:${userId}` with a 5-minute TTL (PERMISSION_CACHE, line 208). The only invalidation path is invalidatePermissionCache (line 325), but a repo-wide search shows it is never called from any production module (only its own file, tests, and graphify artifacts). Consequence: when a member's roles change (promotion to staff/reviewer, or demotion), their /help output stays stale for up to 5 minutes. This is not merely cosmetic: showCommandDetail (index.ts:220-235) reuses filterCommandsByPermission as an authorization gate and replies "You don't have permission to view /<cmd>" for any command not in the cached list. So a just-promoted staffer is falsely told they cannot view staff command help, and a just-demoted user can still read help for commands they lost — until the TTL expires. The code's own comment (lines 206-207) promises this invalidation happens; it does not.
fix: Call invalidatePermissionCache(guildId, userId) from the role-change paths (e.g., roleAutomation / guildMemberUpdate handlers), or key the cache on a hash of the member's role IDs so role changes naturally miss the cache. At minimum, shorten the TTL or expose a bulk clear hook that role-update events invoke.

title: Transient member-fetch failure poisons the permission cache with a public-only list
detail: All help entry points fetch the member with `members.fetch(userId).catch(() => null)` and tolerate null (autocomplete.ts:53, index.ts:90/319/397/461). When the fetch rejects (Discord API hiccup/rate limit — explicitly anticipated by the code comments), member is null and filterCommandsByPermission is called with member=null. hasPermissionLevel(line 213) then returns true only for `public` (and bot owner), so the result is the public-only command list — and that list is cached under `${guildId}:${userId}` for 5 minutes (line 283). Because autocomplete fires on every keystroke and is usually the first help interaction, a single failed fetch there poisons the shared module-level PERMISSION_CACHE, so the subsequent `/help` execute and the showCommandDetail permission gate (index.ts:220) both serve the stale public-only list, falsely hiding staff/reviewer/admin commands and denying their detail view for the whole TTL. Combined with the fact that invalidatePermissionCache is never wired up, nothing clears it early.
fix: Do not cache results computed from a null member (skip PERMISSION_CACHE.set when member is null), or treat a fetch failure as 'unknown' rather than 'public-only' and bypass the cache. Alternatively key the cache on resolved role IDs so a null-member computation can't masquerade as a real permission set.

title: INSERT catch block treats ALL errors as 'duplicate verification' and silently aborts
detail: The try/catch around the INSERT (lines 195-203) assumes any thrown error means a UNIQUE-constraint duplicate and replies 'You're already verified!' then returns. But the same catch fires for unrelated failures: missing verified_users table (migration 064 not run), disk full / SQLITE_BUSY, corruption, etc. In those cases the user is falsely told they are already verified, no role is granted, and no log is written — a silent failure that masks the real DB error from operators (only logger.warn 'duplicate verification attempt' is emitted, with the actual err object buried). Genuine duplicates are also already prevented earlier by the existence check at line 61, so reaching this catch via a true duplicate requires the rare double-run race, making the misclassification of other errors the more likely real-world trigger.
fix: Inspect the error: only treat it as a duplicate when err.code === 'SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE' (or the message contains 'UNIQUE constraint failed'); otherwise log at error level and tell the user verification failed and to try again later. Re-throw or surface unexpected errors instead of swallowing them as 'already verified'.

title: Finalize button interaction is awaited but never acknowledged → user sees 'This interaction failed'
detail: The Finalize button press is captured via `await uploadMessage.awaitMessageComponent(...)` (line 179) but the resolved component interaction is discarded — it is never acknowledged with update()/deferUpdate()/reply(). Discord requires every component interaction to be acknowledged within 3 seconds; otherwise the client shows a red 'This interaction failed' on the button. The verification still completes server-side (the message is edited at line 191 and the record is inserted), but the user who clicked Finalize is shown a failure state, which is confusing for an honor-system verification flow and will generate support noise. Contrast with line 154 where the select-menu interaction IS correctly acknowledged via categoryInteraction.update().
fix: Capture the interaction and acknowledge it, e.g. `const finalizeInteraction = await uploadMessage.awaitMessageComponent({...}); await finalizeInteraction.deferUpdate();` (or .update({components: []})) before continuing.

title: Env SILENT_FIRST_MSG_DAYS silently overrides an explicit per-guild DB value of exactly 7
detail: getFlaggerConfig uses silentDays === 7 as the sentinel for 'DB had no value' (lines 166-169). But 7 is also a valid, explicitly-settable per-guild value: setSilentFirstMsgDays accepts the range 7..365 (line 236) and 7 is the minimum allowed. If a guild deliberately sets silent_first_msg_days = 7 in guild_config and the SILENT_FIRST_MSG_DAYS env var is set to a different number (e.g. 30), the DB read sets silentDays = 7 (line 140-142), then line 166 sees silentDays === 7 and overwrites it with the env value (30). The guild's explicit choice is silently discarded, changing flagging behavior. The code comment itself flags this fragility ('this logic assumes 7 is the default').
fix: Track whether the DB actually supplied a value using a real sentinel instead of the magic number. e.g. let dbDays: number | null = null; set it from row.silent_first_msg_days when non-null; apply the env fallback only when dbDays === null; finally silentDays = dbDays ?? envDays ?? 7.

title: /stats history export produces a download link to a non-existent /exports/ route (always 404)
detail: When export:true is passed, the handler writes the CSV to data/exports/<file>.csv and then surfaces a link `${process.env.PUBLIC_URL || "https://pawtropolis.tech"}/exports/<filename>` to the moderator, labeled "Download CSV ... Link expires in 24 hours". I grepped the bot's web bootstrap (src/startup/web.ts, src/web/dashboardApi.ts) and the entire SvelteKit route tree (web/src/routes). There is no route, static handler, or @fastify/static mount that serves `/exports/...`. The only export endpoint is web/src/routes/api/export/+server.ts, which generates its CSV inline from action_log and never reads data/exports. So every link rendered by this feature resolves to a 404 — the export is effectively unusable; the file is written to disk but can never be downloaded.
fix: Either (a) attach the generated CSV directly to the editReply via AttachmentBuilder (as /stats export in export.ts already does) instead of writing to disk and linking, or (b) add a real authenticated `/exports/:filename` route that serves files from data/exports with path-traversal protection. Option (a) is simpler and removes the disk dependency entirely.

title: Exported CSVs accumulate forever in data/exports despite "expires in 24 hours" claim
detail: Each export writes a uniquely-named file (stats-history-<modId>-<ts>-<rand>.csv, up to MAX_EXPORT_ROWS=50000 rows) into data/exports via writeFileSync, but nothing ever deletes them. I searched the whole repo (schedulers, startup tasks, scripts) for any cleanup of data/exports or any honoring of the advertised 24h expiry — there is none. The embed text "Link expires in 24 hours" is therefore false, and the directory grows unboundedly on every invocation. On the 2GB-RAM / constrained-disk host described in src/db/db.ts, repeated large exports can fill the volume. Combined with finding above, these files are also never even served, so they are pure dead weight.
fix: Stop persisting to disk and attach the buffer to the reply (preferred). If on-disk staging is required, add a scheduler that prunes data/exports files older than 24h (matching the promise), or write to an OS temp dir and unlink after streaming.

title: SILENT_FIRST_MSG_DAYS env var silently overrides a guild's explicit DB value of 7
detail: getFlaggerConfig initializes silentDays=7, then reads the DB row. If the DB has a non-null silent_first_msg_days it is assigned to silentDays (lines 140-142). The env fallback at line 166 only fires when `silentDays === 7`. The problem: 7 is a VALID, user-settable value (setSilentFirstMsgDays accepts days>=7, line 236). So a guild that deliberately ran `/config set flags.silent_days 7` stores 7 in the DB, but on read the code cannot distinguish "DB said 7" from "DB had no row / null", and therefore overwrites the guild's explicit 7 with the env default (e.g. SILENT_FIRST_MSG_DAYS=60). This violates the documented resolution priority (DB > ENV, lines 102-106) for exactly the value 7. Impact: a guild that intentionally set the most-aggressive 7-day threshold gets a different (env) threshold applied to first-message flagging, changing who gets flagged. The in-code comment even acknowledges the brittleness ('GOTCHA: This logic assumes 7 is the default').
fix: Track whether the DB actually supplied a value instead of overloading the sentinel 7. e.g. `let dbProvidedDays = false;` set true inside the `row.silent_first_msg_days !== null` branch, then gate the env fallback on `!dbProvidedDays` instead of `silentDays === 7`.

title: DB row inserted before role grant; if role grant fails the user is permanently locked out and falsely told they have the role
detail: The INSERT into verified_users (line 196-198) commits BEFORE the role is added (lines 206-217). If `member.roles.add(VERIFIED_ROLE_ID)` throws (missing Manage Roles perm, role above bot in hierarchy, transient API error), the error is caught and only logged (line 215-216); roleGranted stays false but the DB row already exists. On any subsequent `/verify`, the existing-row check (line 69) short-circuits and tells the user 'You have the Thin Line role' (line 78) — which is false — and never retries the role grant. Result: a user whose role-add failed can never obtain the Thin Line role through this command. The log embed even records 'Role Granted: Failed' (line 233), confirming the path is expected to occur.
fix: Either (a) grant the role first and only INSERT after a confirmed grant, or (b) in the existing-row branch, re-check member.roles.cache.has(VERIFIED_ROLE_ID) and re-attempt the grant if the role is missing rather than asserting the user already has it.

title: Finalize button interaction is never acknowledged → user sees "This interaction failed"
detail: The select-menu step correctly acknowledges its component interaction via categoryInteraction.update(...) (line 154). The Finalize step, however, only awaits the button via uploadMessage.awaitMessageComponent({...}) (lines 179-183) and discards the resulting ButtonInteraction without ever calling .update(), .reply(), or .deferUpdate(). discord.js collectors/awaitMessageComponent do NOT auto-acknowledge. Discord requires a component interaction to be acknowledged within 3 seconds; otherwise the clicking user is shown "This interaction failed". So every successful verification finalization shows the user an error toast even though the backend proceeds to insert the record, grant the role, and DM them. This is confusing and looks broken to end users in the exact honor-system flow the feature is built around.
fix: Capture the interaction and acknowledge it, e.g. `const finalizeInteraction = await uploadMessage.awaitMessageComponent({...}); await finalizeInteraction.deferUpdate();` (or .update({ components: [] })), then proceed. Mirror the pattern already used for categoryInteraction.update() on line 154.

title: User-uploaded identity documents (badges/IDs) are posted to a hardcoded channel and retained indefinitely
detail: The flow invites users to upload verification documents such as badges and IDs (lines 141-145). Every uploaded image URL is then re-posted into a channel identified by a hardcoded snowflake LOG_CHANNEL_ID = "1430015254053654599" (line 26) as embed images (lines 240-253). Although the prompt asks users to redact PII, this is an honor-system flow and many users will upload un-redacted government-issued IDs / first-responder credentials. The consequences: (1) sensitive PII is durably stored in a Discord channel with whatever broad staff access that channel has, beyond the stated "internal records" need and with no retention/deletion; (2) the channel ID is hardcoded rather than configurable, so if the channel is deleted/changed the documents silently fail to log (caught only by a warn) or, worse, a reused ID could route PII to the wrong channel. The attachment.url values are also CDN links that remain accessible.
fix: Make the log channel configurable per-guild (e.g. via guild_config) instead of a hardcoded ID, restrict it to a least-privilege staff channel, and avoid persisting raw ID images — store only a boolean "documents provided" or a short-lived reference, and document a deletion policy. At minimum, do not echo the uploaded image URLs into a long-lived channel.

title: 7-day reopen window mis-computed due to local-time parsing of UTC SQLite timestamp
detail: `ticket.closed_at` is stored by closeTicket() (src/features/modmail/tickets.ts:165) as SQLite `datetime('now')`, i.e. a UTC string of the form "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" with no timezone marker (confirmed by schema src/db/db.ts:186-187: `closed_at TEXT`). Line 73 does `new Date(ticket.closed_at).getTime()`. V8 parses the space-separated, marker-less format as LOCAL time, not UTC. Verified empirically: on a UTC-5 host, `new Date('2026-05-31 12:00:00').toISOString()` === '2026-05-31T17:00:00Z' — a 5-hour error equal to the host's UTC offset. Effect: `now - closedAt` is off by the host offset, so the `> sevenDays` boundary at line 77 is wrong by that offset. On a host behind UTC the reopen window is effectively lengthened; on a host ahead of UTC it is shortened, so a ticket closed ~6d 16h ago (with a +9h offset) can be wrongly treated as >7 days and routed to create a brand-new thread (line 79) instead of reopening. The bot is not guaranteed to run in UTC, so this changes user-visible behavior at the boundary.
fix: Parse as UTC. Either append 'Z'/replace space with 'T'+'Z' (`new Date(ticket.closed_at.replace(' ','T')+'Z')`), or better, store/compare epoch seconds consistently (e.g. compare via SQLite `strftime('%s',closed_at)` or use the project's nowUtc/time helpers). Apply the same parsing fix anywhere closed_at/created_at TEXT columns are turned into Date().

title: ensureGateEntryStartup iterates pinned MessagePin objects as if they were Message objects, so pinned gate panels are never detected
detail: fetchPins().items is `readonly MessagePin[]` where MessagePin = { message, pinnedAt, pinnedTimestamp } (typings 6586-6590). The startup code does `const pinnedCollection = (pinned as { items?: { values: () => Iterable<Message> } }).items;` then `for (const m of pinnedCollection.values()) candidates.set(m.id, m);`. Array.prototype.values() yields the elements, which are MessagePin objects, NOT Message objects. So `m.id` is undefined (every pinned entry is keyed under the same `undefined` slot in the candidates Map) and `m` has no `.components`/`.embeds`. The later guard `if (!Array.isArray(m.components) || !Array.isArray(m.embeds)) continue;` (line 263) is therefore always true for these entries, so the pinned branch contributes nothing. Impact: the startup foreign-bot-panel cleanup and current-bot pinned-panel reuse never see pinned messages; after a bot-identity swap an old foreign pinned panel can be missed, and a current pinned panel may be re-posted instead of edited. The recent-50 fetch at line 256 partially masks this (the panel is usually also in recent history), so it limps along rather than fully failing.
fix: Iterate items as a plain array of MessagePin and use the inner message: `const items = (pinned as { items?: ReadonlyArray<{ message?: Message }> }).items; if (Array.isArray(items)) { for (const it of items) { const m = it?.message; if (m) candidates.set(m.id, m); } }` — matching findExistingGateEntry in the same file.

title: DM verification sessions are looked up by userId only, ignoring guildId, so a user in two bot guilds gets cross-guild misrouting
detail: Sessions are stored keyed by `${guildId}:${userId}` (sessionKey, line 83-85; activeSessions.set at 326) but hasActiveSession(userId) (87-92) and getSessionForUser(userId) (94-99) scan only by session.userId and return the FIRST match. messageCreate.ts:154-156 and interactionCreate.ts routing call these with only the author/user id. The bot is explicitly multi-guild (startup/ready.ts and several schedulers loop over client.guilds.cache). Consequences for a user who is in two guilds where the bot lives: (a) startDmVerification's duplicate guard at line 191 keys by guild+user, so it WILL create a second session for guild B while guild A's session exists, but getSessionForUser then returns whichever was inserted first — a DM answer intended for guild B can be persisted against guild A's appId via upsertAnswer (handleDmAnswer line 380), and the Submit button resolves to the wrong guild's application; (b) only one of the two verifications is reachable via DM at a time. This is data-integrity-relevant (answers written to the wrong application) though it requires the dual-guild precondition.
fix: Key all session operations by guild+user. Either thread guildId through the message/button routing (parse it from the active session's stored thread/guild, or include it in the button customId which already carries a nonce) and look up via activeSessions.get(sessionKey(guildId,userId)), or at minimum disallow more than one active session per user globally and tie the DM answer to the single session deterministically. The nonce on the buttons already scopes button actions, but text-answer routing (handleDmAnswer) has no guild scoping at all.

title: closeModmailThread / closeModmailForApplication are check-then-act with no atomic guard: concurrent close (double-click, or manual close racing auto-close-on-decision) double-flushes transcripts and double-DMs the user
detail: closeModmailThread guards only with a plain read: getTicketById then `if (ticket.status === 'closed') return` (lines 211-228). Two near-simultaneous invocations (e.g. a fast double-click of the Close button — handleModmailCloseButton at handlers.ts:144-159 calls deferUpdate then closeModmailThread, and Discord delivers two distinct interactions; OR a moderator clicking Close while an approve/reject decision concurrently runs closeModmailForApplication, which is fired unawaited via .catch() from web/routes/review.ts:223-608 and review/handlers/actionRunners.ts) both read status='open', both pass the guard, and both proceed. flushTranscript is NOT idempotent: the first call posts the transcript and deletes the in-memory buffer (transcript.ts:262); the second call finds an empty buffer, reconstructs the same conversation from modmail_message in the DB (transcript.ts:129-160), and posts a SECOND transcript message to the log channel. The user also receives two 'Modmail Closed' DMs, the dashboard gets two thread_closed notifications, and two modmail_close action-log rows are written. closeModmailForApplication has the same plain-read guard (getOpenTicketByUser at lines 456-460) and shares no lock with closeModmailThread, so the two functions can race each other as well.
fix: Make the status flip the atomic gate. Perform the close inside a transaction that conditionally updates only when still open and checks the affected row count, e.g. `UPDATE modmail_ticket SET status='closed', closed_at=datetime('now') WHERE id=? AND status='open'`; if changes()===0, another path already closed it — return early and skip transcript flush, DM, archive, logging, and dashboard notify. Apply the same guarded UPDATE in both closeModmailThread and closeModmailForApplication so they mutually exclude.

title: reopenModmailThread can throw on partial unique index when user already has a newer open ticket
detail: reopenModmailThread (userId path) selects the most recent ticket WHERE status='closed' (lines 46-56), then reopenTicket(ticket.id) runs `UPDATE modmail_ticket SET status='open' ...` (tickets.ts:174-179) with no guard against an existing open ticket for the same (guild_id, user_id). The runtime schema defines a partial unique index `idx_modmail_open_unique ON modmail_ticket(guild_id, user_id, status) WHERE status='open'` (src/db/db.ts:193-199). If the user already has an open ticket (e.g. a fresh thread was created after the prior one closed, or via the >7-day branch at threadReopen.ts:77-85 which opens a new ticket), flipping the old closed ticket back to 'open' violates the index and throws SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE inside the transaction (lines 89-109). The catch returns a generic 'Failed to reopen modmail thread' with no explanation. Integrity is preserved by the constraint, but the operation fails confusingly and the DM/unarchive side effects never run.
fix: Before reopening, check for an existing open ticket for (guildId, userId) and either refuse with a clear message ('User already has an open modmail thread: <#...>') or close/merge it first. Alternatively wrap reopenTicket in a guard that detects the constraint and surfaces a specific message.

title: Already-resolved/terminal/invalid guard replies overwrite the review card embed after deferUpdate
detail: All of the run*Action functions are reached after the interaction has already been acknowledged with interaction.deferUpdate() (every modal handler in modals.ts calls deferUpdate before invoking the runner, and the wrong_password/stale_modmail button paths in buttons.ts:96-141 also deferUpdate before calling runRejectAction). After deferUpdate, discord.js sets interaction.deferred = true (verified in node_modules/discord.js InteractionResponses.deferUpdate, and the deferUpdate doc explicitly says it defers an update to 'the message to which the component was attached'). lib/cmdWrap.replyOrEdit then takes the `interaction.deferred` branch and calls interaction.editReply(), which edits the SOURCE review-card message. So when two moderators race (e.g. one approves, the other clicks reject/kick/approve a moment later), the loser's guard branch (`replyOrEdit(interaction, { content: 'Already approved.' })` / 'This application is already resolved.' / 'Already resolved (...)' / 'Application not ready' etc.) replaces the entire review card's embed + buttons with a bare plain-text line. The card is only repaired later if some other path happens to call ensureReviewMessage; on these early-return guard branches it is not refreshed, so the card stays clobbered. Note the modal-opener guards in helpers.ts correctly pass flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral and run before showModal (interaction not yet acked) so they reply ephemerally and are fine — the defect is specifically the post-deferUpdate runners which omit the ephemeral flag.
fix: On the early guard branches inside the run*Action functions (and the duplicate-resolution checks in runVoteOutAction), do not use editReply on a component-deferred interaction. Either pass flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral and use interaction.followUp(...) for the notice (followUp is valid after deferUpdate and posts an ephemeral message instead of editing the card), or refresh the card via ensureReviewMessage and send the notice as an ephemeral followUp. Concretely, replace replyOrEdit(interaction, { content: ... }) with interaction.followUp({ content: ..., flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }).catch(...) in these guard paths.

title: permanent=false reject UPDATE unconditionally clears a prior permanent rejection flag/timestamp is avoided, but permanently_rejected is overwritten to 0 on every non-permanent reject
detail: rejectTx always runs `permanently_rejected = ?` with `permanent ? 1 : 0`. The terminal-state guards above only short-circuit when the current status is exactly 'rejected'/'approved'/'kicked'. A row can legitimately be permanently_rejected=1 while its status is, e.g., 'needs_info' or 'submitted' if a new application/flag path set the permanent flag without flipping status to 'rejected' (the permanent flag is a per-(guild,user) blocklist concept queried in claimHandlers.ts:84-88 across ANY of the user's rows). When a moderator then performs a normal (non-permanent) reject on such a row, this UPDATE forces permanently_rejected back to 0, silently un-banning a user who was previously permanently rejected. Even within a single row, doing a normal reject after the flag was set elsewhere downgrades it. The permanent_reject_at CASE correctly preserves the timestamp, but permanently_rejected itself is clobbered to 0.
fix: Do not lower the flag on a non-permanent reject. Use `permanently_rejected = CASE WHEN ? = 1 THEN 1 ELSE permanently_rejected END` (mirroring the permanent_reject_at CASE), so a normal reject never clears an existing permanent ban; only an explicit perm-reject sets it to 1.

title: Permanently-rejected check runs AFTER claimTx, leaving an orphaned claim on early return
detail: In handleClaimToggle, claimTx(app.id, ...) (line 43) atomically creates the review_claim row + audit row and commits. Only AFTER that does the code run the permRejectCheck query (lines 84-88: SELECT permanently_rejected ... WHERE guild_id=? AND user_id=? AND permanently_rejected=1). If that matches, the function replies 'permanently rejected ... cannot reapply' and returns at line 101 WITHOUT releasing the claim it just acquired (no unclaimTx/clearClaim). Result: the application is now claimed by a moderator who was told the action failed, blocking other Gatekeepers from claiming/acting until an admin force-clears it. Note the dashboard equivalent (src/web/routes/review.ts:49-50) performs the SAME perm-reject check and is documented as intended behavior (docs/reference/dashboard-api-security.md:42), so this is real defense-in-depth code, not dead code. Trigger requires app.user_id to have BOTH a non-terminal app row (so claimTx succeeds) and a separate row with permanently_rejected=1; getOrCreateDraft (src/features/gate/drafts.ts:155-162) normally blocks perm-rejected users from new drafts, which lowers (but does not eliminate) the probability — admin/unblock paths or direct flag-setting can produce the coexisting rows. The failure mode is fail-unsafe: state is corrupted instead of the action being rejected cleanly.
fix: Move the permanently_rejected check BEFORE claimTx so a perm-rejected applicant never gets claimed. Alternatively, if the check must stay post-claim, call clearClaim(app.id) (or unclaimTx) before returning at line 101 so the orphaned claim is released.

title: ManageRoles Scope Warning reports role.position as the count of manageable roles
detail: The issue text reads `Role can assign/remove ${role.position} roles below it.` but role.position is the hierarchy position index, not the number of roles beneath this one. The code computes `rolesAbove` (line 369) but never computes a roles-below count, then substitutes the position integer as if it were that count. Example: a staff role at position 50 with only 3 roles beneath it will tell moderators it can assign/remove 50 roles. This is misinformation inside a security advisory generated by `/audit security` (CONFLICTS.md) and shown to leadership, undermining trust in the audit and potentially causing wrong remediation decisions. Detection of the issue itself is fine; only the reported number is wrong.
fix: Compute the actual count, e.g. `const rolesBelow = roles.filter((r) => r.position < role.position && r.name !== '@everyone').length;` and interpolate `${rolesBelow}` instead of `${role.position}` in the issue string.

title: 7-day reopen window parses UTC SQLite timestamp as local time
detail: `const closedAt = ticket.closed_at ? new Date(ticket.closed_at).getTime() : 0;` then `if (now - closedAt > sevenDays)`. `closed_at` is written by `closeTicket` as `datetime('now')` (src/features/modmail/tickets.ts:165) and the column is TEXT (src/db/db.ts:187), producing a UTC string like `"2025-05-31 14:00:00"` with no timezone marker. Per V8/Node semantics, `new Date("YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS")` (space-separated, no 'Z') is interpreted in the host's LOCAL timezone, not UTC. Comparing that against `Date.now()` (true UTC epoch) shifts `closedAt` by the host's UTC offset (up to ±14h), so the 7-day boundary is wrong by that offset whenever the bot host is not on UTC — a ticket can be treated as 'too old' (forcing a brand-new thread) or 'still reopenable' incorrectly near the boundary. The codebase already knows the correct fix: src/ui/reviewCard.ts:108-111 and src/features/review/card.ts:129 normalize with `trimmed.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z'` before parsing; this call site omits it. (Same defect exists in the sibling src/features/modmail/dashboardBridge.ts:304.)
fix: Normalize before parsing, mirroring reviewCard.ts: `const raw = ticket.closed_at; const iso = raw && raw.includes(' ') && !raw.includes('T') ? raw.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z' : raw; const closedAt = raw ? Date.parse(iso) : 0;` Or store closed_at as a Unix epoch integer (strftime('%s','now')) consistently and compare numerically.

title: INSERT OR IGNORE keyed on whole-second joined_at_s silently drops a session on rapid same-second rejoin
detail: insertVoiceJoin inserts (guild_id, user_id, channel_id, joined_at_s) with INSERT OR IGNORE, and joined_at_s = floor(Date.now()/1000) (1-second resolution). The table's UNIQUE constraint is exactly (guild_id, user_id, channel_id, joined_at_s) (migrations/052_voice_session.ts:27). Scenario: a user with an open row for channel A at second T leaves (Case 2 closes that row, setting left_at_s=T) and rejoins channel A within the same second (Case 1). The new INSERT collides with the just-closed row's identical 4-tuple and is silently IGNORED, so no open session exists. The user's voice time in A is then untracked until a later second boundary. The same collision can happen on a quick A→B→A move sequence within one second. Voice minutes feed newsletter/pulse stats (web/src/lib/server/queries/pulse.ts:334-344), so this under-counts voice activity. Low frequency but real and silent.
fix: Drop INSERT OR IGNORE in favor of a plain INSERT (the UNIQUE was meant only to dedupe true duplicates), or add a finer-grained discriminator to the uniqueness (e.g., include a monotonic counter or use millisecond precision for joined_at), or close+insert atomically while ensuring the new row cannot collide with the row just closed.

title: create() creates the Discord channel before the DB insert; an insert failure orphans an untracked channel
detail: The Discord channel is created at line 241 (guild.channels.create), and only after that does getInsertTicketStmt().run(...) insert the tracking row (line 252). create() is not wrapped in any compensating try/catch. If the DB insert throws (e.g., ticket table missing per the lazy-prepare warning at lines 39-44, a constraint violation, or a transient SQLite error), the function rejects but the Discord channel already exists with no corresponding ticket row. It will never be found by findByChannelId, never closed by the lifecycle, and the allocated number is consumed. The handler (handlers.ts:247) just reports the error to the user, leaving a permanent orphan channel under the Tickets category.
fix: Insert the DB row first (using a placeholder channel_id is awkward), or wrap the post-create steps in try/catch and delete the freshly-created channel (channel.delete()) if the DB insert fails, so a failed open leaves no orphan.

title: Reopen 7-day window uses local-time parsing of a UTC SQLite timestamp (timezone-dependent boundary error)
detail: closeTicket() in tickets.ts writes closed_at with SQLite datetime('now'), which produces a UTC wall-clock string WITHOUT a timezone marker, e.g. '2026-05-31 12:00:00' (space-separated, no 'Z'). threadReopen.ts line 73 then does `new Date(ticket.closed_at).getTime()`. V8/Node parses a non-ISO, space-separated date string as LOCAL time, not UTC. So the parsed instant is shifted by the host's UTC offset. The result feeds the 7-day comparison `now - closedAt > sevenDays` (line 77), which decides whether to reopen the existing thread vs. create a brand-new one (line 79). On a host behind UTC the effective window is lengthened; ahead of UTC it is shortened — by up to the full UTC offset (e.g. ~5-8h for US zones). Tickets right at the boundary will take the wrong branch: either spuriously spawning a new thread (and new ticket row) for a ticket that should reopen, or reopening a thread Discord may have already auto-archived. The unit tests mask this because threadReopen.test.ts constructs closed_at via Date.toISOString() (with 'Z', parsed as UTC), which never matches the real datetime('now') format the DB actually stores. dashboardBridge.ts:304 repeats the same `new Date(ticket.closed_at)` pattern on the same column, so the inconsistency is systemic.
fix: Parse closed_at as UTC explicitly. Either store epoch seconds (strftime('%s','now')) like open_modmail.created_at and compare numerically, or normalize on read, e.g. `const closedAt = ticket.closed_at ? Date.parse(ticket.closed_at.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z') : 0;`. Align closeTicket() and the reopen/dashboard readers on one canonical format, and update tests to use the actual DB format.

title: Modal error replies overwrite the public review card content instead of being ephemeral
detail: Each modal handler calls interaction.deferUpdate() (e.g. lines 49-53, 87-91, 126-130, 165-169, 203-207, 242-246) before doing work, so interaction.deferred is true. On the error paths these handlers call replyOrEdit(interaction, { content: 'Failed to process ... (trace: <id>).' }) with no flags, which takes the editReply branch in src/lib/cmdWrap.ts:503-506 and PATCHes the card's '@original' message -- replacing the review card's content line with the failure/trace text visible to the whole channel. The unclaim-cancelled branch (modals.ts:258-265) additionally passes flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral, which is then stripped by replyOrEdit, so 'Unclaim cancelled. You must type UNCLAIM...' is shown publicly on the card too. Result: a transient handler error visibly corrupts the shared card content for all moderators.
fix: On these post-deferUpdate error paths, use interaction.followUp({ content, flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }) so the failure notice is a separate ephemeral message and the card content is left intact.

title: Garbled claim error during panic mode (fragile message string parsing)
detail: On a failed claim, INVALID_STATUS is rendered as `Cannot claim: application is already **${err.message.split(" ")[2]}**.` This assumes the ClaimError message is always the terminal-state form "Application already <status>" (split()[2] == status). But claimTx() throws the SAME INVALID_STATUS code for panic mode with message "Panic mode is active. All review operations are suspended." (reviewActions.ts:62). split(" ")[2] of that string is "is", so during panic mode a moderator clicking Claim sees the nonsensical message "Cannot claim: application is already **is**." It also needlessly calls ensureReviewMessage() to "refresh card after blocked claim" even though nothing changed. The claim is still correctly blocked, so this is cosmetic/diagnostic, but it actively misleads the operator during an emergency (panic) when clear messaging matters most.
fix: Do not parse the human message. Either (a) carry the status as a structured field on ClaimError (e.g. add a `status?` property set when throwing terminal-state errors) and render that, or (b) add a distinct error code for panic (e.g. "PANIC_MODE") and branch on it explicitly so panic shows "Review operations are suspended (panic mode)."

title: claimTx writes integer Unix seconds into ISO/TEXT claimed_at, breaking the review-card claim timestamp parser
detail: claimTx inserts claimed_at = nowUtc() (an INTEGER, Unix seconds — see src/lib/time.ts:34). The review_claim.claimed_at column is TEXT (src/db/db.ts:132) and the shared type declares it `string // ISO timestamp string` (src/features/review/types.ts:66). SQLite TEXT affinity coerces the integer to the string "1735689600". The review card's embed builder parses it with a naive branch: `typeof claim.claimed_at === "number" ? claim.claimed_at : Math.floor(new Date(claim.claimed_at).getTime()/1000)` (src/features/review/card.ts:339-342). Because the stored value is a numeric STRING, the else branch runs `new Date("1735689600")` which is an Invalid Date, so getTime() is NaN and the rendered Discord relative timestamp `<t:NaN:R>` is broken on the live "Claim Status" line. (src/ui/reviewCard.ts:96 has a robust parseClaimedAt that handles numeric strings; card.ts does not, so the two renderers disagree.) Root cause is the type/representation mismatch introduced at this write site.
fix: Standardize the representation. Simplest: store ISO text here (e.g. tsToIso(nowUtc()) or datetime('now')) so it matches the declared type and both parsers; OR change card.ts:339-342 to use the tolerant parseClaimedAt() (or Number()-first heuristic) like ui/reviewCard.ts. Pick one canonical format and apply it at every read/write of claimed_at.

title: Unclaim via modal: 'ephemeral' confirmation is not ephemeral and overwrites the review card
detail: handleUnclaimAction is reached two ways: directly from the unclaim button (deferUpdate'd) and from the unclaim confirmation MODAL (handlers/modals.ts:242-270 calls deferUpdate() then handleUnclaimAction). After unclaim succeeds, line 243 calls replyOrEdit(interaction, { content: `Application \`code\` unclaimed successfully.`, flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }). When the interaction is deferred (both paths defer), replyOrEdit takes the editReply branch (src/lib/cmdWrap.ts:503-506) which DESTRUCTURES AND DISCARDS `flags` and edits the deferred source message. So (a) the Ephemeral flag is silently ignored, and (b) editReply targets the review card message the unclaim button lives on, overwriting the freshly re-rendered card (ensureReviewMessage was just called at line 233) with the plain text "Application … unclaimed successfully.", dropping the embed/buttons. handleClaimToggle relies on this same editReply-edits-card behavior ON PURPOSE (line 145-150), which is why this asymmetric misuse for unclaim is easy to miss.
fix: For confirmations that must be ephemeral after a deferUpdate, use interaction.followUp({ content, flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral }) instead of replyOrEdit, or have replyOrEdit fall through to followUp when the caller passes Ephemeral on a deferred(update) interaction. Do not editReply the card unless that is the intent.

title: beforeSend only scrubs event.message, not exception values — Discord tokens/secrets in thrown errors reach Sentry unredacted
detail: The beforeSend hook applies the Discord-token regex and env scrubbing ONLY to event.message and event.contexts.runtime.env. However, captureException() (the primary path, called from index.ts uncaughtException/unhandledRejection handlers and captureException() throughout the codebase) puts the error text in event.exception.values[].value and stack frames, NOT event.message. So if a Discord bot token, DSN, or other secret ever appears in a thrown Error's message or stack (e.g. a discord.js error echoing an Authorization header, or an error string built from config), it is sent to Sentry verbatim with no redaction. The token regex never runs against the field that actually carries exception text. This defeats the stated purpose ('tokens in error messages would be a security nightmare').
fix: In beforeSend, also iterate event.exception?.values and run the same token regex on each value.value (and optionally on stack frames / breadcrumb messages / event.request data). Factor the redaction into a helper and apply it to message, exception values, and breadcrumbs uniformly. Consider also setting sendDefaultPii:false and using Sentry's built-in data scrubbing.

title: Sentry onFatalError calls process.exit(1) immediately, bypassing the app's deliberate delayed-exit-to-flush and buffered-write flush
detail: onUncaughtExceptionIntegration.onFatalError logs then calls process.exit(1) synchronously. But src/index.ts:54-63 installs its own uncaughtException handler that intentionally does setTimeout(() => process.exit(1), UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION_EXIT_DELAY_MS) specifically to 'Give Sentry time to flush'. Sentry's integration also listens on uncaughtException; its onFatalError firing an immediate process.exit(1) preempts that delay, so (a) the Sentry capture may not finish flushing over the network, and (b) buffered writes that are only drained in the SIGTERM/SIGINT graceful path (messageActivityLogger.flushOnShutdown, messageArchive.flushArchiveBuffersOnShutdown, voice session close, DB close) are skipped entirely on an uncaught exception, risking lost activity/archive data. The comment 'let app handle gracefully / Allow existing handlers to run' directly contradicts the immediate exit.
fix: Do not call process.exit(1) inside onFatalError. Either let the app's own uncaughtException handler own the exit (after its flush delay), or in onFatalError await Sentry.close(timeout) and trigger the same buffer-flush sequence before exiting. At minimum, replace the immediate exit with a short setTimeout matching UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION_EXIT_DELAY_MS so the delayed-flush intent is preserved.

title: closed_at parsed with new Date() treats SQLite's space-separated UTC timestamp as local time, skewing the 7-day reopen window
detail: closeTicket (tickets.ts:165) writes closed_at via datetime('now'), which yields a string like '2026-05-31 12:00:00' — UTC with a SPACE separator and NO 'Z'/offset. At line 73, closedAt = new Date(ticket.closed_at).getTime(). Per ECMAScript, a non-ISO, space-separated datetime string is parsed in the host LOCAL time zone, not UTC (only the 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ' ISO form is guaranteed UTC). So the computed epoch is shifted by the server's UTC offset (up to ~14h). The threshold 'now - closedAt > 7 days' (line 77) therefore decides reopen-vs-new-thread using a time that is off by the offset: on a server west of UTC it makes the window effectively longer (reopens threads that are actually older than 7 days), east of UTC effectively shorter. The team already KNOWS this exact pitfall: web/src/lib/server/queries/shared.ts normalizeTimestamp() comments 'SQLite datetime(now) returns YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (UTC, no Z suffix). new Date() parses space-separated formats as local time — normalize to ISO8601 UTC' and the dashboard modmail query uses it. This reopen path (and the identical dashboardBridge.ts:304) bypass that normalization. Tests miss it because the fixtures feed closed_at via Date.toISOString() (threadReopen.test.ts:191/255/286), i.e. proper ISO with 'Z', which never reproduces the space-separated production format.
fix: Normalize before parsing, mirroring shared.ts: const iso = ticket.closed_at.includes('T') ? ticket.closed_at : ticket.closed_at.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z'; const closedAt = ticket.closed_at ? new Date(iso).getTime() : 0; (or store closed_at as a unix epoch via strftime('%s','now') consistently). Apply the same fix to src/features/modmail/dashboardBridge.ts:304.

title: clearStaleAcknowledgments deletes ALL acks when validKeys is empty (json_each NOT IN empty set)
detail: clearStaleAcknowledgments runs `DELETE ... WHERE guild_id = ? AND issue_key NOT IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?))`. When `validKeys` is empty, `keysJson` is '[]', so `json_each('[]')` yields zero rows and `issue_key NOT IN (<empty>)` is TRUE for every row -> every acknowledgment for the guild is deleted. The sole caller (src/features/serverAuditDocs.ts:76-77) builds `validKeys = new Set(issues.map(i => i.issueKey))` from analyzeSecurityIssues(). If a transient/partial Discord fetch (fetchRoles/fetchChannels) yields incomplete data so analyze produces zero issues, every previously-acknowledged issue is permanently wiped, and on the next clean audit those issues reappear as un-acknowledged 'new' warnings, spamming staff. (For a genuinely clean server with no issues this delete is harmless because there is nothing left to ack, so impact is limited to the partial-fetch / analyzer-regression case.)
fix: Guard the empty case: `if (validKeys.size === 0) return 0;` before running the delete, and/or only run the cleanup when the audit fetch is known to be complete (e.g., roles/channels arrays non-empty). Alternatively skip the prune when issues.length === 0 in serverAuditDocs.ts.

title: Crash recovery loads game-night sessions into the movie session map
detail: recoverPersistedSessions() reads active_movie_events and active_movie_sessions with NO event_type filter, even though those tables are shared with game nights (gameNight.ts persists rows with event_type='game'). gameNight.recoverPersistedGameSessions (gameNight.ts:444,467) correctly filters WHERE event_type='game', but the movie recovery does not. After a restart, game-night active events/sessions are loaded into movieSessions/activeEvents and will be treated as movie attendance (e.g. surfaced by /movie resume, finalized as movie rows). Both recovery paths run at startup, so the game rows get pulled into both maps.
fix: Filter the movie recovery queries to event_type='movie' (or IS NULL for legacy rows): add WHERE event_type='movie' to both SELECTs in recoverPersistedSessions, mirroring gameNight.ts.

title: Gatekeeper-denial tests only assert the guard was *called*, never that the command aborted — an inverted/removed authz check would not be caught
detail: The 'denies access when user lacks gatekeeper role' test sets requireGatekeeper -> false and then asserts only `expect(requireGatekeeper).toHaveBeenCalled()`. It never asserts that the privileged work was skipped (e.g., that findAppByShortCode / approveTx were NOT invoked, or that no approval reply was produced). Because the denial message is produced inside requireGatekeeper itself (which is mocked away), the test has no observable post-condition for the abort. Consequence: if src/commands/gate/accept.ts regressed to `if (requireGatekeeper(...)) return;` (inverted) or dropped the early `return`, an unprivileged user could drive the approval flow and the suite would stay green. The identical weak pattern appears in the sibling gate-command tests, all on security-critical authz paths: gate/reject.test.ts (127-144), gate/kick.test.ts (137-146), gate/unclaim.test.ts (130-139), and gateMain.test.ts (202-209, requireStaff).
fix: After the guarded execute() call, also assert the command short-circuited: e.g. `expect(findAppByShortCode).not.toHaveBeenCalled();` and `expect(approveTx).not.toHaveBeenCalled();` (and the analogous tx/lookup mocks for reject/kick/unclaim/gate). This makes an inverted or removed guard fail the test.

title: reopenTicket can violate partial unique index when user has a newer open ticket
detail: db.ts defines `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_modmail_open_unique ON modmail_ticket(guild_id, user_id, status) WHERE status='open'` (db.ts:195-198), enforcing at most one open ticket per (guild,user). reopenModmailThread's user-based lookup (threadReopen.ts:44-57) explicitly selects the most recent ticket WHERE status='closed'. If, after that ticket was closed, a NEW modmail was opened for the same user (a normal sequence), that new ticket is already status='open'. reopenTicket() then runs `UPDATE ... SET status='open'` on the old closed ticket inside the db.transaction at threadReopen.ts:89-109, which collides with the partial unique index and throws SQLITE_CONSTRAINT. The transaction rolls back and the catch at threadReopen.ts:150-154 returns a generic 'Failed to reopen modmail thread. Check logs.' Impact: staff get an opaque failure (and a logged error/Sentry capture) instead of a clear 'user already has an open modmail' message; the real cause is hidden. The guard-table UPSERT in the same transaction would also have pointed the open_modmail row at the wrong (old) thread had the UPDATE succeeded.
fix: Before reopening by userId, check for an existing open ticket (getOpenTicketByUser) and short-circuit with a clear message linking the existing thread; otherwise catch SQLITE_CONSTRAINT specifically in reopenModmailThread and surface 'This user already has an open modmail thread.'

title: Hive tests re-implement parsing logic inline and never call detectHive — zero real coverage
detail: The file's stated purpose is to 'Verify response parsing and error handling' of src/features/aiDetection/hive.ts, but detectHive is never imported or invoked. Every 'parsing' test (lines 40-196) copies the nesting/loop logic into the test body and asserts on that local copy (e.g., lines 58-75, 92-106, 148-160). Config/timeout tests (lines 199-223) assert string/number literals constructed in the test. Because the real detectHive (which performs the fetch, the !response.ok throw at hive.ts:39-42, the output guard at hive.ts:60-64, and the class scan at hive.ts:68-76) is never executed, any regression in the real parser (wrong key path, dropped typeof guard, inverted ok check) passes this suite. This is a test that looks like coverage but provides none for the module it names.
fix: Mock global.fetch (the file already saves originalFetch at line 27 but never uses it) and call detectHive(url), asserting the returned number/null for the documented response shapes and error codes. Remove or convert the inline-logic 'tests' into real calls.

title: Optic tests re-implement parsing inline and never call detectOptic — zero real coverage
detail: Same pattern as the Hive test. The file claims to verify src/features/aiDetection/optic.ts response parsing/error handling, but detectOptic is never imported or called. The 'parsing' tests (lines 33-101) just read `response?.report?.ai?.confidence` from local literals; the API-config tests (lines 105-123) assert locally-built strings; the 'non-numeric confidence' test (lines 91-101) only checks `typeof x === 'number'` on a local object, not optic.ts's actual guard at optic.ts:57-60. The real function's behavior (Bearer header, `object` body key at optic.ts:32-34, !response.ok throw, null on non-numeric) is never exercised, so regressions in optic.ts would not fail this suite.
fix: Mock fetch and invoke detectOptic(url); assert the numeric/null return and that the request used the `object` body key and Bearer auth. Replace inline-logic assertions with real calls.

title: Most activityTracker tests assert local literals/SQL strings, not the module under test
detail: Only the first describe block (lines 59-86) actually calls trackJoin. Everything after line 88 — the UPSERT SQL block (92-102), silent-days math (114-166), config checks (171-197), first-message existence (201-224), embed format (229-258), edge cases (263-295), and schema-column lists (299-330) — constructs strings/objects/arithmetic inside the test and asserts on those, never touching activityTracker.ts. For example the 'uses UPSERT for join tracking' test (92-102) asserts a SQL string defined in the test, while the real trackJoin SQL lives at activityTracker.ts:40-48 and additionally sets `left_at = NULL` on conflict (not present in the test's copy). The silent-days flag logic is re-derived (143-165) instead of calling evaluateAndFlag. These pass unconditionally and cannot detect a real change in the module (e.g., flipping `< config.silentDays` at activityTracker.ts:213, or changing the UPSERT). Note trackFirstMessage/trackLeave/evaluateAndFlag have no real test here at all.
fix: Drive behavior through the exported functions: assert trackJoin's prepared SQL via the db mock (it can capture the SQL passed to prepare) including the `left_at = NULL` clause, and add tests that call trackFirstMessage to exercise the threshold/flag path. Delete or rewrite the literal-only describe blocks.

title: Synchronous DB throw escapes Promise.allSettled, defeating the partial-results design
detail: executeAnalyticsCommand builds the Promise.allSettled input by EAGERLY calling the query functions: `Promise.resolve(getActionCountsByMod(...))`, `Promise.resolve(getTopReasons(...))`, etc. The real query functions in src/features/analytics/queries.ts are synchronous (better-sqlite3) and re-throw on any DB error (queries.ts:144, 258, 357, 457, 527). Because the call happens during array-literal construction, a synchronous throw propagates out BEFORE Promise.allSettled is ever invoked, so it is NOT captured as a 'rejected' settlement. It is instead caught by the outer try/catch at command.ts:336, which logs an error and replies '❌ Analytics query failed' — the exact opposite of the intended behavior, which is to show partial results (warn + show whatever succeeded). One failing query thus blanks the entire command instead of degrading gracefully. The test tests/features/analytics/command.test.ts:271-283 ('handles query failures gracefully') hides this because it uses mockGetActionCountsByMod.mockRejectedValue(...) which returns an already-rejected Promise (async) rather than throwing synchronously like the real code path; so the test exercises a code path that production never takes.
fix: Wrap each call so a synchronous throw becomes a rejected promise that allSettled can capture, e.g. use `Promise.resolve().then(() => getActionCountsByMod(...))` for each entry, or wrap the bodies in async helper functions. Then allSettled will correctly mark individual failures as rejected and the partial-results/warn path will run.

title: Monthly leaderboard/stats compare ISO-8601 string against SQLite datetime('now') format, undercounting month-boundary completions
detail: getMonthlyLeaderboard and getArtistStats compute the month start with `new Date(); setDate(1); setHours(0,0,0,0); .toISOString()`, producing a string like '2026-05-01T00:00:00.000Z' (with 'T' separator, milliseconds, and 'Z'). They then compare `completed_at >= startIso`. But completed_at is written by `datetime('now')` (store.ts:297) which produces SQLite's canonical format '2026-05-01 00:00:00' (SPACE separator, no ms, no 'Z'). The two formats are compared lexically. At character index 10 the stored value has ' ' (0x20) while the bound has 'T' (0x54); since ' ' < 'T', any job whose completed_at date-part equals the boundary day (the 1st of the month at/after midnight) compares as LESS THAN startIso and is wrongly excluded from the monthly count. Additionally, toISOString() converts LOCAL midnight to a UTC instant while completed_at is stored in UTC, so the boundary is further skewed by the server's UTC offset. Net effect: a recurring, silent undercount of jobs completed around the start of each month in artist leaderboards and stats. store.test.ts mocks db.get/all and only asserts pass-through values, so it never exercises this comparison and cannot catch the bug.
fix: Make the bound match the stored format and timezone. Either compute the boundary with SQLite (e.g. `completed_at >= datetime('now','start of month')`) or format the JS Date as a UTC 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' string (space separator, no ms/Z) using UTC getters. Whichever is chosen, the comparison string and the stored column must use the same format and the same (UTC) timezone.

title: Local BUTTON_RE diverges from the real BTN_DECIDE_RE it claims to test, giving false coverage of the review button router
detail: The `describe("BUTTON_RE pattern")` block defines its OWN regex `const BUTTON_RE = /^v1:decide:(\w+):code([0-9A-F]{6})$/;` and asserts against it. The production symbol it purports to cover is `src/features/review/handlers/helpers.ts:38` `export const BUTTON_RE = BTN_DECIDE_RE;`, which resolves to `src/lib/modalPatterns.ts:35`: `/^(?:v1:decide|review):(approve|accept|reject|kick|claim|unclaim|wrong_password|stale_modmail):code([0-9A-F]{6})$/`. The two differ materially: (1) the test uses `(\w+)` for the action, accepting ANY word, whereas production restricts to a fixed allowlist; (2) the test omits the `review:` prefix alias that modalPatterns.ts explicitly keeps for weeks-old button embeds. Because the test never imports the real regex, a regression in BTN_DECIDE_RE (e.g. dropping `kick` from the allowlist, or removing the `review:` alias) would NOT fail any of these tests. The button router gates moderation actions (approve/reject/kick/claim), so this is security-relevant code with effectively zero regression protection from this suite.
fix: Import the real constant instead of redefining it: `import { BUTTON_RE } from "../../../../src/features/review/handlers/helpers.js";` (or import `BTN_DECIDE_RE` from `src/lib/modalPatterns.js`) and assert against that. Add cases proving the action allowlist is enforced (e.g. `v1:decide:bogus:codeABCDEF` must NOT match) and that the `review:` prefix alias matches.

title: actionRunners.test.ts never imports or invokes the action runners it claims to test (vacuous coverage)
detail: The file is titled 'Unit tests for review action runner functions' and contains describe blocks named runApproveAction/runRejectAction/runPermRejectAction/runKickAction, but it never imports actionRunners.ts and never calls runApproveAction/runRejectAction/runPermRejectAction/runKickAction (grep confirms these names appear only inside describe() strings). Every 'it' asserts against a locally re-implemented literal, e.g. line 161 `const feature = ["review","approve"]; expect(feature).toContain("review")`, line 219 `expect(Object.values(conditions).every(Boolean)).toBe(true)`, line 264 a hand-written roleNote string. The only real imports (approveTx/rejectTx/kickTx from flows/index.js, getClaim/claimGuard) are mocked and then the mocks are called directly (e.g. line 124 `approveTx(...)` returns the mock). Impact: the critical moderation orchestration in actionRunners.ts -- claim-guard enforcement (lines 75-82), the 'role grant failed -> abort approval, do NOT send welcome DM' BLOCK (actionRunners.ts:128-149), modmail auto-close ordering, dmDelivered/roleApplied meta writes, and the duplicate ensureReviewMessage refresh -- has ZERO behavioral coverage from this file while the file name implies it is covered. A regression in any of those paths (e.g. removing the role-grant block, letting an unclaimed mod approve) would not fail a single assertion here. The divergence is concrete: line 124/151 mock approveTx to return {kind:"ok"}, but the real TxResult union (src/features/review/types.ts:132-136) has no "ok" kind (success is "changed"), showing the test was written against a misremembered contract.
fix: Import the real runners and drive them with the existing discord.js/db mocks (the sibling approve.test.ts shows the pattern). Assert on the mocked collaborators: that replyOrEdit gets the claim-guard string when claimGuard returns non-null, that channel.send + updateReviewActionMeta({roleApplied:false,dmDelivered:false}) fire and deliverApprovalDm is NOT called when accepted_role_id is set but roleApplied is false, etc. At minimum delete the literal-only assertions so they stop counting toward the coverage gate and misrepresenting coverage.

title: buttons.test.ts never imports the button handlers; all assertions are local re-implementations
detail: Despite describe blocks for handleReviewButton/handleModmailButton/handlePermRejectButton/handleCopyUidButton/handlePingInUnverified/handleDeletePing, the file never imports buttons.ts and never calls any handler. The customId regexes are re-declared inline (e.g. line 84 BUTTON_RE, line 155 BTN_MODMAIL_RE) instead of imported from src/lib/modalPatterns.js, so if the real regex drifts from the test copy the tests still pass. Routing assertions are tautologies, e.g. line 100-103 `const opensModal = ["reject",...].includes("reject"); expect(opensModal).toBe(true)`. Security-relevant behavior in the real handler is therefore untested: requireInteractionStaff gating (buttons.ts:77,216,286,319,637), the per-action rate-limit deferUpdate path (buttons.ts:84-92), allowedMentions hardening on the unverified ping (buttons.ts:494 `{users:[userId],parse:[]}`), and findAppByShortCode existence check before replying with a UID (buttons.ts:334). A regression that, say, dropped the staff check or widened allowedMentions would not fail here even though 'permission checks' tests exist. Impact: false confidence on a moderator-only, mention-capable surface.
fix: Import BUTTON_RE/BTN_* from src/lib/modalPatterns.js so the test exercises the real patterns, and invoke the exported handlers with mocked ButtonInteraction objects, asserting that non-staff interactions get the 'Gatekeeper role required' reply and that the ping path sends with parse:[] and only the target user. Remove the tautological `.includes(...)` literal assertions.

title: claimHandlers.test.ts never imports handleClaimToggle/handleUnclaimAction; tests assert only literals
detail: The file claims to test handleClaimToggle and handleUnclaimAction but never imports claimHandlers.ts and never calls either function. Each case rebuilds a string locally, e.g. line 72-75 `const msg = errorCode === "ALREADY_CLAIMED" ? "..." : "..."; expect(msg).toContain("already claimed")`, and the 'permanent rejection check' (line 110-112) asserts a hard-coded SQL string rather than that the handler actually runs that query. Consequently the real claim flow is untested: the post-claim permanently_rejected re-check (claimHandlers.ts:84-102), the ClaimError->message mapping, the assumption that the parent already called deferUpdate, and the audit/log/notify side effects. A regression (e.g. removing the perm-rejected block so a banned user can be claimed/approved) passes all assertions here.
fix: Import the real handlers and drive them with mocked reviewActions.claimTx/unclaimTx (throwing ClaimError instances) plus a mock db, asserting replyOrEdit content and that ensureReviewMessage/logActionPretty/notifyDashboard are invoked on the success path and skipped on the error paths.

title: Entire 'modals' suite never imports or executes the module under test (tautological tests)
detail: The file is named/structured as tests for the review modal submission handlers (handleRejectModal, handleAcceptModal, handlePermRejectModal, handleKickModal, handleUnclaimModal) in src/features/review/handlers/modals.ts, and it sets up vi.mock for logger/sentry/cmdWrap as if it will drive that module. But it imports NOTHING from modals.ts. Every single 'it' block re-implements the logic inline (e.g. `reasonRaw.trim().slice(0,500)`, regex literals re-declared locally, `customId` string templates) and asserts on those local re-implementations. Concrete impact: a real regression in modals.ts (wrong field id, missing trim/slice, wrong action dispatch, removed staff check, dropped deferUpdate) would NOT fail this suite — it provides false coverage. The describe blocks 'action dispatching', 'staff validation', 'application resolution' assert hard-coded booleans/strings (`expect(checkPerformed).toBe(true)`, `expect(action).toBe('runRejectAction')`) that can never fail.
fix: Import the actual handlers from src/features/review/handlers/modals.js and invoke them with a mocked ModalSubmitInteraction (fields.getTextInputValue, deferUpdate, customId, user.id, inGuild). Assert that resolveApplication/runRejectAction/etc. (mocked) are called with the parsed code and trimmed/truncated reason, and that non-matching customIds early-return. Delete the assert-a-literal tests.

title: Trace-ID tests assert behavior the source does not implement (interactionId.slice(-8))
detail: Tests 'generates trace ID from interaction ID', 'uses last 8 chars of interaction ID', and 'converts to uppercase' assert that the error trace id equals `interactionId.slice(-8).toUpperCase()`. The real modals.ts catch blocks compute `const traceId = ctx().traceId ?? newTraceId();` (modals.ts lines 66,104,143,182,272). newTraceId() (src/lib/reqctx.ts:39) returns an 11-char random base62 string and never touches the interaction id. So the documented/asserted trace-id derivation is simply false. Because the tests only exercise their own inline slice() expression they still pass, masking that (a) the real trace logic is untested and (b) the described behavior is wrong. Anyone reading the suite is misled about how trace ids are produced.
fix: Remove these trace-id-from-interaction tests, or rewrite them to mock src/lib/reqctx (ctx/newTraceId) and assert the handler logs/replies with the value returned by newTraceId()/ctx().traceId. Do not assert a slice of interaction.id.

title: isStaff / requireInteractionStaff / resolveApplication tests never call the real functions
detail: The describe blocks for isStaff, requireInteractionStaff and resolveApplication do not import or call those functions from src/features/review/handlers/helpers.ts. They instead call the mocked primitives directly (e.g. `hasRole(member,'gatekeeper-role-id')`, `findAppByShortCode(...)`, `loadApplication(...)`) and assert the mock returns what it was told to return (e.g. line 155-159 sets findAppByShortCode -> {id:'app-123'} then asserts it returns {id:'app-123'}). The real branching logic — bypass-then-role precedence in isStaff, guild/guildId rejection + reply in requireInteractionStaff, and the guild-mismatch / null-app early returns in resolveApplication — is never executed. A bug such as inverting `shouldBypass`, dropping the `app.guild_id !== guildId` check (a real authz guard, helpers.ts:117), or failing to send the ephemeral 'Guild only.' reply would pass this suite.
fix: Import isStaff/requireInteractionStaff/resolveApplication from helpers.js and assert their real return values and side-effects (reply/replyOrEdit called with the right content/flags, null returned on guild mismatch). Keep shouldBypass/hasRole/findAppByShortCode/loadApplication mocked as inputs.

title: "returns a copy" tests pass trivially and miss the real shallow-copy aliasing bug in getSchedulerHealth
detail: getSchedulerHealth() returns `new Map(schedulerHealth)` (schedulerHealth.ts:114) which is a SHALLOW copy: the SchedulerHealth value objects are the SAME references stored internally. recordSchedulerRun mutates those objects in place (lines 73-83: health.lastRunAt = now; health.consecutiveFailures++ etc.). Therefore a caller holding a result from getSchedulerHealth() will see its objects mutate out from under it on the next scheduler run, and could even corrupt internal state by writing to them. getSchedulerHealthByName, by contrast, returns a spread copy ({ ...health }, line 132), so the two accessors are inconsistent. The test "returns a copy of the internal map" only checks `health1 !== health2`, which is trivially true for any `new Map()` and does NOT detect the value-object aliasing. The timestamp-preservation tests (246-266) also re-read via getSchedulerHealthByName (which copies) so they never exercise the aliased map. Impact: the unit tests give false assurance that getSchedulerHealth returns an isolated snapshot; the underlying aliasing/shared-mutable-state defect is real but uncaught.
fix: In schedulerHealth.ts make getSchedulerHealth() deep-copy the values: `return new Map(Array.from(schedulerHealth, ([k, v]) => [k, { ...v }]));`. Then strengthen the test to capture a value object from getSchedulerHealth(), call recordSchedulerRun again, and assert the previously captured object did NOT change (e.g., totalRuns stayed the same).

title: "clamps odds to minimum/maximum" tests are vacuous: odds=0 is coerced to 1000 before the clamp, and mocked constants diverge from production
detail: Two problems. (1) The test 'clamps odds to minimum' (line 265-272) sets dadmode_odds: 0 and expects a reply. But the source (src/listeners/messageDadMode.ts:73) computes `odds = Math.max(DADMODE_ODDS_MIN, Math.min(DADMODE_ODDS_MAX, Number(cfg.dadmode_odds || 1000)))`. Because `0 || 1000` evaluates to 1000 (0 is falsy), the value 0 is replaced by 1000 BEFORE reaching Math.max, so the DADMODE_ODDS_MIN clamp branch is never exercised — the test name is misleading and the lower-bound clamp is effectively untested. (2) The test mocks src/lib/constants.js (line 27-30) with DADMODE_ODDS_MIN:1, DADMODE_ODDS_MAX:10000, but the real constants (src/lib/constants.ts:34-35) are DADMODE_ODDS_MIN:2, DADMODE_ODDS_MAX:100000. So 'clamps odds to maximum' (line 274-282) asserts a 10000 ceiling that does not exist in production (real ceiling 100000). A regression that changed the real MIN/MAX constants would not be caught by these tests. Impact: false confidence that odds clamping is validated; the actual production clamp bounds are untested.
fix: Use a non-falsy out-of-range value to exercise the lower clamp (e.g. dadmode_odds: -5 or 1, which survives the `|| 1000` guard and reaches Math.max(DADMODE_ODDS_MIN,...)). Do NOT mock constants.js (or mock it with the real values) so the test validates the production bounds; assert the effective odds via the number of Math.random buckets or by spying on the computed odds.

title: Skullmode clamp tests are vacuous (odds=0 coerced to 1000) and mock SKULLMODE_ODDS_MAX=10000 while production is 1000
detail: Same defect class as the dadmode test.
