'clamps odds to minimum' (line 146-153) sets skullmode_odds: 0 and expects a react, but src/listeners/messageSkullMode.ts:44 does `Number(cfg.skullmode_odds || 1000)` so 0 becomes 1000 and the SKULLMODE_ODDS_MIN clamp (Math.max) is never exercised. 'clamps odds to maximum' (line 155-163) and 'does not react when roll is non-zero' (line 136-144) run against a MOCKED SKULLMODE_ODDS_MAX of 10000 (test line 27-30), but the real constant (src/lib/constants.ts:39) is SKULLMODE_ODDS_MAX = 1000 — a 10x divergence. The max-clamp behavior the test claims to verify (cap at 10000) is not what production does (cap at 1000). A change to the real bound would not be caught. Impact: false confidence; production odds bounds untested.
fix: Exercise the lower clamp with a value that is not falsy (e.g. 1 or a negative number). Stop mocking constants.js with non-production values; import the real bounds or assert the clamped odds explicitly so the test reflects SKULLMODE_ODDS_MAX=1000.

title: Heatmap can include messages outside the requested range when span isn't a multiple of 7 days
detail: getHeatmapDataForRange computes weeksCount = ceil(spanS / 7d) and then carves 7-day windows strictly backwards from endS: weekEndS = endS - offset*7d, weekStartS = weekEndS - 7d. The oldest window therefore starts at endS - weeksCount*7d, which is EARLIER than the requested range.startS whenever (endS - startS) is not an exact multiple of 7 days. For a custom window (e.g., a 10-day or 40-day range from the dashboard time picker), this pulls message_activity rows from before the user-selected start into the totals/trends, so totalMessages, avgMessagesPerHour, busiest/least-active hours and week-over-week growth are computed over a wider span than requested. The COUNT/trends silently over-report.
fix: Clamp the oldest window to startS: compute weekStartS = Math.max(weekStartS, startS) for the final iteration (or derive weeksCount so the earliest weekStartS == startS). Alternatively iterate forward from startS and let the last week be the partial one, clamping weekEndS to endS.

title: Stale push subscriptions keep receiving tier-gated PII after a user is demoted or removed
detail: Tier on a push subscription is only refreshed reactively when a 'role:changed' SSE event arrives (updateTier on lines 87-96). If a moderator is demoted or leaves the guild while the bot/web is down, or if the role:changed event is never emitted for that user, their stored `tier` stays at the old (higher) value. pushBroadcast then still passes the hasMinTier check (line 122) and sends notifications whose body/data include sensitive content — applicant display names (review:submitted body, line 63) and appId, and modmail/audit context — to a device that should no longer have access. There is no authoritative re-check of the subscriber's current roles at send time; tier is trusted from the local push.db row.
fix: Treat the stored tier as a cache only: re-resolve the user's current tier at send time (or on a short TTL) via the Discord role source / session, and/or proactively delete subscriptions on demotion and guild-leave events. At minimum, run deleteStaleSubscriptions on role loss and verify tier against a fresh roles lookup before sending tier-restricted payloads.

title: Recurring schedulers run on setInterval(async …) with no re-entrancy guard — overlapping ticks duplicate work
detail: Every scheduler uses `const i = setInterval(async () => { try { await work() } … }, MS)` with no 'is a previous run still in flight?' flag (securityAuditScheduler.ts:349, guildSnapshotScheduler.ts:117, staleApplicationCheck.ts:393, modMetricsScheduler.ts:100, byteMultiplierScheduler.ts:210, diskSpaceScheduler.ts:247, eventTimeoutScheduler.ts:83). setInterval does not await the callback, so if one run's awaited work (Discord REST, guild.fetch(), generateAuditDocs which walks all roles/channels + saves a snapshot) exceeds the interval, the next tick starts a second concurrent run. For securityAudit this means two overlapping runs each call generateAuditDocs/saveSnapshot (src/store/securitySnapshotStore.ts:243) and each post to the logging channel with leadership pings (securityAuditScheduler.ts:195) — duplicate critical-alert pings and a diff computed against a snapshot the other run just wrote. guildSnapshotScheduler additionally mutates module state `_snapshotCount` (guildSnapshotScheduler.ts:94) non-atomically across overlapping async runs, perturbing the 'fetch online every 6th run' cadence. Lower-frequency than finding #1 but unbounded if any single run hangs on a slow API call.
fix: Add a module-level `let running = false` (or a shared promise) guard at the top of each interval callback: `if (running) { logger.warn('previous run still in flight, skipping'); return; } running = true; try { await work() } finally { running = false; }`. This is the standard fix and also fixes the _snapshotCount/_lastAlertTime ordering issues for free.

title: Analytics CSV export can hang forever (retaining full CSV buffer + interaction) due to end-listener race
detail: In the /stats export flow the handler builds a PassThrough, attaches a 'data' listener that accumulates the entire CSV into `chunks: Buffer[]`, then calls `streamReviewActionsCSV(opts, stream)` and `await`s it. Inside src/lib/csv.ts (line 253) `streamReviewActionsCSV` itself calls `stream.end()` on the success path and then resolves. Only AFTER the await resolves does command.ts register `await new Promise(resolve => stream.on('end', resolve))` (line 444-446). Because the PassThrough is already flowing (a 'data' listener is attached) and `end()` was already called inside the awaited promise, the terminal 'end' event can be emitted before this late listener is attached. When that happens the Promise never resolves: the command handler is stuck awaiting forever, permanently retaining the accumulated `chunks` array (the entire CSV, up to many MB for large exports), the PassThrough, the AttachmentBuilder closure, and the un-replied Discord interaction. Repeated exports that lose this race accumulate retained buffers and pending promises in the bot process. This is a cross-file trust bug: command.ts assumes 'end' will fire after it awaits, but csv.ts ends the stream before returning.
fix: Register the completion listener BEFORE awaiting the producer, e.g. capture `const done = once(stream, 'end')` (or use `stream.promises.finished(stream)` / `pipeline`) prior to calling streamReviewActionsCSV, then `await Promise.all([exportPromise, done])`. Better: have streamReviewActionsCSV NOT call stream.end() and let the caller own lifecycle, or collect via `await text(stream)` from node:stream/consumers. Also add an `'error'` handler so a producer error rejects the collection promise instead of leaving it pending.

title: Scheduler deletes the multiplier DB row even when panic mode blocks role removal, and SELECT-then-DELETE is non-atomic across overlapping ticks
detail: cleanupExpiredMultipliers calls removeExpiredMultipliers() (store line 37) which SELECTs all expired rows and then DELETEs them (byteMultiplierStore.ts:182-204) as two separate statements, not inside a db.transaction. The scheduler runs an immediate startup pass (lines 197-207) AND a periodic interval (lines 210-218); if the startup pass is still awaiting Discord REST when the first interval fires (or any tick runs long), a second invocation can SELECT the same not-yet-deleted rows and process them twice — double-removing roles and double-logging byte_multiplier_expired to the audit trail. Separately, processExpiredMultiplier returns early under panic mode (lines 100-109) AFTER the row has already been deleted from the DB, so the multiplier role is left on the member with no tracking row; when panic clears, nothing will ever remove it (the comment at 105-108 acknowledges this requires manual cleanup). Both issues stem from deleting the authoritative row before the side effect that the row exists to drive is confirmed.
fix: Wrap the SELECT+DELETE in a single db.transaction so a batch is claimed atomically (better-sqlite3 transactions are synchronous/ACID), and guard cleanupExpiredMultipliers with a reentrancy lock so overlapping ticks can't both run. For panic mode, check isPanicMode BEFORE deleting the row (or re-insert the row when skipping due to panic) so expired-but-unremoved multipliers are retried after panic clears instead of being orphaned.

title: resolveApplication failure replies wipe the review card when called after deferUpdate()
detail: resolveApplication() emits its not-found / guild-mismatch feedback with replyOrEdit(interaction, { content: ... }) and no ephemeral flag. It is invoked from the modal handlers (modals.ts) and from the claim/wrong_password/stale_modmail button paths (buttons.ts) AFTER deferUpdate() has run. Because deferred=true, replyOrEdit -> editReply edits the source review card, replacing it with 'No application with code XXXXXX.' publicly and stripping its buttons. This turns a benign 'card references a since-deleted app' situation into destruction of the live card. (When invoked from the modal-opening button paths before any defer it is fine — there it correctly uses reply.)
fix: Have resolveApplication detect an already-acknowledged component interaction and use followUp({ flags: Ephemeral }) for its failure messages, or pass a flag from callers indicating whether the interaction was deferUpdate'd so it can choose followUp vs reply.

title: Router error-card fallback uses ensureDeferred (ephemeral deferReply) + editReply, clobbering the source message for component interactions
detail: The catch-all safety net calls ensureDeferred(interaction) then postErrorCard(...). ensureDeferred (cmdWrap.ts:437-474) only ever does deferReply({Ephemeral}); it never handles component interactions via deferUpdate. For a button/select that threw BEFORE acknowledging itself, ensureDeferred issues a deferReply (valid), so postErrorCard's editReply targets the ephemeral reply — OK. But for a button handler that already called deferUpdate() and then threw (e.g. redeemreward confirm in features/artistRotation/handlers.ts:120 onward, byteToken confirm), ensureDeferred sees deferred=true and returns, then postErrorCard -> replyOrEdit -> editReply edits the ORIGINAL component message, overwriting the confirmation/panel embed with the public error card. Note buttons are routed directly (not through wrapCommand), so their post-defer throws land here. The 'public so staff can see' comment in errorCard.ts:224-227 is also wrong on the common path where the prior defer was ephemeral.
fix: Make the router fallback component-aware: if interaction.isMessageComponent() and not yet acknowledged, deferUpdate() (or just followUp) rather than deferReply; and deliver the error card via followUp({ flags: Ephemeral }) when the interaction was acknowledged with deferUpdate, instead of editReply over the source message.

title: Unrecognized modal customId prefixes are silently dropped with no ack and no error card
detail: The isModalSubmit() block handles a fixed set of prefixes (tk:closemod:, help:modal:search, v1:modal:/v1:avatar:confirm18:, v1:gate:reset:, isitreal_modal_). A route-miss error card is posted ONLY inside the v1:modal:/v1:avatar: branch (lines 981-1000). A modal whose customId matches none of these prefixes falls through to the end of the function and returns without ever acknowledging the interaction — no reply, no deferUpdate, no error card, not even a route-miss log. The user sees Discord's generic 'Something went wrong' and there is no trace ID. This is exactly the failure mode that occurs after renaming a modal customId or shipping a new modal without registering its route — the symptom is invisible in logs. Contrast with the slash path (line 234-251) and the inner modal route-miss, both of which respond/log.
fix: Add a final else at the end of the isModalSubmit() block that logs evt:'ix_route_miss' and posts the same postErrorCard route-miss as the inner v1:modal: branch, so any unhandled modal yields an acknowledgement and a reportable trace ID.

title: Entire /analytics command module is dead (never registered or imported)
detail: command.ts exports executeAnalyticsCommand, executeAnalyticsExportCommand, and parseWindow — full slash-command handlers for an /analytics command. But "analytics" is NOT in src/commands/runtimeManifest.ts SLASH_COMMAND_NAMES, is not registered in src/index.ts, and the module is imported by nothing in src/ (only tests/features/analytics/command.test.ts references it). The functionality was reimplemented under src/commands/stats/ (the consolidated /stats command). A startup drift guard in index.ts (lines 274-294) enforces that registered handlers match the manifest, so this module can never be reached at runtime. ~481 lines of dead handler code plus a test suite that only exercises dead code.
fix: Delete src/features/analytics/command.ts and tests/features/analytics/command.test.ts. Confirm /stats fully covers the prior /analytics summary + export behavior before removal.

title: analytics/queries.ts is transitively dead (only consumer is the dead command.ts)
detail: queries.ts exports getActionCountsByMod, getTopReasons, getVolumeSeries, getLeadTimeStats, getOpenQueueAge. Across src/ the only importer is src/features/analytics/command.ts (itself dead) plus tests/features/analytics/queries.test.ts. The single non-test mention elsewhere (src/db/ensure.ts:267) is a comment, not an import. The live /stats command uses src/features/analytics/approvalRate.ts and src/commands/stats/* queries, not this file. ~528 lines dead.
fix: Delete src/features/analytics/queries.ts and its test once command.ts is removed. Verify none of stats/* re-imports these names (they do not).

title: /approval-rate standalone handler is fully orphaned
detail: approvalRateCommand.ts exports executeApprovalRateCommand. Grep across the whole repo shows zero importers — not src/, not even a test. The live approval-rate feature is the /stats approval-rate subcommand (src/commands/stats/approvalRate.ts -> src/commands/stats/index.ts case 'approval-rate'), which imports the shared query module features/analytics/approvalRate.ts directly. This standalone command handler was superseded and left behind. ~196 lines dead.
fix: Delete src/features/analytics/approvalRateCommand.ts. The shared query module src/features/analytics/approvalRate.ts must be kept (it is used by stats/approvalRate.ts).

title: avatar_confirm18 modal route is dead infrastructure and has no handler (latent route-miss bug)
detail: modalPatterns.ts defines MODAL_18_RE (/^v1:avatar:confirm18:code([0-9A-F]{6})$/), the ModalRoute union member { type: 'avatar_confirm18' }, and identifyModalRoute returns it (lines 149-152). However: (1) No code anywhere in src/web/scripts ever creates/shows a modal with customId 'v1:avatar:confirm18:' — grep finds the string only in modalPatterns.ts and interactionCreate.ts, never in a ModalBuilder/showModal call, so the route is unreachable in practice. (2) Even if such a modal were shown, the router in src/events/interactionCreate.ts handles gate_submit_page, review_reject/perm_reject/accept/kick/vote_out/unclaim, report_resolve, qotd_suggest, qotd_reject — but has NO branch for route.type === 'avatar_confirm18'. It would fall through to the catch-all at interactionCreate.ts:984-1000 and post an 'Unhandled modal' error card. So the union member is both dead and a latent bug.
fix: Either remove MODAL_18_RE, the 'avatar_confirm18' union member, its identifyModalRoute branch, and the '|| customId.startsWith("v1:avatar:confirm18:")' clause in interactionCreate.ts:769; or, if the 18+ avatar-source confirmation is intended to exist, wire the showModal producer AND add a matching route.type === 'avatar_confirm18' handler in the router.

title: detectNsfwFlagSurge and detectModmailResponseTime use strftime() on TEXT timestamp columns, forcing full scans
detail: detectNsfwFlagSurge filters nsfw_flags with strftime('%s', flagged_at) >= ? (lines 1216,1222). nsfw_flags.flagged_at is TEXT (migration 032_nsfw_flags.ts:45) and the only indexes are (guild_id) and (guild_id, reviewed) (migration 032:53-54). Wrapping the column in strftime() makes the predicate non-sargable, so SQLite cannot use any time index and scans every flag row for the guild twice (this-window + prev-window). detectModmailResponseTime has the same problem: it computes strftime('%s', mt.created_at) in both the WHERE and via correlated MIN per ticket (lines 1176-1180), defeating any index on modmail_ticket. On servers with large flag/modmail history this is a repeated full/partial scan on the SSR path.
fix: Store/compare timestamps as INTEGER unix seconds (as action_log/message_activity already do) or add a generated/stored *_s column with an index, then filter with plain range comparisons (flagged_at_s >= ? AND flagged_at_s < ?). At minimum add an index on the raw text column and compare against ISO string literals (datetime(?, 'unixepoch')) so the index can be used instead of strftime per row.

title: Review queue layout runs uncached query with ~3 correlated modmail subqueries per application row on every navigation
detail: getReviewQueue() is invoked from dashboard/reviews/+layout.server.ts:14 with NO caching, so it executes on every page load and every client-side navigation into any /dashboard/reviews/* route (the layout re-runs). The query attaches, per pending application row, two correlated scalar subqueries in the SELECT (has_unread_modmail EXISTS at 404-411, modmail_awaiting_since at 412-419) plus a third correlated EXISTS in the ORDER BY (432-439). Each of those contains a further nested 'SELECT MAX(mm2.id) ... WHERE ticket_id = mt.id' subquery. So the work is roughly 3 x (pending app count) correlated subqueries, each doing a nested aggregate. idx_modmail_message_ticket_id(ticket_id, id DESC) (migration 063) helps the MAX lookups but the per-row fan-out and the ORDER BY recomputation remain. Synchronous handle => blocks event loop per load.
fix: Precompute the 'latest message direction + timestamp per open ticket' once via a single GROUP BY / window-function CTE joined to applications, instead of three correlated subqueries per row (the ORDER BY repeats the same EXISTS a fourth time). Cache the queue with the existing cached() helper (short TTL) since the same payload is recomputed on every reviews navigation.

title: Heatmap builder issues one query per week (up to 26) and pulls every raw message row into JS instead of aggregating
detail: getHeatmapDataForRange() loops weeksCount (capped MAX_WEEKS=26) and calls buildWeek() each iteration (lines 180-183). buildWeek() runs 'SELECT created_at_s FROM message_activity WHERE guild_id=? AND created_at_s>=? AND created_at_s<?' (122-127) returning EVERY raw message row for that week, then buckets them in a JS loop (144-150). So a 26-week window = 26 separate queries, each potentially returning tens of thousands of rows, all materialized and iterated in Node on the SSR path. message_activity already has hour_bucket plus idx_message_activity_guild_hour, so the entire grid could be one GROUP BY. Mitigated by the 60s page cache (heatmap/+page.server.ts:20) but every cold load / new window pays it.
fix: Replace the per-week raw-row fetch with a single query over the whole range that GROUPs BY hour_bucket (or by day-of-week/hour), e.g. SELECT (created_at_s/3600)%24 ... COUNT(*) GROUP BY ..., then distribute counts into the week grids in JS. This turns 26 row-streaming queries into one aggregate query and removes the per-row JS bucketing.

title: Third legacy deploy script skips migrations entirely and uses set -e without pipefail/-u
detail: scripts/deploy.sh (distinct from the root deploy.sh) is yet another deploy path to the same prod host. It uses only `set -e` (line 12) — no `-u` (undefined vars silently empty) and no `pipefail` (a failing command upstream of a pipe is masked). More importantly it has NO migration step at all: it extracts the tarball, runs `npm ci --omit=dev`, and `pm2 restart` (lines 122-133), so deploying through this script ships new code that expects a new schema without ever running migrations. Its tarball (line 108) also omits .env.build, web/build, and ecosystem.config.cjs that the root deploy.sh ships, so the build-info/runtime env and web app drift. Having three divergent deploy scripts (root deploy.sh, deploy-no-tests.sh, scripts/deploy.sh) all pointed at PM2 process 'pawtropolis' is a maintenance trap where the safe behavior depends entirely on which file the operator happens to run.
fix: Remove or clearly archive scripts/deploy.sh; converge on the root deploy.sh. If kept, add `set -euo pipefail` and the migration step, and make the tarball contents identical to the canonical deploy.

title: Standalone migration 046 records into a different bookkeeping table than the migration framework
detail: The canonical migration tracker is schema_migrations (scripts/migrate.ts:71-78 and migrations/lib/helpers.ts:149-213 via recordMigration). migrations/046_extend_user_cache_profile.ts:32 correctly calls recordMigration(db, '046', ...) which writes to schema_migrations. But the hand-run helper scripts/run-migration-046.mjs:24-27 writes to a separate `migration_log` table instead. Its filename invites manual use during incident response; if an operator runs it, the ALTERs are applied but schema_migrations is NOT updated, so the next deploy's migrate.ts sees 046 as pending and re-runs migrations/046_*.ts. The 046 migration guards each ALTER with columnExists, so the re-run is non-destructive today, but the divergence is a latent footgun: any future standalone fix script following this pattern for a non-idempotent migration would double-apply.
fix: Make run-migration-046.mjs either call into the same recordMigration logic (write to schema_migrations) or, better, delete it in favor of `npm run migrate`. At minimum, stamp schema_migrations, not migration_log, so the two paths agree.

title: Per-migration transaction does not roll back side effects that do not throw, and version is stamped even for no-op-but-wrong migrations
detail: applyMigration wraps migrateFn in db.transaction (lines 209-213), but as the in-file GOTCHA at 206-208 notes, the transaction only rolls back on a thrown exception. A migration that performs a partial/incorrect change without throwing still commits, and because each migration calls recordMigration itself (inside the same transaction), the version is permanently marked applied. Since the deploy harness above (deploy.sh:435) also swallows failures, a migration that logs an error but exits the function normally will be recorded as applied and never retried. Combined, there is no end-to-end guarantee that 'recorded as applied' means 'schema is correct'.
fix: Have the runner (not each migration) own the stamping: only call recordMigration after migrateFn returns AND after a post-condition check where feasible. Surface any migration-internal error by throwing rather than logging-and-returning. Pair with fixing the deploy.sh swallow so a throw actually aborts.

title: ensureReviewMessage check-then-create race posts duplicate review cards (and double Gatekeeper ping) under concurrent calls
category: Concurrency / check-then-act on shared external state
detail: ensureReviewMessage reads the existing review_card mapping once near the top (lines 799-801) and then decides create-vs-edit based on that snapshot. The decision and the create are separated by many awaits (embed render via inSpan at 837-851, several dynamic imports). On the no-mapping path it does `await channel.send(...)` to post a brand-new card (lines 919-929, including a one-time Gatekeeper/bot-dev role ping) and only writes the review_card row at the very end (upsert at line 958, after the send). If two callers invoke ensureReviewMessage for the same appId while no card exists yet, both read mapping===undefined, both fall into the create branch, both channel.send a card, and the second upsert (review_card.app_id is PRIMARY KEY, db.ts:127-135) either throws a PRIMARY KEY constraint or overwrites -- but two physical Discord messages have already been posted with duplicate role pings, and only one survives in the mapping table (the orphan keeps live buttons). This concurrent no-mapping window is real and acknowledged in-tree: src/features/gate/scan.ts:66-102 added waitForReviewCardMapping() specifically because the avatar-scan job (fired via setImmediate on submit) calls ensureReviewMessage concurrently with the submit handler's own ensureReviewMessage. That poller is only a mitigation with a 5s timeout, and scan.ts:210-217 explicitly calls ensureReviewMessage even when the wait times out (cardReady===false), so a slow initial card-create re-opens the double-post window. ensureReviewMessage has no internal mutex; the comment at scan.ts:71-73 admits 'Polling is simpler than adding cross-module eventing.'
fix: Make card creation atomic against the PRIMARY KEY instead of relying on a pre-read snapshot. Move the channel.send into a flow like modmail threadOpen: first INSERT a placeholder review_card row (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) to claim ownership; only the caller whose INSERT changed a row proceeds to channel.send and then UPDATEs with the real message_id; losers re-read the mapping and edit instead. Alternatively serialize ensureReviewMessage per-appId with an in-process promise chain keyed by appId (as inviteTracker.ts does with trackingQueue). At minimum, re-query the mapping immediately before the create branch (after all awaits) and switch to edit if a row now exists.

title: Level-reward dedup row is committed BEFORE grants succeed, so a transient grant failure permanently skips the reward
detail: handleLevelRoleAdded() writes the dedup marker first: `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO level_reward_granted (guild_id,user_id,level)` (lines 130-133). It then loops over rewards calling assignRole() (line 180). I confirmed in src/features/roleAutomation.ts:298-318 that assignRole()'s `member.roles.add()` call is wrapped in try/catch and returns `{success:false, action:'skipped'}` on ANY error (Discord 429 rate-limit, 5xx, network blip) WITHOUT throwing. levelRewards.ts records these in `failedRewards` and logs 'reward_error' (lines 198-209) but never deletes the dedup row. On the next guildMemberUpdate for the same level (the code explicitly notes Amaribot re-syncs and re-joins are normal, lines 268-269), `dedupResult.changes === 0` triggers the early return at line 143, so the previously-failed reward role is never retried. The user permanently loses that reward. A repo-wide grep confirms there is NO DELETE from level_reward_granted anywhere (only the migration backfill + this insert). docs/INCIDENTS.md:57 documents the dedup-first design as the INC-005 TOCTOU fix, but the ordering converts a transient failure into a permanent one — the code carefully distinguishes granted/skipped/failed yet treats all three identically for dedup purposes.
fix: Only write the dedup marker after a reward is actually granted, OR delete/avoid the dedup row when failedRewards.length>0. Concretely: move the INSERT OR IGNORE to run per-reward after `result.action === 'add'` succeeds, or wrap the dedup-insert + grants in a transaction and `throw` to roll back the marker if any reward returns success:false (so the next event retries). At minimum, on failure execute `DELETE FROM level_reward_granted WHERE guild_id=? AND user_id=? AND level=?` so the failed grant can be retried.

title: Command-center decisionsToday and weekStats omit 'perm_reject', undercounting decisions and skewing avg response time
detail: decisionsToday (line 74) and the weekStats decisions+avg query (line 88) filter `action IN ('approve', 'reject', 'kick')`, omitting 'perm_reject'. Permanent rejections ARE written to review_action with action='perm_reject' (src/features/review/flows/reject.ts:69-77: `const action = permanent ? 'perm_reject' : 'reject'`). Every other decision query in the codebase consistently uses the 4-verb set `('approve','reject','perm_reject','kick')` (see web/src/lib/server/queries/stats.ts and observatory refresh). A grep confirms home.ts lines 74 and 88 are the ONLY occurrences of the 3-verb set anywhere. Result: the home dashboard's 'decisions today' and 'this week' counts under-report by the number of permanent rejections, and the weekly avg-response-time computation excludes perm_reject decisions entirely, so its mean is biased.
fix: Add 'perm_reject' to both IN lists so home.ts matches the rest of the system: `action IN ('approve', 'reject', 'perm_reject', 'kick')`.

title: getApplicationFunnel counts status='perm_rejected', a status the bot never writes, so permRejected is always 0 and permanent rejections are silently bucketed as 'rejected'
detail: The funnel query has `SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'perm_rejected' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as perm_rejected` and also lists 'perm_rejected' in the 'submitted' rollup. But there is no 'perm_rejected' application status anywhere: the application CHECK constraint only allows ('draft','submitted','approved','rejected','needs_info','kicked') (tests/fixtures/schema.sql:201) and the reject transaction sets status='rejected' (with permanently_rejected=1) for BOTH normal and permanent rejections (src/features/review/flows/reject.ts:82-91). This is documented in src/features/gate/drafts.ts:193 and src/commands/listopen.ts:46: 'Permanently rejected apps have status=\'rejected\' with permanently_rejected=1'. Consequences: FunnelMetrics.permRejected is permanently 0, and every permanent rejection is counted in the `rejected` bucket -- the funnel cannot distinguish them. The query ignores the application.permanently_rejected flag entirely.
fix: Count permanent rejections via the real signal: `SUM(CASE WHEN status='rejected' AND permanently_rejected=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS perm_rejected` and, if `rejected` should exclude them, `SUM(CASE WHEN status='rejected' AND COALESCE(permanently_rejected,0)=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS rejected`. Drop 'perm_rejected' from the status IN-lists.

category: JOIN/source correctness (event-log assumption on a current-state table)
title: Observatory leaves / cumulative_net / cohort retention treat user_activity as a join/leave event log, but it stores one current-state row per user that is mutated on rejoin
detail: rebuildDailyMetrics derives daily `leaves` from `COUNT(*) ... WHERE left_at IS NOT NULL GROUP BY date(left_at)` and `joins` from `date(joined_at)`, and cumulative_net accumulates joins-leaves. rebuildCohortRetention buckets members by join-week. But user_activity has PRIMARY KEY (guild_id, user_id) and is upserted: trackJoin (src/features/activityTracker.ts:40-48) does `ON CONFLICT(guild_id,user_id) DO UPDATE SET joined_at = excluded.joined_at, left_at = NULL`. So a member who leaves and later rejoins has their prior leave ERASED (left_at reset to NULL) and their original join day MOVED to the latest join. This makes historical daily `leaves` and `cumulative_net` change retroactively on every rejoin, undercounts gross churn, and shifts cohort membership/size for past weeks. The rollup faithfully reflects stored data, but it trusts user_activity to be an append-only event log when activityTracker maintains it as mutable current-state. (Same assumption underlies the pulse leave-spike / rapid-join-leave detectors in queries/pulse.ts.)
fix: Either source join/leave events from an append-only log (e.g. action_log member_join/member_leave events or invite_usage.joined_at_s) instead of user_activity, or explicitly document leaves/cohort as 'net current-state' metrics. If event-accurate churn is required, stop resetting left_at to NULL on rejoin and record each membership span separately.

title: Expiry cleanup deletes the DB tracking row before (and regardless of whether) the Discord multiplier role is removed; panic mode and member-fetch failures orphan the boost role with no record to retry
detail: removeExpiredMultipliers (byteMultiplierStore.ts line 182-204) fetches expired rows and DELETEs them in the same call. cleanupExpiredMultipliers then tries to strip the Discord role per entry. But if the guild is in panic mode the handler returns early at line 100-109 AFTER the row is already deleted (the code comment at line 105-107 acknowledges staff must remove the role manually). The same orphaning occurs on any non-thrown early return: guild not cached (line 90-97) or member fetch returning null (line 112-120). Because the authoritative record was already destroyed, the scheduler can never retry these, so an expired XP multiplier role persists indefinitely on the member - a continuing economic over-grant (free boost) that no automated process will reclaim. Cross-file: the store's 'delete-on-read' design (intended to prevent double-processing) trades away the ability of the scheduler to recover from its own skipped work.
fix: Only delete rows that were actually reconciled. Either (a) select expired rows, attempt role removal, and DELETE only the successfully-processed ids; or (b) keep the row and mark a processed/last_attempt column, deleting only after confirmed Discord removal. Skip-and-retain on panic mode / fetch failure so the next run can finish the job.

title: Legendary and Epic tokens map to the same multiplier role and value, so the single-row tracking model lets a consumed higher token silently downgrade an active boost with no real warning
detail: BYTE_TOKEN_CONFIG.epic and .legendary share multiplierRoleId '1405369052829974543' and multiplierValue 5, differing only in durationHours (48 vs 72). active_byte_multipliers enforces UNIQUE(guild_id,user_id) (migration 044 line 87), so a user can hold only one tracked multiplier. If a user redeems Legendary (role X, 72h) and later redeems Epic while X is still active, byteTokenHandler upsert overwrites expires_at to now+48h (byteMultiplierStore.ts line 71-78) - the consumed Epic token strictly shortens their remaining boost. The confirmation UI's replace-warning (usebyte.ts line 224-231 / byteTokenHandler.ts line 568-574) shows both as '[5x] Byte'/5x, so the user sees no indication they are trading down. Net effect: a redeemed token can be wasted (or actively reduce value) with no surfaced downside, and the two rarities can never be 'active simultaneously' despite being distinct entitlements.
fix: Either give legendary its own multiplier role, or, before overwriting, compare expiries and keep the longer-lived boost (only extend, never shorten, when the incoming multiplierValue is equal). Make the replace-warning show actual remaining time vs proposed time so users can see a downgrade. Confirm with product whether legendary collapsing into the epic role is intended.

title: Watchdog auto-defers modals with deferReply, racing handlers that ack via deferUpdate
detail: armWatchdog() is armed in interactionCreate.ts (line 219) for EVERY interaction before dispatch, and its 2500ms timer calls modalInteraction.deferReply({ephemeral}) for any unacked ModalSubmitInteraction. However, the review modal handlers (src/features/review/handlers/modals.ts handleRejectModal/handleAcceptModal/handleKickModal/handleUnclaimModal/handleVoteOutModal, all lines ~49/87/126/166/203) and the QOTD reject handler (src/features/qotd/handlers.ts:288-290) acknowledge the SAME modal via deferUpdate(), NOT deferReply. These handlers do meaningful pre-ack work first: requireInteractionStaff -> resolveApplication (findAppByShortCode + loadApplication SQLite) before calling deferUpdate. If that work plus event-loop contention pushes past 2500ms, the watchdog wins the race and calls deferReply first. The handler's later deferUpdate() then fails with 40060 (caught/swallowed by the .catch). Net result: a stray ephemeral 'Bot is thinking...' spinner that never resolves to content (the action's real output goes to interaction.channel.send / interaction.message.edit, not the deferred reply), and the response-state telemetry in the wide event is corrupted (markDeferred recorded, deferUpdate path not). The watchdog and the deferUpdate-based handlers were written against different ack models and only coexist safely because handlers are usually <2500ms. cmdWrap's own comment claims the watchdog 'Only defers modals; slash/button defers are handled by higher-level wrappers' but does not account for handlers that deliberately use deferUpdate.
fix: Make the watchdog ack-type aware, or do not arm it for routes that ack via deferUpdate. Simplest: have armWatchdog use deferUpdate() for modals that originate from a message component (interaction.message != null) and deferReply() only for showModal-from-slash modals; OR drop the global watchdog and let each wrapCommand-wrapped handler own its defer. At minimum, raise WATCHDOG_MS only matters if handlers are slow; the correct fix is to not let two code paths defer the same token with different methods.

title: replyOrEdit silently drops ephemeral (and all) flags on the deferred path
detail: replyOrEdit destructures and discards `flags` when the interaction is deferred: `const { flags, ...editPayload } = withFlags; result = await interaction.editReply(editPayload);` (lines 504-506). editReply genuinely cannot change ephemerality (it's fixed at defer time), so the discard is technically necessary, but the function accepts `flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral` from callers and silently ignores it with no warning. Multiple callers pass ephemeral expecting privacy and trust replyOrEdit to honor it: e.g. handleUnclaimModal's 'You must type UNCLAIM' branch (src/features/review/handlers/modals.ts:259-261), runVoteOutAction's 'Vote out requires a reason' (actionRunners.ts:830-833), and the openRejectModal/openAcceptModal already-resolved branches (helpers.ts:187, 212) all pass flags:Ephemeral. Today these are visually correct only by luck because the preceding ack on those paths was already ephemeral (deferUpdate on the source message keeps the response component-scoped, or ensureDeferred deferred ephemeral). The cross-file trust hazard: any handler that defers PUBLIC (e.g. handleModmailContextMenu deferReply() with no flag, modmail/handlers.ts:190) and then routes a sensitive message through replyOrEdit({flags:Ephemeral}) will leak it publicly with zero indication the flag was dropped.
fix: If a caller passes Ephemeral on a deferred interaction whose deferral was public, log a warning (the flag cannot be honored) so the mismatch is visible. Better: track the deferral's ephemerality on the wide event and assert callers' flags match; or split the API into replyOrEditPublic / replyOrEditEphemeral so the intent is fixed at defer time, not silently reconciled at edit time.

title: safeShowModal dead-ends the user (no ack, no message) past the 2500ms token boundary; caller ignores the false return
detail: safeShowModal returns false (a) if the interaction is already acked, (b) if Date.now()-createdTimestamp > 2500ms, or (c) if showModal throws — and in cases (b)/(c) it sends NO user-facing feedback and performs NO acknowledgement. handleReviewButton (buttons.ts) calls openRejectModal/openAcceptModal/openKickModal/openUnclaimModal/openVoteOutModal which call safeShowModal, and NONE of these call sites inspect the boolean return. For reject/accept/kick/unclaim the button path runs resolveApplication (two synchronous SQLite lookups) BEFORE reaching safeShowModal; under DB lock contention (the codebase elsewhere retries SQLITE_BUSY, see dmVerification.ts:378-389) or event-loop pressure the interaction can cross 2500ms, after which safeShowModal silently bails and the moderator's click resolves to Discord's generic 'This interaction failed' with no modal, no ephemeral error, and no logged trace surfaced to them. Because the interaction was never acked, no error card fires either. This is a cross-file trust gap: buttons.ts trusts safeShowModal to either show the modal or surface a failure, but safeShowModal's contract is 'return false and stay silent'.
fix: Have safeShowModal's caller act on the false return: when it returns false and the interaction is still unacked, send an ephemeral reply ('That action timed out, click again.'). Alternatively move the resolveApplication DB work to AFTER showModal where possible, since showModal needs the fresh token most; for reject/accept the app existence can be revalidated in the modal-submit handler (which it already is via resolveApplication).

title: Entire /analytics command module is unreachable (not registered); 481 lines kept compiling only by tests
detail: command.ts exports executeAnalyticsCommand, executeAnalyticsExportCommand, parseWindow. Outside its own file and tests/features/analytics/command.test.ts, the module has zero importers (verified: grep for the symbol names and 'analytics/command' returns only the file itself + the test). The command name 'analytics' is NOT in src/commands/runtimeManifest.ts (full SLASH_COMMAND_NAMES list dumped and checked) and is not registered in src/index.ts. The functionality was consolidated into /stats (src/commands/stats/* with handlers wired in stats/index.ts). So this is a fully unreachable command handler: it can never be invoked at runtime. It only survives the noUnusedLocals/typecheck gate because its test imports it. This also drags src/features/analytics/queries.ts (528 lines: getActionCountsByMod/getLeadTimeStats/getTopReasons/getVolumeSeries/getOpenQueueAge) into deadness -- queries.ts is imported ONLY by this dead command.ts (verified per-symbol).
fix: Delete src/features/analytics/command.ts and src/features/analytics/queries.ts plus their test files (tests/features/analytics/command.test.ts, queries.test.ts). Keep src/features/analytics/approvalRate.ts -- it is still live (used by src/commands/stats/approvalRate.ts). Confirm nothing in /stats relies on queries.ts (it does not; /stats uses its own handlers) before removal.

title: Entire /approval-rate command module is unreachable (not registered); 196 dead lines
detail: executeApprovalRateCommand (approvalRateCommand.ts:39) is the handler for a standalone /approval-rate command. The module is imported by nobody (verified: only self-references in its own header/docstring; no import of 'approvalRateCommand' anywhere in src/web/scripts/tests). 'approval-rate' is not a standalone entry in runtimeManifest -- only '/stats approval-rate' exists (stats/index.ts:50 routes to handleApprovalRate in commands/stats/approvalRate.ts). So this old top-level handler is unreachable; the live approval-rate path is the /stats subcommand, which independently consumes analytics/approvalRate.ts. Dead since the stats consolidation.
fix: Delete src/features/analytics/approvalRateCommand.ts. Verify no test imports it (none found) and that analytics/approvalRate.ts query functions remain referenced by commands/stats/approvalRate.ts (they are).

title: detectModmailResponseTime wraps indexed TEXT column in strftime(), forcing a full ticket scan
detail: The Pulse insights detector filters modmail_ticket with `WHERE mt.guild_id = ? AND strftime('%s', mt.created_at) >= ? AND strftime('%s', mt.created_at) < ?` (line 1179) and also computes `strftime('%s', mm.created_at) - strftime('%s', mt.created_at)` per message. Wrapping the column `mt.created_at` in strftime() makes the time-range predicate non-sargable: SQLite cannot use the available index on modmail_ticket(guild_id, status) (migration 038) to seek on the time bound, and there is no expression index on strftime(created_at). The query runs twice per Pulse load (this-window + prior-window) inside getInsights, and joins every matching ticket to modmail_message. created_at is declared TEXT (confirmed via modmail_message migration 021 / modmail_ticket schema and the strftime usage), so this is a genuine scan, not an index seek. A secondary correctness smell: strftime('%s', ...) returns a string compared against a numeric bind param, relying on SQLite type coercion. Impact is bounded today because (a) the whole Pulse bundle is cached (CACHE_TTL.medium, in-flight dedup) and (b) ticket volume is moderate, so this is a latent scaling cost rather than an active outage.
fix: Store/compare modmail timestamps as unix-seconds, or compare the raw TEXT column directly against an ISO bound computed in JS (e.g. `mt.created_at >= ?` with an ISO string), so the predicate is sargable against an index on modmail_ticket(guild_id, created_at). Alternatively add an expression index on strftime('%s', created_at). Same treatment applies to the mm.created_at delta if you start filtering on it.

title: Server-side cached() defeats SSE live-refresh on pulse/stats; invalidate() is never called by any mutation
detail: The two-tier cache exposes invalidate(key), but a repo-wide search shows it has ZERO callers anywhere in web/src (only the definition matches). Meanwhile the mutation API routes (/api/review/[action], /api/modmail/*, /api/config/update, etc.) mutate state through the bot and return without touching the cache. The Pulse page (web/src/routes/dashboard/pulse/+page.svelte:83-92) explicitly subscribes to review:*, modmail:*, flag:* and calls invalidateAll() on each event to deliver 'Live pulse updates'; the Stats page does the same on stats:updated. But the data those pages render comes from cached(guildKey, CACHE_TTL.medium=60_000, ...) (pulse) and cached(personalKey/teamKey, CACHE_TTL.medium, ...) (stats), keyed by rangeCacheKeyParts(range,60) whose minute bucket is stable inside any 60s window. So after a moderator approves an application: the DB changes, the SSE event arrives (~150ms debounce), invalidateAll() re-runs the server load, and cached() returns the SAME pre-mutation L1 object for up to ~60s. The counters (Pending Applications, Open Modmail, Decisions/Approvals, team leaderboard) visibly fail to update despite the live wiring, until the TTL lapses. The reviews queue itself is unaffected because its layout load (reviews/+layout.server.ts) is uncached.
fix: Wire invalidate() into the mutation handlers (or invalidate by key prefix) so a review/modmail/flag/config mutation drops the matching pulse:*/stats:* cache entries. Since keys embed guildId + range bucket + (for personal) userId, add a small prefix-scan invalidation (e.g. track keys per namespace, or switch the L1 Map to allow deleting by startsWith('pulse:guild:'+guildId)). Alternatively, have the SSE-triggered reload pass a cache-busting flag the load honors. Minimum: call invalidate for stats:team:* and pulse:guild:* on any review/modmail mutation so the live refresh shows fresh counts.

lines: 49-74 (Promise.race + timeout); queries in web/src/lib/server/queries/audit.ts:55-60 are synchronous better-sqlite3
title: Audit query 8s timeout is ineffective: Promise.race cannot interrupt synchronous better-sqlite3 work
detail: The audit load wraps cached(key, ...) in Promise.race against a setTimeout(8000) that rejects with 'audit-query-timeout' and maps to a 504 ('Narrow the date range...'). But getAuditLog/getActionTypes run synchronously via better-sqlite3 (db().prepare(...).all/get) and block the Node event loop for their entire duration. While the synchronous query runs, the setTimeout callback cannot fire; by the time control returns to the loop, the cached() promise has already resolved and wins the race. The timeout therefore provides no protection at all: a genuinely heavy audit query (broad FTS search over a large window) freezes the whole web process (all concurrent requests, SSE heartbeats, other tabs) for its full runtime, and the 504 branch is effectively dead code. The load trusts Promise.race to bound work that is fundamentally uninterruptible from JS.
fix: Either (a) remove the timeout and bound the work at the SQL/data layer instead (hard LIMITs, mandatory date window, FTS prefix caps, a covering index, or a statement-level progress-handler/interrupt on the better-sqlite3 connection), or (b) move audit queries to a worker_thread so a watchdog timer can actually cancel/abandon them. Do not present a Promise.race timeout as a guard against synchronous DB calls; at minimum drop the misleading 504 path.

title: Pre-deploy DB backup copies a live WAL-mode DB without a checkpoint and misreports any cp failure as 'not found'
detail: maybe_backup_remote_db does `cp ${REMOTE_PATH}/data/data.db .../data.db.${ts} 2>/dev/null && echo OK || echo 'WARNING: data.db not found'`. Two problems. (1) No WAL checkpoint before the copy: the DB runs in WAL mode (ecosystem starts the bot which opens WAL; migrate.ts also sets journal_mode=WAL), so a bare `cp` of just data.db can capture a state missing the committed pages still sitting in data.db-wal, yielding a stale or torn backup. Note the OTHER ops paths get this right: scripts/switch.sh:93 and scripts/start.sh:275,313 run `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)` before copying and also copy -wal/-shm. deploy.sh's backup path is the inconsistent, less-safe sibling. (2) The `2>/dev/null && ... || echo 'data.db not found'` collapses every failure mode (disk full, permission denied, I/O error) into the single misleading message 'data.db not found, skipping backup', and because maybe_backup_remote_db always `return`s success, the deploy proceeds to run destructive migrations (035 DROP TABLE) with no valid backup. This directly undermines the stated guarantee 'a botched migration can be reverted by hand' (deploy.sh:122).
fix: Before copying, run `sqlite3 ${DB} 'PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE);'` (or copy data.db plus -wal/-shm), mirroring switch.sh/start.sh. Distinguish 'file absent' from 'copy failed': test `[ -f data.db ]` first, and on a real cp failure abort the deploy (return non-zero) instead of printing a benign-sounding warning and continuing into destructive migrations.

title: stamp-migrations version-to-name map is misaligned, so it marks the wrong (and unapplied) migrations as applied
detail: stamp-migrations.mjs hardcodes a list mapping versions to names and inserts them into schema_migrations with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. The names are wrong: it maps '047' -> 'lock_db_mode', but the real migration is migrations/047_nsfw_reviewed_tracking.ts (verified on disk and via its exported migrate047NsfwReviewedTracking). There is no 047_lock_db_mode file at all. The list is effectively shifted/invented relative to the actual migrations directory. Because the migration runner (migrate.ts:253) decides what to skip purely by `version` membership in schema_migrations, stamping version '047' makes the runner skip the real 047 migration forever, even though its column changes (nsfw_flags.reviewed_by/reviewed_at) were never applied. The stored `name` being wrong also corrupts the audit trail. The same shift affects other entries (the names do not line up with the on-disk NNN_*.ts files). This is a footgun script that, if run on a fresh or partially-migrated DB, silently desyncs tracking from reality.
fix: Generate the version/name pairs by scanning the migrations/ directory (same regex as migrate.ts: /^(\d{3})_(.+)\.ts$/) instead of a hand-maintained literal list, or delete the script. If a stamping tool must exist, have it import the scan from migrate.ts so it can never drift from the real filenames.

title: run-migration-046 tracks via a different table (migration_log) than the canonical runner (schema_migrations)
detail: run-migration-046.mjs records its completion into a `migration_log` table (lines 24-27), but the canonical runner migrate.ts and migrations/lib/helpers.ts track exclusively in `schema_migrations` (migrate.ts uses schema_migrations 8x, migration_log 0x; migration 046 itself is 046_extend_user_cache_profile.ts and calls recordMigration into schema_migrations). Consequences: (a) running this ad-hoc script does NOT mark 046 as applied in schema_migrations, so the next `./deploy.sh` will re-run migration 046 via migrate.ts; (b) it ALSO opens the DB with `new Database(dbPath)` defaulting fileMustExist:false and DB_PATH defaulting to './data/data.db' relative to cwd, so if invoked from the wrong directory it creates an empty DB and ALTERs a non-existent user_cache; (c) the `SELECT id FROM migration_log` will throw if migration_log does not exist on a given box, since nothing in the canonical schema creates it. The additive ALTERs are individually guarded by a column-existence check so re-running 046 via migrate.ts won't duplicate columns, which is the only reason this is medium and not high, but the dual-table tracking is a real inconsistency that breaks the 'applied versions' contract the whole deploy relies on.
fix: Delete run-migration-046.mjs (migration 046 is already covered by migrations/046_extend_user_cache_profile.ts run through migrate.ts). If kept for emergencies, have it write to schema_migrations via the same recordMigration helper, require fileMustExist:true, and resolve DB_PATH the same way migrate.ts does.

lines: 18 (invoked by deploy.sh:435; tsx classified dev-only in package.json:90 / package-lock.json:7944)
title: Prod migration step runs `npx tsx`, auto-downloading an unpinned build tool against the live DB
detail: deploy.sh:435 runs `node scripts/migrate-remote.js` on the production host (via ssh_remote), and migrate-remote.js:18 does `spawnSync('npx', ['tsx', 'scripts/migrate.ts', ...], { shell: true })`. tsx is a devDependency (package.json:90; package-lock.json:7940-7944 has `"dev": true`), so the prod install via `npm ci --omit=dev` (deploy.sh:341/421/428) excludes it from node_modules. When `npx tsx` runs and tsx is not locally installed, npx fetches it from the registry on demand. The deploy ssh invocation is non-interactive (no TTY), so npx skips its 'Ok to proceed?' prompt and installs automatically. Net effect: every production migration downloads tsx (and its transitive deps) fresh from npm at an unpinned latest-matching version and executes it with full access to the production SQLite database. A compromised tsx release (or a registry MITM) would run arbitrary code on the DB host during migration. This is distinct from CI, where `npx tsx` (ci.yml:54) runs only after `npm ci` has already installed tsx locally.
fix: Make tsx available deterministically on prod for the migration path: either move tsx to dependencies, or compile the migration runner to plain JS in `dist` and invoke `node dist/.../migrate.js` so no runtime TypeScript loader is needed, or pin the exact tsx version with `npx -p tsx@<pinned> tsx ...` after verifying it is installed from the lockfile. Avoid bare `npx <tool>` on the production host.

title: Alternate `--fresh` deploy path runs `npm ci` (with devDependencies) on the production host
detail: The hardened canonical deploy (deploy.sh:341, 421, 428) correctly installs prod deps with `npm ci --omit=dev`. But the alternate remote-fresh deploy paths in scripts/start.sh:700 (`ssh ... 'cd ${REMOTE_PATH} && tar -xzf deploy.tar.gz && npm ci'`) and scripts/start.cmd:656 (identical) run plain `npm ci`, which installs the FULL devDependency tree on prod: eslint, @typescript-eslint/*, vitest, @vitest/*, tsup, tsx, prettier, @anthropic-ai/sdk, pino-pretty, etc. (package.json:76-93). Every one of those plus their transitive deps gets installed and may execute install lifecycle scripts on the production host, substantially enlarging the supply-chain attack surface for no runtime benefit (the bot runs from prebuilt dist/ via ecosystem.config.cjs and does not need the dev toolchain). The inconsistency also means dependency provisioning differs depending on which deploy entrypoint the operator uses.
fix: Change both start.sh:700 and start.cmd:656 to `npm ci --omit=dev` to match deploy.sh, or deprecate these legacy fresh-deploy paths in favor of the hardened deploy.sh so there is a single, consistent install command on prod.

title: `--limit` with a missing value yields NaN and the per-run limit is silently ignored
detail: `const LIMIT = limitArg >= 0 ? parseInt(args[limitArg + 1], 10) : Infinity;` When `--limit` is passed as the final argument with no following value, `args[limitArg+1]` is undefined and `parseInt(undefined,10)` is NaN. Later `if (runAdded >= LIMIT)` (line 153) is `runAdded >= NaN`, which is always false, so the intended smoke-test cap never triggers and the script pages the entire #general history instead of stopping. Not data-corrupting (INSERT OR IGNORE), but defeats the documented `--limit 500` smoke-test mode and can run far longer / hit far more Discord API than the operator intended.
fix: Validate the parsed value: `const n = parseInt(args[limitArg+1], 10); const LIMIT = Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 ? n : Infinity;` and error out (or warn) if `--limit` is present but the value is missing/NaN.

title: `--batch` with a missing/non-numeric value produces NaN and the LIMIT bind throws a datatype-mismatch
detail: `const MAX_BATCH = batchArg >= 0 ? parseInt(args[batchArg + 1], 10) : 5000;` If `--batch` is supplied without a following numeric value, `MAX_BATCH` becomes NaN, which is then bound as the `LIMIT ?` parameter at line 37. better-sqlite3 rejects NaN as an integer parameter with `SQLITE_MISMATCH: datatype mismatch`, so the cron-run aborts with an unhandled exception before doing any work. Fails safe (no corruption) but the scheduled context materialization silently stops making progress until someone notices the crashing cron job.
fix: Guard the parse: `const n = parseInt(args[batchArg+1], 10); const MAX_BATCH = Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 ? n : 5000;`

title: Unguarded .get().sql throws opaque TypeError when source table is absent
detail: Line 13 does src.prepare(`SELECT sql ... name='general_messages_embed'`).get().sql. If the table does not exist in the source DB, .get() returns undefined and .sql throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading sql)' with no context. The sibling export-processed.mjs handles this gracefully with `?.sql` + a 'skip (not found)' message (lines 29-30). export-score.mjs and export-substantiveness.mjs share the identical defect on their line 13. Impact is limited to operator confusion on a misconfigured/empty snapshot DB; data is not corrupted.
fix: Use optional chaining and a clear error/skip: `const row = src.prepare(...).get(); if (!row?.sql) { console.error('table general_messages_embed not found in', SRC); process.exit(1); } dst.exec(row.sql);` — matching export-processed.mjs.

title: Unguarded .get().sql throws opaque TypeError when general_messages_score is absent
detail: Same defect as export-embed.mjs line 13: `src.prepare(...).get().sql` dereferences undefined and throws an opaque TypeError if the source table is missing, instead of a clear message. Trusted-local-data tool, so impact is operator confusion only.
fix: Guard with `const row = ...get(); if (!row?.sql) { ...exit with message... }` before dst.exec.

title: Unguarded .get().sql throws opaque TypeError when general_messages_substantiveness is absent
detail: Same defect as export-embed.mjs/export-score.mjs line 13: `src.prepare(...).get().sql` will throw an opaque TypeError if the table is missing rather than reporting it. Trusted-local-data tool; impact is operator confusion only.
fix: Guard the result with optional chaining and exit with a descriptive message before dst.exec.

title: Non-idempotent insert with fixed audit_run_id double-counts on re-run
detail: auditRunId is the hardcoded constant "audit-20260112-manual" (line 7). Each finding is written via insertFinding(...) which runs a plain INSERT into audit_findings; that table (migrations/043_audit_findings.ts) has only an AUTOINCREMENT primary key and NO unique constraint on (audit_run_id, command_name, subcommand). Re-running the script therefore inserts a second full copy of every finding under the same run id. generateReportData() then aggregates by audit_run_id, so totalCommands, passCount, skipCount, etc. (and the generated markdown report) silently double (or triple) for that run. The script also has no pre-delete of the existing run. Impact is limited because this is a manual one-shot script, not a runtime path.
fix: Before inserting, delete existing rows for the run (DELETE FROM audit_findings WHERE audit_run_id = ?) inside a transaction, or add a UNIQUE(audit_run_id, command_name, subcommand) index and use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE. At minimum, derive auditRunId from a timestamp at runtime so each run is distinct.

title: Health-check timeout timer is never cleared and not unref'd, keeping a 5s timer + closure alive after every /health
detail: timeoutPromise creates setTimeout(...HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS=5000) but the handle is never stored or cleared. In the normal fast path healthCheckPromise wins Promise.race, yet the 5s timer keeps running to completion on every single /health invocation, holding the reject closure (and the rejected Error it constructs) alive. Unlike armWatchdog in cmdWrap.ts (which calls timer.unref()), this timer is not unref'd, so it can also delay graceful process shutdown by up to 5s. It is not a correctness bug in the happy path (the late rejection is still consumed by Promise.race so no unhandled rejection), but it is an avoidable per-call resource/lifecycle leak in a command anyone can spam.
fix: Capture the handle and clear it in a finally: `let t: NodeJS.Timeout; const timeoutPromise = new Promise<never>((_, reject) => { t = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error('Health check timeout')), HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS); }); try { await Promise.race([...]); } finally { clearTimeout(t!); }` and/or call t.unref().

title: review_action meta 'via' mislabels the @user-mention path as 'code'
detail: updateReviewActionMeta is called with via: uidRaw ? "uid" : "code". There are three identifier inputs: app (short code), user (@mention), and uid. When a moderator approves via the `user` mention option, uidRaw is null so via is recorded as "code", even though no short code was used. This corrupts the analytics the comment at lines 329-330 explicitly says this field exists for ('track whether mods prefer short codes or user IDs'). Same pattern in reject.ts.
fix: Derive via from which option was actually provided, e.g. const via = codeRaw ? 'code' : userOption ? 'mention' : 'uid'; and pass that. Apply identically in reject.ts.

title: review_action meta 'via' mislabels the @user-mention path as 'code' (reject)
detail: Both updateReviewActionMeta calls in executeReject use via: uidRaw ? "uid" : "code". The `user` (@mention) lookup path leaves uidRaw null, so a mention-based rejection is logged as via='code'. Inaccurate audit/analytics metadata for how the action was initiated.
fix: Compute via from the actually-provided option: codeRaw ? 'code' : userOption ? 'mention' : 'uid', and use it in both the success and fetch-failure meta updates.

title: Search-session storage is written every search but never read
detail: storeSearchSession (line 359) is called on every search (index.ts:267) and generateNonce (line 352) mints a nonce embedded into the select-menu custom ID (components.ts:260). However getSearchSession (line 373) is never called anywhere in production code (only in tests/graphify artifacts). The search select-menu handler (index.ts:403-413) ignores the nonce/session entirely and simply acts on interaction.values[0]. The entire SEARCH_SESSIONS LRUCache, the nonce generation, and storeSearchSession are therefore dead weight — allocating crypto randomBytes and cache entries on every search for data that is never consumed.
fix: Either remove SEARCH_SESSIONS/generateNonce/storeSearchSession/getSearchSession (and simplify buildSearchComponents to not need a nonce), or actually use getSearchSession in handleHelpSelectMenu to validate/restore the search context. Pick one; right now it's wasted work and misleading API surface.

title: Permission-filtered command list is cached without keying on member-fetch success/roles, so a transient member fetch failure pins a user to 'public-only' help for up to 5 minutes
detail: filterCommandsByPermission caches the filtered result under key `${guildId}:${userId}` only. The actual permission computation depends on the `member` argument (its roles), which is NOT part of the cache key. In both callers (autocomplete.ts:50-60 and index.ts:88-94 / handleHelpButton index.ts:316-323 / handleHelpSelectMenu index.ts:394-401 / handleHelpModal index.ts:458-465) the GuildMember is fetched with `.catch(() => null)`. If that fetch transiently fails, `member` is null, and for any non-owner hasPermissionLevel() returns true only for 'public' commands. That degraded public-only list is then written to PERMISSION_CACHE (line 283). For the next 5 minutes (TTL) the same staff/reviewer/admin user is served the public-only list from cache even when subsequent fetches succeed, because the cache hit (line 267-273) short-circuits before member is consulted. Net effect: staff intermittently see /help and /help autocomplete with only public commands. Self-heals after TTL. Display-only (does not affect command execution, which is independently gated), hence low severity.
fix: Either (a) skip caching when `member` is null (the unreliable case), e.g. `if (member || isOwner(userId)) PERMISSION_CACHE.set(...)`, or (b) incorporate a role fingerprint into the cache key (e.g. a hash of sorted role IDs) so a different role set / null-member computes a distinct entry. Option (a) is the minimal fix.

title: invalidatePermissionCache is never called from production code, so the documented 'call this when roles change' contract is unmet and stale help lists persist for the full TTL
detail: invalidatePermissionCache() is exported and unit-tested, and the comment at cache.ts:206-207 explicitly states it must be called when a user's roles change to avoid serving a stale command list. A repo-wide search shows it is referenced only by its own definition/comment and the test file — never by any role-change path (no guildMemberUpdate handler, role automation, or config update calls it). Combined with the cache-key issue above, any role change (e.g., a user promoted to reviewer) is not reflected in /help for up to 5 minutes. Impact is limited to help-display accuracy, so low severity, but the function is effectively dead and the invariant it guards is not enforced.
fix: Call invalidatePermissionCache(guildId, userId) from the member/role update path (e.g., guildMemberUpdate when roles change) and from config changes that affect mod_role_ids/reviewer_role_id, or document that staleness up to CACHE_TTL_MS is accepted and remove the misleading 'call this' comment.

title: searchCommands scoring compares the full multi-word query against single command names, so every multi-term search collapses to the lowest 'description' score
detail: After AND-matching individual terms, the scoring block sets `queryLower = query.toLowerCase()` (the entire raw query, line 156) and compares it with `lowerName === queryLower`, `lowerName.startsWith(queryLower)`, `lowerName.includes(queryLower)`, alias includes, etc. For any multi-word query (e.g., 'role config'), no single command name/alias contains the full multi-word string, so all branches fail and every result is scored 50 / matchedOn='description' (lines 181-184). The subsequent sort (line 190-193) then degenerates to pure alphabetical order, defeating relevance ranking for multi-term searches. Single-word searches are unaffected. Impact is degraded result ordering only, not wrong results, so low severity.
fix: Score against individual terms rather than the whole query — e.g., compute the best per-term match (max over terms of name-exact/startsWith/includes) instead of using the full `query` string, or score using the first term and use the rest only for filtering.

title: handleHelpButton switch has no case for the 'search' navigation type and no button ever emits a search nonce id, leaving both the parse branch and a switch path dead
detail: parseHelpCustomId can return { type: 'search', nonce } for ids matching /^help:search:([a-f0-9]+)$/ (metadata.ts:257-264), but buildHelpCustomId({ type:'search' }) is never called anywhere in src (only the type union and the builder case exist). Search results are navigated via the select menu id `help:select:search:${nonce}` (components.ts:260), which is routed to handleHelpSelectMenu, not through a button. Consequently: (1) no button ever produces `help:search:<nonce>`, and (2) even if one did, handleHelpButton's switch (lines 326-343) has cases only for overview/category/command/search_modal, so 'search' would hit `default` and reply 'Unknown navigation'. This is dead/unreachable code rather than a live bug; flagged for cleanup and to document the gap should a future change start emitting search-nonce buttons.
fix: Either remove the unused 'search' member from HelpNavigation + its builder/parser branches, or add a `case 'search':` that loads the session via getSearchSession(nav.nonce) and re-renders results, if button-based search navigation is intended.

title: Any gatekeeper can flush/close a batch session owned by a different gatekeeper via the send branch
detail: The toggle 'send and close' branch is entered solely when isMemberBuffered(guild.id, target.id) is true (line 118), with no check that the current user opened the session. addMember (the add branch) explicitly guards against cross-opener interference and returns 'denied_other_opener' (welcomeBatch.ts line 204-205), but flushSession has no such owner check. So if gatekeeper A opens a batch and queues user X, gatekeeper B right-clicking the buffered user X will flush and close A's in-progress session prematurely. This is an asymmetric authorization inconsistency: B is blocked from adding to A's session but allowed to send/close it. Impact is limited because all actors are trusted gatekeepers, but it can cause A's batch to be sent before A finished queueing.
fix: In the isMemberBuffered branch, fetch the session opener (getSessionStatus(guild.id).openedBy) and if it differs from interaction.user.id (and the user is not a bypass/owner), reply that another gatekeeper owns the session instead of flushing it.

title: Env fallback overrides a guild's explicitly-configured silent_first_msg_days when the configured value equals the default (7)
detail: getFlaggerConfig uses `silentDays === 7` as a sentinel meaning "DB had no value" (lines 166-169). But 7 is also a fully valid value a guild can persist: setSilentFirstMsgDays accepts the range 7-365 (line 236), so a guild can explicitly set 7. When such a guild exists AND process.env.SILENT_FIRST_MSG_DAYS is set to a different number (e.g. 30), the DB-provided 7 is silently clobbered by the env value, ignoring the guild's explicit configuration. The comment on lines 162-163 even acknowledges the fragility. Trigger is narrow (guild explicitly set the boundary value 7 while a differing env default is present), hence low severity, but the resolution logic is genuinely incorrect.
fix: Track whether the DB actually supplied a value with a separate boolean (e.g. `let dbHadDays = false;` set inside the `row.silent_first_msg_days !== null` branch) and only apply the env fallback when `!dbHadDays`, instead of overloading the magic number 7.

title: listCandidates maps foreign_key_violations from the row_count column
detail: When building a BackupCandidate from persisted metadata, `foreign_key_violations: existingMeta?.row_count` reads the wrong column (row_count) — a copy-paste error. The db_backups table (migrations/012:52-62) has no foreign-key-violation column at all, and validateCandidate persists only row_count (the summed row total). Consequently any UI/embed that shows cached FK violations for a not-yet-revalidated candidate will display the total row count as the FK-violation count, which is misleading (e.g., a healthy backup appears to have thousands of FK violations).
fix: Set `foreign_key_violations: undefined` here (it is not persisted), or add a dedicated `foreign_key_violations` column to db_backups and persist/read it. Do not alias it to row_count.

title: 7-day reopen window miscomputed due to UTC-vs-local Date parsing of closed_at
detail: closeTicket() (src/features/modmail/tickets.ts:165) writes closed_at via SQLite datetime('now'), which produces a space-separated UTC string with NO timezone marker, e.g. "2026-05-31 12:00:00". At threadReopen.ts:73 this is parsed with `new Date(ticket.closed_at).getTime()`. Per ECMAScript, a date-time string that uses a space separator and omits a timezone offset is treated as LOCAL time by V8/Node, not UTC. So the computed `closedAt` epoch is shifted by the host's UTC offset (e.g. +7h on a UTC-7 server, making the ticket look ~7h newer; -offset on UTC+ servers, making it look older). The `now - closedAt > sevenDays` boundary at line 77 is therefore wrong by the server's UTC offset, so tickets near the 7-day edge are routed down the wrong branch: some get a brand-new thread when they should reopen the old one, and others reopen an old (possibly already-archived/locked) thread when they should start fresh. The unit tests in tests/features/modmail/threadReopen.test.ts pass only because they feed closed_at via Date.toISOString() (with a 'Z'), which IS parsed as UTC — masking the production format mismatch. The same bug exists in src/features/modmail/dashboardBridge.ts:304 (dashboardReopenThread) and the modstats calc in context/06 docs, so behavior is inconsistent across entry points.
fix: Parse the stored value as UTC explicitly. Either store an epoch (strftime('%s','now')) and read it as a number, or normalize before parsing: replace the space with 'T' and append 'Z' (e.g. `new Date(ticket.closed_at.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z')`), or route through the existing normalizeTimestamp helper used in web/src/lib/server/queries/modmail.ts. Apply the same fix in dashboardBridge.ts:304 and update the tests to use the SQLite datetime format ('YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS') so they actually exercise the production path.

title: Non-null assertion on a possibly-undefined Guild passed to logActionPretty (guild!) drops the audit-log entry when the guild is uncached
detail: guild is obtained via interaction.client.guilds.cache.get(session.guildId) (line 534), typed Guild | undefined, and the `if (guild)` block (535-538) explicitly handles the undefined case for member fetch. But at line 565 logActionPretty(guild!, ...) uses a non-null assertion. logActionPretty immediately dereferences guild.id synchronously (src/logging/pretty.ts:488) with no undefined guard. If the guild is not in cache at submit time (sharding eviction, large-guild lazy cache), guild is undefined and logActionPretty rejects with TypeError. It is an async function so the throw becomes a rejected promise caught by the `.catch()` at line 571 — so no crash, but the gate_submit audit-log row is silently never written and only a warn is logged. The `!` hides a genuinely possible undefined.
fix: Guard before logging: `if (guild) { await logActionPretty(guild, {...}).catch(...); }` (you already fetched/checked guild above), or change logActionPretty to accept Guild | undefined and no-op when absent. Do not use `!` here.

title: closed_at parsed as local time but stored as UTC, skewing the 7-day reopen window
detail: closeTicket writes `closed_at = datetime('now')` (tickets.ts:164-166), which SQLite stores as a space-separated UTC string like '2026-05-31 12:34:56' (TEXT column, src/db/db.ts:186-187). reopenModmailThread computes `const closedAt = new Date(ticket.closed_at).getTime()` (line 73). Per the ES spec, the date+time space-separated form (no 'T', no 'Z') is parsed as LOCAL time by V8, not UTC (verified: new Date('2026-05-31 12:34:56') yields a local-time instant, off by the host UTC offset). So closedAt is shifted by the server's UTC offset (e.g. several hours), making the `now - closedAt > sevenDays` boundary (lines 75-77) decide reopen-vs-new-thread incorrectly near the 7-day edge. Low impact (hours of skew on a 7-day window) but a real correctness defect.
fix: Parse explicitly as UTC: `new Date(ticket.closed_at.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z').getTime()`, or store/compare epoch seconds consistently. Best: use a shared dt helper that knows the SQLite storage format.

title: Modmail close transcript buffer leaks in memory when no log channel is configured
detail: closeModmailThread relies entirely on flushTranscript to clear the per-ticket in-memory transcript buffer. flushTranscript only deletes transcriptBuffers entries on its success paths (transcript.ts:203 and 262). When `modmail_log_channel_id` is not configured it returns early at transcript.ts:119-122 WITHOUT deleting the buffer, and the exception path (transcript.ts:265-283) also never deletes it. closeModmailThread never calls the exported clearTranscriptBuffer as a safety net (grep shows it is only re-exported, never invoked in the close flow). Result: on every modmail close in a guild with no log channel set, the ticket's transcript lines remain in the module-level transcriptBuffers Map forever, growing unbounded with message volume. Same gap applies to closeModmailForApplication (lines 505-511).
fix: After flushTranscript returns (regardless of outcome), call clearTranscriptBuffer(ticketId) in both closeModmailThread and closeModmailForApplication; or have flushTranscript delete the buffer in a finally block / on the no-log-channel early return.

title: Dead defensive check: closeModmailForApplication tests status!=='open' on a query that already filters status='open'
detail: getOpenTicketByUser only returns rows WHERE status='open' (tickets.ts:59-77), so `if (!ticket || ticket.status !== 'open')` at lines 457-460 can only ever be true via the `!ticket` branch; the status comparison is unreachable. Harmless, but it implies a guard that does not actually exist (it will not catch a 'closed' ticket because such a ticket is never returned here).
fix: Drop the redundant status comparison, or fetch via a status-agnostic lookup (getTicketById/getTicketByThread) if the intent is genuinely to re-check status.

title: Garbled user-facing message for INVALID_STATUS claim errors (esp. panic mode)
detail: For err.code === 'INVALID_STATUS' the handler builds the message via err.message.split(' ')[2] to extract the status word. claimTx throws INVALID_STATUS in two cases: (1) terminal status, message 'Application already <status>' -> split[2] = '<status>' (works); (2) panic mode (src/features/reviewActions.ts:60-62), message 'Panic mode is active. All review operations are suspended.' -> split(' ')[2] = 'is'. So when a guild is in panic mode and a moderator clicks Claim, they see 'Cannot claim: application is already **is**.' instead of the panic-mode notice. This is misleading exactly during an emergency lockdown. The technique (parsing a human-readable Error.message by word index) is also brittle to any future wording change.
fix: Carry structured data on ClaimError (e.g., a `status` field or a distinct PANIC code) and branch on that instead of string-splitting the message. At minimum, special-case the panic-mode message (or add a PANIC ClaimError code) so the reply reads 'Panic mode is active; review operations are suspended.'

title: close() writes the permanent archive BEFORE applying the closed state, so the archive records the ticket as still open
detail: In close(), writeArchive(ticket) is awaited at line 465 using the in-memory ticket object fetched by findById (status='open', closedAt=null, closeReason=null). Only afterward (line 466) does getSetClosedStmt() flip status to 'closed' and set closed_at/close_reason. writeArchive serializes that stale ticket object into the JSON payload (service.ts:560-568 `payload.ticket = ticket`). The archive file — the long-term auditable record the module exists to produce — therefore says status:'open', closedAt:null, closeReason:null for a ticket that is being closed.
