The 'closed' and 'archived' events are captured, but the embedded ticket snapshot is wrong.
fix: Run getSetClosedStmt() first, then re-read the row (or mutate the local object's status/closedAt/closeReason/closedByUserId) and pass the closed snapshot to writeArchive, so the archived ticket reflects its terminal state.

title: getClaim returns an object typed as ReviewClaimRow but missing the app_id field
detail: This getClaim SELECTs only `reviewer_id, claimed_at` yet casts the result to ReviewClaimRow, whose type declares a non-optional `app_id: string` (types.ts:63-67). At runtime app_id is undefined while the type says it is present — an unsound cast. The sibling implementation in reviewActions.ts:209 correctly selects app_id, reviewer_id, claimed_at, so the two getClaim functions diverge. Current consumers (claimGuard, card.ts) only read reviewer_id/claimed_at, so no crash today, but any future code that trusts the type and reads claim.app_id from this path will get undefined silently.
fix: Add app_id to the SELECT here (SELECT app_id, reviewer_id, claimed_at ...) to match the declared type and the reviewActions.ts implementation, or narrow the return type to Pick<ReviewClaimRow,'reviewer_id'|'claimed_at'>.

title: Initial-check setTimeout is neither captured, cleared on stop, nor unref'd
detail: startDiskSpaceScheduler schedules the first disk check with `setTimeout(async () => {...}, 15000)` but does not store the returned handle. Only the periodic `setInterval` handle is saved to `_activeInterval` and unref'd. Consequences: (1) `stopDiskSpaceScheduler()` cannot cancel this pending timer, so if the bot starts and is asked to shut down within 15s, `checkDiskSpace` still fires after stop was called (touching `client.guilds.cache`, sending an embed) during teardown; (2) unlike the `setInterval`, this timeout is not `.unref()`'d, so for up to 15s it can keep the Node event loop alive and delay a clean process exit. Compare with badgeRefreshScheduler.ts which captures and unref's its startupTimer.
fix: Capture the timeout handle (e.g. a module-level `_startupTimeout`), call `.unref?.()` on it, and clear it in `stopDiskSpaceScheduler()` alongside `_activeInterval`.

title: Scheduler-health assertions are guarded by `if (schedulersField)`, so the test passes vacuously if the field disappears
detail: The test 'shows scheduler status when schedulers are tracked' mocks getSchedulerHealth() to return a 2-entry Map, then locates the embed field named 'Schedulers' and only runs its expect() calls inside `if (schedulersField) { ... }`. If a regression in src/commands/health.ts caused the Schedulers field to stop being emitted (e.g., the `if (schedulerHealthMap.size > 0)` block were removed or the field renamed), `schedulersField` would be undefined, the if-block would be skipped, and the test would still report PASS with zero assertions executed. The test therefore does not actually protect the behavior it is named for. (It happens to run the assertions today only because the current implementation does emit the field.)
fix: Assert the field exists before inspecting it: `expect(schedulersField).toBeDefined();` then drop the `if` guard and assert `schedulersField.value` contains 'modMetrics' and 'opsHealth' unconditionally. Optionally also assert the WARN/failure formatting for the opsHealth entry (consecutiveFailures: 2).

title: Subcommand-routing tests assert only the outer `route_subcommand` step, which fires for every subcommand — the assertion is tautological
detail: execute() in src/commands/gate/gateMain.ts wraps the entire switch in `withStep(ctx, 'route_subcommand', ...)`, so ctx.step is called with 'route_subcommand' for EVERY subcommand and group. The test 'routes to welcome preview subcommand' (and the comment claims it verifies welcome-preview routing) asserts `expect(ctx.step).toHaveBeenCalledWith('route_subcommand')`, which would pass for setup, reset, status, set-questions, or any other branch — it does not verify that the preview path specifically ran. It provides no protection against the preview branch being mis-wired. (Contrast with the status/config tests at 211-225, which assert branch-specific steps like 'query_stats'/'load_config' and are meaningful.)
fix: Assert a step or side-effect unique to executeWelcomePreview, e.g. spy on renderWelcomeTemplate and `expect(renderWelcomeTemplate).toHaveBeenCalled()`, or assert a preview-specific withStep phase ('render_preview').

title: claimedAtToDate/claimedAtToEpoch mis-parse the actual stored claimed_at format (epoch-seconds string) -> Invalid Date / NaN
detail: These helpers do `new Date(claimed_at)` and `new Date(claimed_at).getTime()/1000`, and their JSDoc/param type declare claimed_at as an "ISO timestamp string". But the value is never ISO: review_claim.claimed_at is a TEXT column (src/db/db.ts:132) and claimTx (src/features/reviewActions.ts:114) inserts nowUtc(), which returns epoch SECONDS as a number (src/lib/time.ts:34 `Math.floor(Date.now()/1000)`). SQLite stores that as a numeric string like "1748600000". `new Date("1748600000")` yields Invalid Date, so claimedAtToDate returns Invalid Date and claimedAtToEpoch returns NaN. The real card consumer sidesteps them with a custom parser (src/ui/reviewCard.ts parseClaimedAt, which explicitly notes the DB "may contain numeric strings from nowUtc()"). A grep shows claimedAtToEpoch/claimedAtToDate are defined but never called anywhere in src/tests/web, so today this is dead code -- but it is a latent trap: any future caller trusting the JSDoc ("ISO timestamp string") will silently get NaN/Invalid Date for every claim.
fix: Make the helpers tolerant of epoch-seconds numeric strings (and epoch ms), e.g. detect an all-digit string and treat it as seconds: `const n = Number(claimed_at); const ms = Number.isFinite(n) ? (n < 1e12 ? n*1000 : n) : Date.parse(claimed_at); return new Date(ms);`. Alternatively delete the unused helpers and standardize on parseClaimedAt. Also correct the ReviewClaimRow.claimed_at type/comment which claims ISO but is actually an epoch-seconds string.

title: Panic-mode claim error mis-parses ClaimError message, showing "application is already **is**"
detail: For an INVALID_STATUS ClaimError the handler builds the user message via `err.message.split(" ")[2]`. This assumes the message is exactly `Application already <status>` (reviewActions.ts:82), where token[2] is the status -> correct for terminal states. But claimTx ALSO throws INVALID_STATUS for panic mode with message "Panic mode is active. All review operations are suspended." (reviewActions.ts:62). split(" ")[2] of that is "is", so a moderator clicking Claim while panic mode is active sees: "Cannot claim: application is already **is**." -- nonsensical and hides the real (panic) reason. It also needlessly calls ensureReviewMessage to "refresh" for a non-status condition.
fix: Stop string-slicing err.message. Either add a dedicated error code for panic mode (e.g. PANIC_MODE) or pass the status in a structured field on ClaimError and branch on it. At minimum, special-case the panic message text before the generic INVALID_STATUS branch.

title: Cleanup setInterval is never unref'd or cleared — keeps the event loop alive (hangs tests/shutdown)
detail: At module load, rateLimiter.ts calls `setInterval(cleanupOldCooldowns, CLEANUP_INTERVAL_MS)` (10 min) and never calls `.unref()` on the returned timer, nor stores it for clearing, nor guards on a test env. By contrast, cmdWrap.ts (armWatchdog, line ~192) correctly does `timer.unref()`. A live, ref'd interval keeps the Node process alive. This is exercised by my bucket: tests/commands/listopen.test.ts imports src/commands/listopen.js, which imports rateLimiter (`checkCooldown`, `clearCooldown`, `COOLDOWNS`). The module's own comment even admits this: 'This interval is never cleared, so this module can't be cleanly unloaded ... If tests start hanging, this is why.' Impact: vitest workers may not exit cleanly (forces teardown timeout / --forceExit reliance), and in production it blocks graceful shutdown.
fix: Capture the handle and unref it, mirroring cmdWrap.ts: `const t = setInterval(cleanupOldCooldowns, CLEANUP_INTERVAL_MS); if (typeof t.unref === 'function') t.unref();`. Optionally export a `stopCleanup()` that clears it for deterministic test teardown.

title: 7-day reopen window parses SQLite UTC timestamp as local time
detail: closed_at is written by closeTicket() in tickets.ts via SQLite datetime('now'), which yields a space-separated UTC string like "2026-05-31 12:34:56" with no timezone marker (confirmed: db.ts line 187 `closed_at TEXT`, and closeTicket uses `datetime('now')`). At threadReopen.ts:73 this is parsed with `new Date(ticket.closed_at).getTime()`. Node/V8 parses non-ISO, space-separated datetime strings as LOCAL time, not UTC. The comparison `now - closedAt > sevenDays` (lines 74-77) is therefore skewed by the host's UTC offset. On a server several hours behind UTC, a freshly-closed ticket can compute a NEGATIVE elapsed time (closedAt appears in the future) and on a server ahead of UTC the window is shortened. Impact: the boundary between 'reopen in place' and 'create a brand-new thread' (lines 78-85) is off by the offset, so tickets near the 7-day edge are mis-routed. Not exploitable, but a genuine boundary/timezone bug.
fix: Parse as UTC explicitly. Either store/read epoch seconds, or normalize: `const closedAt = ticket.closed_at ? new Date(ticket.closed_at.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z').getTime() : 0;`. Best: make SQLite emit ISO-Z (e.g. strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ','now')) or unixepoch() and parse consistently.

title: Unreachable null branch in lensUrl ternary
detail: avatarUrl is set from user.displayAvatarURL({ size: 128 }) (line 364), which always returns a non-empty CDN URL string, never null/empty. The ternary at lines 369-371 (`avatarUrl ? ... : null`) therefore always takes the truthy branch; the `: null` and the later `if (lensUrl)` guard (line 389) are effectively dead. No runtime impact, but misleading defensive code.
fix: Drop the ternary and unconditionally build lensUrl from the encoded avatarUrl, or remove the dead null branch/guard.

title: Default mockAll return value is unreachable; per-action count assertions are vacuous
detail: The default mock is `mockAll.mockImplementation((query) => { if (typeof query === "string") return []; return [{action:"approve",cnt:80},{action:"reject",cnt:15},{action:"kick",cnt:5}]; })`. The intent is that the per-action counts query returns the approve/reject/kick array. But in the source (src/commands/stats/history.ts lines 111-118) the counts query is built as `db.prepare(SQL).all(moderator.id, guildId, fromTimestamp)` — the SQL string is the argument to db.prepare(), and the FIRST argument passed to `.all()` is always `moderator.id` (the string "mod-user-123"). The test's withSql mock passes the SQL string as `_sql` and ignores it, invoking `fn()` which calls `.all(moderator.id, ...)`. Therefore the `query` parameter the mock inspects is ALWAYS the actor-id string, so `typeof query === "string"` is ALWAYS true and the mock ALWAYS returns []. The `[{approve:80}...]` branch is dead code. Consequence: in every test using the default beforeEach (e.g. 'embed contains approvals and rejections' L347, 'embed contains reject rate' L361), `counts` is always {} and computed Approvals/Rejections/Reject-Rate values are 0/0.0. Those tests only assert the field NAMES exist (toContainEqual with name only, never value), so they pass regardless and would NOT catch a regression that mis-computes approval/rejection counts or reject rate. This is a false sense of coverage on the command's core numeric output.
fix: Make the mock branch on the SQL text rather than the bound parameters, e.g. set per-call implementations via the prepared SQL: have `mockPrepare.mockImplementation((sql) => ({ get: mockGet, all: (...args) => routeBySql(sql, args) }))` and key the returned rows off `sql` (counts vs response_ms vs daily). Then add value assertions like `expect(fields.find(f=>f.name==="Approvals").value).toBe("80")` so the count math is actually exercised.

title: 'CSV contains correct header row' test asserts nothing about the header
detail: The test is named 'CSV contains correct header row' and includes the comment 'AttachmentBuilder stores the data - need to access it', but the only assertion is `expect(attachment).toBeDefined()`. It never decodes the AttachmentBuilder buffer nor checks the header string. The handler (src/commands/stats/export.ts L116) emits a specific header 'Moderator ID,Total Decisions,Approvals,...'; if that header were reordered, renamed, or dropped, this test would still pass. It provides no protection for the behavior its name claims.
fix: Read the attachment payload (e.g. `(attachment.attachment as Buffer).toString('utf-8')`) and assert it `.startsWith('Moderator ID,Total Decisions,Approvals,Rejections,Modmail,Perm Reject,Kicks,Avg Response Time (seconds),Avg Response Time (formatted)')`, plus assert a sample data row is present. Or delete the test if redundant.

title: Unused afterEach import
detail: `afterEach` is imported from vitest (L8) but never used anywhere in the file (unlike reset.test.ts which uses it for timer teardown). Harmless at runtime but indicates leftover scaffolding; under a strict noUnusedLocals/eslint config this would fail the lint/build gate.
fix: Remove `afterEach` from the import list.

title: getAvgClaimToDecision / getAvgSubmitToFirstClaim SQL is never actually exercised by any test
detail: shared.test.ts only asserts these two functions are `typeof === 'function'` (lines 145-157) and explicitly documents (lines 142-144) that they are 'tested indirectly through the command handler tests that mock the shared module'. But stats/user.test.ts ALSO mocks them (user.test.ts lines 39-41 replace them with vi.fn()). The net result is that the real bodies of getAvgClaimToDecision/getAvgSubmitToFirstClaim in src/commands/stats/shared.ts (lines 60-132) — including their multi-CTE action_log JOIN SQL and the `c.claim_time < d.decision_time` / `c.claim_time > s.submit_time` guards — are executed by zero tests. A regression in that SQL (e.g. flipping the inequality, dropping a bind param, the INNER JOIN losing rows) would pass the entire suite green. This is a real coverage blind spot on the moderator-performance metric, not a wrong assertion.
fix: Add a focused test that imports shared.ts WITHOUT mocking db (use an in-memory better-sqlite3 with a small action_log fixture, like tests/config.test.ts does) and asserts the computed averages for known claim/decision/submit timestamps, including the boundary where claim_time == decision_time (should be excluded).

title: Failure message reports un-stripped matches (includes allowed code-block mentions), confusing diagnostics
detail: The assertion correctly uses `realMatches` (mentions after fenced code blocks are stripped, lines 91-92), but the error message interpolates `matches` (line 89/95), which is computed against the FULL text including code blocks. If a file legitimately contains mention syntax inside a ``` fenced block AND also has a real violation outside it, the failure message will list the code-block mentions too, sending the developer to lines that are actually allowed. If a file's only mentions are inside code fences, realMatches is empty so the test passes (correct) — but `matches` would be non-empty, which is harmless only because the message isn't shown on pass. This is a diagnostics defect, not a guard-correctness defect.
fix: Interpolate `realMatches.join(", ")` (not `matches`) into the failure message so the reported mentions are exactly the ones that caused the failure.

title: closed_at parsed as local time instead of UTC, skewing the 7-day reopen window
detail: closeTicket() (tickets.ts:165) writes closed_at via SQLite datetime('now'), which yields a UTC string of the form 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' with NO timezone designator (the schema column is closed_at TEXT, db.ts:187). Line 73 does `new Date(ticket.closed_at).getTime()`. V8/Node parses a space-separated, zone-less datetime string as LOCAL time, not UTC. So `closedAt` is offset from the true close instant by the server's UTC offset. The 7-day boundary test on line 77 (`now - closedAt > sevenDays`) is therefore wrong by up to the host UTC offset (~14h max). On a server with a positive UTC offset this makes `now - closedAt` larger than reality, so a ticket closed at ~6.8 days can be mis-classified as >7 days and a brand-new thread is created (via openPublicModmailThreadFor) instead of reopening the existing one; on a negative-offset server the window stays open too long. This is confirmed to be an inconsistency in THIS codebase: the correct normalization pattern is used elsewhere for the same kind of SQLite timestamp (src/ui/reviewCard.ts:110 and src/features/review/card.ts:129 both do `trimmed.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z'` before new Date()). The identical raw-parse bug also exists in src/features/modmail/dashboardBridge.ts:304 (out of bucket) for the same field.
fix: Normalize the SQLite UTC string before parsing, e.g. `const iso = ticket.closed_at.includes('T') ? ticket.closed_at : ticket.closed_at.replace(' ', 'T') + 'Z'; const closedAt = ticket.closed_at ? new Date(iso).getTime() : 0;` (reuse the existing helper used by reviewCard.ts / review/card.ts). Apply the same fix at dashboardBridge.ts:304.

title: Tautological tests re-implement logic inline instead of calling the source (false confidence)
detail: Large blocks of this suite never invoke any function from src/features/modmail/threadClose.ts. The 'reason text' tests (lines 255-307) copy-paste the exact reason-selection ternary from threadClose.ts (source lines 466-473) into the test body and assert on the copy. Likewise the 'closing embed format' (lines 311-330), 'archive/delete strategies' (lines 332-351, re-implementing `cfg?.modmail_delete_on_close !== false`), 'log URL format' (lines 353-361), 'duplicate close detection' (lines 364-377), and 'ticket structure' (lines 380-408) blocks only assert against literals/inline expressions defined within the test. These tests pass unconditionally regardless of the real implementation, so if someone changes the reason wording, the embed color/title, the delete-on-close default, or the log-URL template in threadClose.ts, these tests will NOT fail. Impact: false sense of coverage for closeModmailForApplication's user-facing strings and close behavior; a real regression in those strings would ship undetected.
fix: Replace the inline-reimplemented assertions with assertions on values produced by the source. E.g. drive closeModmailForApplication() past its early-return guard with a fully mocked open ticket and assert that user.send was called with the expected embed title/description/color and reason text, rather than asserting on a locally-recomputed `text`/`description`/`color` variable.

title: mockTransaction has wrong shape vs better-sqlite3 / source usage; only unexercised because no test hits the in-7-day reopen success path
detail: The hoisted mock is `mockTransaction: vi.fn((fn) => fn())`, which immediately INVOKES the callback and returns its (undefined) result. But the real `db.transaction(fn)` (better-sqlite3, see src/db/db.ts:96-98) returns a CALLABLE wrapper, and the source uses it as `db.transaction(() => {...})()` (threadReopen.ts:89-109). With this mock, `db.transaction(fn)` returns `undefined`, and the source's trailing `()` would call `undefined()` -> TypeError. The tests pass only because NONE of them exercise the successful within-7-days reopen branch (every success test uses a ticket closed >7 days ago, which returns at threadReopen.ts:79 before reaching the transaction; the 'error handling' test makes db.transaction throw synchronously before the trailing `()`). Net effect: the core reopen transaction logic (reopenTicket + open_modmail guard re-insert + addOpenThread + thread unarchive/unlock + applicant DM) at threadReopen.ts:87-149 is entirely untested, and the mock that exists would actually break if a test were added. Contrast with the sibling threadOpen.test.ts:16 which correctly uses `(fn) => fn`.
fix: Change the mock to `mockTransaction: vi.fn((fn: Function) => fn)` (return the function, matching better-sqlite3 and threadOpen.test.ts), then add a test for the happy path: a closed ticket within 7 days that asserts reopenTicket is called, the open_modmail UPSERT runs, addOpenThread is called with the thread_id, and the success message `Modmail thread reopened: <#...>` is returned.

title: Vacuous tests assert on inline string/boolean literals instead of exercising any source code
detail: The describe blocks 'modmail thread customId format', 'modmail race condition handling', and 'primary key constraint detection' (lines 350-401) construct local literals (e.g. `const customId = ` + tts + `v1:modmail:close:${ticketId}` + tts + `` then expect it to equal `v1:modmail:close:123`; `const isRace = error.message.includes('UNIQUE') || ...`) and assert on those local expressions. They import nothing from threadOpen.ts for these cases and would still pass if the corresponding production logic (customId construction at threadOpen.ts:384, race detection at threadOpen.ts:444-448) were deleted or changed. They provide false confidence in coverage of the customId format and race-detection logic without testing it.
fix: Either remove these blocks or rewrite them to assert against the real code paths: parse a customId actually emitted by openPublicModmailThreadFor, and drive openPublicModmailThreadFor with a thrown UNIQUE/PRIMARY KEY/SQLITE_CONSTRAINT error to assert the 'already exists' / 'being created by another moderator' branches at threadOpen.ts:450-473.

title: Helper tests assert against mocks/inline literals and never invoke the functions under test
detail: The `describe`s for `isStaff`, `requireInteractionStaff`, `resolveApplication`, and all the `openRejectModal`/`openAcceptModal`/`openPermRejectModal`/`openKickModal`/`openUnclaimModal` blocks do not import or call any of those real functions (defined in src/features/review/handlers/helpers.ts). Instead they call the mocked dependencies directly (e.g. `hasRole(...)`, `findAppByShortCode(...)`, `getClaim(...)`) or assert on inline-recomputed expressions like `["rejected","approved","kicked"].includes(app.status)` and `\`v1:modal:reject:code${code}\``. These are tautologies that re-test JavaScript/Vitest, not the module. The real `openRejectModal` has non-trivial ordering (status check, claimGuard, then `safeShowModal` token-age/replied checks at helpers.ts:138-202) that is entirely unverified. Concrete impact: the suite reports green while providing no protection against regressions in staff gating or modal pre-checks.
fix: Import the real functions and exercise them with mocked discord.js interaction objects, asserting on observable effects (replyOrEdit content, whether showModal is/ isn't called, return value of requireInteractionStaff). Remove the tautological assertions or convert them into behavioral tests.

title: Modal-handler tests redefine patterns locally and never call the real handlers, providing no regression coverage
detail: Every block (`handleRejectModal`, `handleAcceptModal`, `handlePermRejectModal`, `handleKickModal`, `handleUnclaimModal`, plus the `action dispatching` block) asserts on locally-declared regexes (`MODAL_RE`, `ACCEPT_MODAL_RE`, `MODAL_PERM_REJECT_RE`, `MODAL_KICK_RE`, `MODAL_UNCLAIM_RE`) and inline string/`slice`/`trim` recomputations rather than importing and invoking the handlers in src/features/review/handlers/modals.ts. The local copies happen to match src/lib/modalPatterns.ts today (so no currently-false assertion), but if those production patterns or the handlers' parsing/dispatch (e.g. `reason = raw.trim().slice(0,500) || null`, the deferUpdate-then-resolveApplication-then-runXAction sequence) regress, none of these tests fail. The `action dispatching` cases like `expect("runRejectAction").toBe("runRejectAction")` are pure tautologies. Real risk surface (staff gate via requireInteractionStaff, deferUpdate timing, dispatch to the correct runner) is untested here.
fix: Import the handlers and the canonical patterns from the source modules; drive each handler with a mocked ModalSubmitInteraction and assert the correct runner is invoked with the trimmed/truncated reason and that non-matching customIds early-return. Delete the string-equals-itself assertions.

title: Test encodes a fabricated INVALID_STATUS string and masks a real garbled-message bug for panic mode
detail: The test 'extracts status from error message' uses errorMessage = "Cannot claim: status is approved" and asserts split(" ")[2] === "status". This is not the real message and the asserted value ("status") is meaningless. The production handler (src/features/review/handlers/claimHandlers.ts:49-50) does `msg = `Cannot claim: application is already **${err.message.split(" ")[2]}**.`` against the ClaimError thrown by claimTx. claimTx throws INVALID_STATUS in TWO shapes: (a) terminal state -> "Application already approved" where split[2] = "approved" (correct), and (b) PANIC MODE -> "Panic mode is active. All review operations are suspended." (src/features/reviewActions.ts:62) where split[2] = "is". So when a moderator clicks Claim during panic mode they get the nonsensical reply "Cannot claim: application is already **is**." instead of a panic-mode explanation. The vacuous test neither reflects the real message nor catches the panic-mode garble.
fix: In claimHandlers.ts, branch on the actual ClaimError content instead of positional word parsing: surface err.message directly for the panic case (it is already user-friendly), and only do the 'already <status>' phrasing for the terminal-state case (e.g. detect a leading 'Application already '). Then write a real test that calls handleClaimToggle with claimTx mocked to throw both ClaimError shapes and asserts the rendered reply.

title: Local BUTTON_RE copy diverges from the real BTN_DECIDE_RE, so routing-regex tests prove nothing
detail: The suite defines its own `const BUTTON_RE = /^v1:decide:(\w+):code([0-9A-F]{6})$/` and tests claim/unclaim/approve/etc. against it. The actual pattern used by handlers (src/lib/modalPatterns.ts:35, re-exported as BUTTON_RE from helpers.ts:38) is `/^(?:v1:decide|review):(approve|accept|reject|kick|claim|unclaim|wrong_password|stale_modmail):code([0-9A-F]{6})$/`. Two concrete divergences: (1) the real regex also accepts the legacy `review:` prefix, which the test's copy rejects; (2) the real regex constrains the action to a fixed allowlist whereas the test copy accepts ANY `\w+` (so `v1:decide:garbage:codeABCDEF` would 'match' in the test but not in production). The tests therefore validate a fictional regex; a change to the real allowlist or prefix handling would not be caught.
fix: Import the real BUTTON_RE/MODAL_RE/ACCEPT_MODAL_RE from src/features/review/handlers/helpers.js (or BTN_DECIDE_RE etc. from src/lib/modalPatterns.js) instead of re-declaring local literals, then run the same match assertions plus a `review:`-prefixed case and an invalid-action negative case.

title: withTimeout never clears its setTimeout, leaking a 30s timer per DM (also in kick.ts)
detail: withTimeout races the work promise against `new Promise((_,reject)=>setTimeout(...,30000))` but never captures the timer handle, so it is never cleared. When user.send() resolves first (the normal case, exercised by reject.test.ts), the 30s timer stays pending until it fires and rejects an already-settled promise (no-op). Same pattern in src/features/review/flows/kick.ts:29-36 for fetch/send/kick — up to three dangling 30s timers per kick. Production impact is modest (timers are short-lived and self-clear) but it keeps the event loop active and, under bursts of approvals/rejections, accumulates thousands of pending timers; in tests it leaves real timers alive after the test ends since the suite uses no fake timers. Grep confirmed there is no clearTimeout anywhere in src/features/review/flows.
fix: Capture the handle and clear it in a finally: `let t; const timeout = new Promise<T>((_,rej)=>{t=setTimeout(()=>rej(new Error(...)),ms);}); try { return await Promise.race([promise, timeout]); } finally { clearTimeout(t); }`. Apply in both reject.ts and kick.ts.

title: "preserves cause" test has a dead variable and does not test what its name claims
detail: The test creates `const cause = new Error("root cause")` and assigns it as `err.cause`, implying it verifies the original cause chain is preserved by classifyError. But the only assertion is `expect(result.cause).toBe(err)` — it asserts the classified error's `.cause` is the wrapped error itself, never referencing the `cause` variable. Per the source (src/lib/errors.ts:234, `cause: err instanceof Error ? err : undefined`), classifyError stores the passed-in error as `.cause` and silently discards any nested `err.cause` (the real root cause). So the `cause` local on line 237 and the assignment on line 239 are dead, and the test gives false confidence that cause-chain information survives classification when it does not. Impact: a future change that (correctly) starts unwrapping `err.cause` would not be caught here, and the misleading test name hides that root-cause data is dropped during error classification.
fix: Either rename the test to "stores the original error as cause" and remove the unused `cause` variable/assignment, or (if cause-chain preservation is actually desired) change the source to walk `err.cause` and update the assertion to `expect(result.cause).toBe(cause)`.

title: "uses default rate when not specified" test cannot detect a broken default sample rate
detail: The test deletes WIDE_EVENT_SAMPLE_RATE to exercise the DEFAULT_SAMPLE_RATE (0.1) path, but it asserts using an outcome:"error" event. In wideEventEmitter.ts shouldSample() returns true for errors/timeouts BEFORE getSampleRate() is ever consulted (lines 104-105). So logger.error is called regardless of what the default rate is. The test would still pass if DEFAULT_SAMPLE_RATE were 0, or if getSampleRate() returned garbage, or if the default-rate branch were deleted entirely. It provides false confidence that the default sampling behavior is covered. Impact: a regression that breaks default sampling of success events (the actual purpose of the default) would not be caught here.
fix: Use a success event and assert sampling behavior deterministically. Since sampling is hashTraceId(traceId) < rate, pick a traceId whose hash is below/above 0.1 and assert logger.info is/ isn't called; or stub Math via a known traceId. At minimum test a success outcome rather than an error so the default-rate code path is actually reached.

title: `expect.any(Number)` misused as a mock return value, not an assertion
detail: The test "uses current timestamp when joinedAt not provided" passes an asymmetric matcher (`expect.any(Number)`) inside `mockGet.mockReturnValueOnce({ joined_at: expect.any(Number), flagged_at: expect.any(Number), ... })`. `expect.any(...)` only has meaning inside an `expect(...).toEqual(...)`/`toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)` comparison; used as raw data it just stores a matcher object on the returned row. The test never asserts on `result` (the variable is assigned on line 245 but unused), and only checks `expect(mockRun).toHaveBeenCalled()`. So the intended verification (that `now` is used for joined_at/flagged_at when joinedAt is omitted) is not actually performed — the test would pass even if the source forwarded the wrong values. No production impact; it is a weak/ineffective test.
fix: Assert on the real call: capture `insertManualFlagStmt().run` arguments and assert `expect(mockRun).toHaveBeenCalledWith('guild-123','user-456', expect.any(Number), expect.any(Number), 'No join date', 'mod-789')`, verifying joined_at === flagged_at === a recent epoch. Remove the matcher from the mock return object.

title: createMockInteraction clobbers the enriched member/user/guild mocks with the caller's raw partial via trailing `...rest` spread
detail: The factory builds a full `user` (l274), `guild` (l275) and `member` (l276, which injects `roles`, `permissions`, `user`, `send`, `kick`, `ban`). It sets `user`/`member`/`guild` in the returned object (l280-282), but then spreads `...rest` again at l301. Because `rest` still contains the caller's original `user`/`guild`/`member` partials, those raw partials overwrite the enriched mocks. So `createMockInteraction({ member: { permissions: { has: () => true } } })` yields `interaction.member` === just `{ permissions: {...} }` — `member.roles`, `member.user`, `member.send`, etc. are now `undefined`. Note `guildId: guild.id` (l283) is computed before the clobber so it still points at the default guild id even when a custom `guild` partial without an `id` is supplied, producing an inconsistent interaction (guildId from default guild, guild object from the partial). Concrete impact: any test that overrides member/user/guild (e.g. tests/commands/stats/approvalRate.test.ts:109 `createMockInteraction({ member } as any)`) silently receives a degraded mock; code under test that reads member.roles.cache or member.user can hit undefined and either throw or take an unintended branch, making the test weaker/greener than it appears. Same pattern exists in createMockButtonInteraction (l315-339, `...overrides` at l338) and createMockModalInteraction (l353-380, `...rest` at l379).
fix: Drop user/guild/member out of the trailing spread so the enriched objects win, e.g. destructure them out: `const { user: _u, guild: _g, member: _m, ...restNoEntities } = rest;` and spread `...restNoEntities`, OR merge instead of replace: build the return object then deep-merge only the remaining keys. Apply the same fix to the button and modal factories.

title: "allows direct ID routes when enabled" test never exercises the direct-ID path it claims to cover
detail: src/web/badgeEndpoint.ts captures `ALLOW_DIRECT_ID_ROUTES` at module import time (badgeEndpoint.ts l40-42), so setting `process.env.BADGE_ALLOW_DIRECT_DISCORD_ID_ROUTES = 'true'` inside the test (l141) has no effect on the already-loaded module — the test's own comment (l142-145) admits this. The request it then issues, `/badges/movie-tier-1.svg`, is served by `tryServeRegistryBadge` because a matching manifest entry was seeded (l147-148); that branch returns 200 regardless of the direct-ID flag. So the assertion `expect(r.status).toBe(200)` (l151) passes via the registry path, not the direct-ID-enabled path. The genuinely flag-gated code (badgeEndpoint.ts l163-187, the `/badges/(roles|channels|users)/<id>.svg` branch and its enabled behavior) is therefore never tested. Impact: false confidence — a regression that broke direct-ID-route serving when the env flag is on would not be caught by this test.
fix: Make the flag injectable so it can be toggled per-test (e.g. read `process.env` at call time inside handleBadgeRequest, or thread an `allowDirectIdRoutes` option through `BadgeStoreConfig`), then assert against a real `/badges/roles/<digits>.svg` request returning a rendered badge (200 + image/svg+xml) when enabled and 404 `direct_id_routes_disabled` when disabled.

title: "timestamp is NaN" test does not exercise the NaN guard it claims to cover
detail: The test builds its body as `{ ...validEvent, timestamp: NaN }` (the `body` path, not `rawBody`). makeEvent serializes it via JSON.stringify, and JSON.stringify converts NaN to `null` (verified: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify({timestamp:NaN})).timestamp === null, typeof === 'object'). So by the time the handler (web/src/routes/api/internal/events/+server.ts) parses the body, `event.timestamp` is null. The handler returns 400 via the `typeof event.timestamp !== "number"` branch (line 67) — the same branch the "timestamp is not a finite number" test ('yesterday' string) already covers. The dedicated `!Number.isFinite(event.timestamp)` guard (line 68) therefore has ZERO test coverage from this suite: no test ever feeds the handler a value that is a number but non-finite. A regression that deletes the `!Number.isFinite(...)` check (e.g. allowing Infinity, which a buggy bot serializer or a non-JSON caller could send) would not be caught. The test passes, giving false confidence.
fix: Drive the handler with a raw body so NaN/Infinity survive to the parser, e.g. `evt({ secret: SECRET, rawBody: JSON.stringify({...validEvent, timestamp: 1}).replace('1','Infinity') })` or post a literal `{"type":"x:y","timestamp":Infinity,"payload":{}}` as rawBody (note: invalid JSON, so instead inject via a number that bypasses stringify). Simplest: add a case that posts rawBody `'{"type":"x:y","payload":{},"timestamp":1e999}'` (1e999 parses to Infinity) and assert 400; that actually exercises the Number.isFinite branch.

title: navigator.clipboard.writeText promise not awaited — shows false 'Copied!' on failure
detail: copy() calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(value)` without awaiting or catching the returned promise, then unconditionally sets `copied = true` and shows the 'Copied!' toast (lines 11-14, 27). clipboard.writeText rejects in insecure contexts (non-HTTPS), when the document is not focused, or when permission is denied. In those cases the value is NOT on the clipboard yet the UI reports success, and the unhandled rejection surfaces as an uncaught promise error. For a copy-the-Discord-ID affordance used throughout the review/config UI, the user is misled into thinking the ID was copied.
fix: Make copy() async and gate the success UI on the resolved promise: `try { await navigator.clipboard.writeText(value); copied = true; ... } catch { /* show failure or fallback to execCommand */ }`. Also guard for `navigator.clipboard` being undefined.

title: Flat (no-change) delta emits the green UP-vote emoji in the copied newsletter
detail: In numDelta (line 36-37) and pctDelta (line 50-51) the `direction` is computed as `abs > 0 ? 'up' : abs < 0 ? 'down' : 'flat'`, but the `emoji` is computed as `abs >= 0 ? UP_EMOJI : DOWN_EMOJI`. When the current and previous values are equal and non-zero (the `prev===0 && cur===0` early-returns do not fire), `abs === 0`, so `direction` is correctly 'flat' but `emoji` is UP_EMOJI. The Discord markdown builder (discordMarkdown, lines 76 and 92-102) unconditionally prints `d.X.emoji` next to the percentage, so a metric that did not change week-over-week renders a green up-vote (<:Iup_Vote:...>) beside a '+0.0%' line. The text copied for the public newsletter therefore signals growth where there was none.
fix: Derive the emoji from `direction` instead of the `>= 0` sign, e.g. `emoji: direction === 'down' ? DOWN_EMOJI : direction === 'up' ? UP_EMOJI : NEUTRAL_EMOJI` (or reuse UP only for true 'up'). At minimum compute emoji from the already-correct `direction` value so flat never maps to the up emoji.

title: fmtDayShort returns 'undefined D' for an out-of-range month instead of falling back to the raw string
detail: fmtDayShort guards against a non-3-part string and against m/d being 0 or NaN (`if (!m || !d) return day`), but does not bound-check m to 1..12. For an input like '2025-13-05' (or any month > 12), `months[m-1]` is undefined and the function returns the string 'undefined 5'. Inputs come from DB day/week buckets so this is unlikely in practice, but a malformed or off-by-one bucket value would render literal 'undefined' in the Observatory axis/labels (DivergingBars, LineChart, QotdFunnel all call it) rather than degrading to the raw value like the other guard paths do.
fix: Add a range check: `if (m < 1 || m > 12 || d < 1 || d > 31) return day;` before indexing months, so any out-of-range value falls back to the raw `day` string consistent with the existing guards.

title: Case-insensitive handbook href rewrite is effectively case-sensitive; mixed-case .md links 404
detail: rewriteHandbookHref() looks up the slug via HANDBOOK_FILENAME_TO_SLUG[filename] ?? [filename.toUpperCase()] ?? [filename.toLowerCase()]. The map keys store a lowercase extension (e.g. 'BOT-HANDBOOK.md', 'TICKET-SYSTEM-GUIDE.md'). filename.toUpperCase() converts 'bot-handbook.md' into 'BOT-HANDBOOK.MD' (extension uppercased too), which does NOT match the key 'BOT-HANDBOOK.md', and filename.toLowerCase() yields 'bot-handbook.md' which also does not match an uppercase-prefixed key. So the two fallbacks are dead for every key except the all-lowercase one ('slash-commands.md'). A cross-reference href written with any non-canonical casing (e.g. 'Bot-Handbook.md' or 'bot-handbook.MD') falls through all three lookups and is returned unmodified, so the rendered link points at a raw '.md' path that 404s instead of '/handbook/<slug>'. The comment explicitly promises 'Case-insensitive lookup', so behavior contradicts intent.
fix: Normalize once and compare against a normalized map, e.g. build a lowercase-keyed index: `const byLower = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(HANDBOOK_FILENAME_TO_SLUG).map(([k,v])=>[k.toLowerCase(),v]));` then `const slug = byLower[filename.toLowerCase()];`. This makes the lookup truly case-insensitive across the whole filename including extension.

title: Cleanup interval is never unref'd or cleared (inconsistent with every other scheduler/limiter)
detail: `setInterval(cleanupOldCooldowns, CLEANUP_INTERVAL_MS)` at module load is neither stored, `.unref()`'d, nor cleared on shutdown. Every other interval in this codebase (notifyLimiter, traceStore, all src/scheduler/* schedulers, badge live updates, dmVerification, movieNight) is explicitly `.unref()`'d and most expose a stop/destroy. The code comment even acknowledges 'This interval is never cleared'. Functional impact in production is small because gracefulShutdown calls `process.exit(0)` explicitly, but: (a) it keeps the event loop alive, so if the explicit exit path is ever bypassed the process will not exit on its own; and (b) it leaks the timer in tests/embedding scenarios that import this module (the very hang the comment warns about). It is the one outlier from an otherwise consistent, leak-safe pattern.
fix: Capture the handle (`const cleanupTimer = setInterval(...)`), call `cleanupTimer.unref()`, and export a `stopRateLimiterCleanup()` that does `clearInterval`. Optionally wire that into the gracefulShutdown cleanup block in src/startup/ready.ts alongside the other limiter teardowns.

title: Wide-event Response State is inaccurate for handlers that defer/reply directly instead of via cmdWrap helpers
detail: markDeferred() is only emitted inside ensureDeferred() and markReplied() only inside replyOrEdit(). The large majority of component/modal handlers call interaction.deferUpdate()/deferReply()/update()/reply()/editReply() DIRECTLY (e.g. byteTokenHandler, artistRotation/handlers, modmail/handlers, qotd/handlers, tickets/handlers, dmVerification). For those flows the wide event's responseState.deferredAt/repliedAt stay null, so the error card's 'Response State' section (errorCardV2.ts:288-325) reports 'Deferred: No (direct reply or error before defer)' and 'Replied: No' even though the user definitely received a response. This degrades the exact debugging signal the wide-event system was built to provide ('did the user see anything?').
fix: Either funnel direct defer/reply calls through the cmdWrap helpers, or add lightweight enrichEvent(e=>e.markDeferred()/markReplied()) calls in the shared handler entry points, so response-state telemetry reflects reality.

title: streamReviewActionsCSV export is dead (only consumer is dead command.ts)
detail: csv.ts exports two functions: generateModHistoryCsv (used by the live src/commands/stats/history.ts) and streamReviewActionsCSV. streamReviewActionsCSV is imported only by the dead src/features/analytics/command.ts (line 37) and tests/lib/csv.test.ts. Once command.ts is removed, streamReviewActionsCSV becomes a dead export inside an otherwise-live file. Side note: the inline comment at csv.ts:43-49 claims RFC4180 quoting 'prevents CSV injection attacks where =,+,-,@ could trigger formula execution' — that is false (Excel still evaluates =cmd inside a quoted field); but since this exporter is dead the claim has no runtime impact.
fix: Remove streamReviewActionsCSV (and CSVExportOptions if it becomes unused) from src/lib/csv.ts when deleting command.ts, keeping generateModHistoryCsv. Separately, do not propagate the misleading CSV-injection comment into the live generateModHistoryCsv.

title: Dead prefix clause for v1:avatar:confirm18 modals in the router guard
detail: The modal dispatch guard `if (customId.startsWith("v1:modal:") || customId.startsWith("v1:avatar:confirm18:"))` includes the second clause solely for the avatar_confirm18 route. Since no modal with that customId is ever shown (see modalPatterns.ts finding) and there is no handler branch inside the block for it, the clause only serves to route such an ID into the block where it immediately hits the catch-all 'Unhandled modal' error card. The clause is effectively dead and misleading.
fix: Drop the `|| customId.startsWith("v1:avatar:confirm18:")` clause (coordinated with removing MODAL_18_RE), or implement the avatar_confirm18 handler if the feature is meant to ship.

title: fireAndForget helper is never used anywhere
detail: fireAndForget(promise, label) was added to 'replace the .catch(() => {}) anti-pattern throughout the codebase' (per its own JSDoc), but a repo-wide search of src/, scripts/, web/, workers/, and tests/ finds zero importers or call sites — only the definition itself. The codebase still uses inline .catch(() => undefined)/.catch(err => logger.warn(...)) (e.g. throughout interactionCreate.ts and movie.ts), so the intended adoption never happened. Dead utility module.
fix: Either delete src/lib/fireAndForget.ts, or actually adopt it by replacing the scattered fire-and-forget .catch patterns with fireAndForget(...). Prefer deletion unless adoption is planned.

title: commandSync.ts is an empty module husk with no exports
detail: After syncGuildCommandsInProcess() and its helpers were removed (v4.4.5, per the file's own comment), the file was 'retained for potential future command sync utilities' but now contains only comments — no code, no exports. Nothing imports it (repo-wide search finds only the file itself). It is a zero-value placeholder that shows up as a source module and in import-graph tooling.
fix: Delete src/lib/commandSync.ts. Re-create it later if/when real command-sync helpers are actually needed; an empty placeholder file adds noise without value.

title: Modmail thread list runs 2 correlated subqueries per row and is recomputed on every modmail navigation (uncached)
detail: getModmailThreads() (called uncached from dashboard/modmail/+layout.server.ts:13 on every navigation) selects, per ticket row, two correlated subqueries that each re-scan modmail_message for the same ticket ordered by created_at DESC LIMIT 1 (latest_message at 55-56, latest_direction at 57-58) in addition to the LEFT JOIN+GROUP BY used for message_count. That is two redundant ordered lookups per ticket on top of the aggregate; both pull the same 'latest row'. Bounded by LIMIT 50 so impact is modest, but it is pure repeated work executed on every layout load.
fix: Fetch the latest message once per ticket via a window function (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ticket_id ORDER BY created_at DESC)) joined to the ticket aggregate, returning content+direction in a single pass. Optionally wrap in cached() with a short TTL.

title: Periodic Patreon role-dedup sweep interval is never unref'd and has no stop function (only un-cleanable long-lived interval in the bot)
detail: sweepPatreonRoleStacks() creates a periodic 10-minute setInterval (line 178) but, unlike every other recurring timer in the bot process, it (a) does NOT call .unref() and (b) does not store the handle anywhere, so there is no way to clearInterval it. Cross-file impact: the entire shutdown contract in src/startup/ready.ts -> gracefulShutdown and src/startup/schedulers.ts -> stopSchedulers() assumes every recurring job is either unref'd or has a stopX() that is called during SIGTERM/SIGINT. Every scheduler (byteMultiplier, securityAudit, staleApplication, modMetrics, guildSnapshot, opsHealth, diskSpace, eventTimeout, badgeRefresh) and every feature timer (movieNight/gameNight persistence, dmVerification cleanup, modmail forwardedMessages cleanup, interactionCreate dedup, traceStore prune, notifyLimiter) follows that pattern. This one does not: there is no stopPatreonRoleDedup() anywhere in the source (verified by grep), and ready.ts never tears it down. Concrete impact is limited because the sweep callback is async and idle-cheap and gracefulShutdown ultimately calls process.exit(0), which terminates regardless. But the un-unref'd ref-counted timer means this module alone can keep Node's event loop alive (delaying a clean, signal-less exit), and it is uncancellable in tests/embeds (no opt-out, no handle), forcing test harnesses to either rely on process.exit or hang. It is the single defensible deviation from an otherwise airtight resource-cleanup convention.
fix: Match the established pattern: store the handle in a module-level let (e.g. let sweepInterval: NodeJS.Timeout | null), call sweepInterval.unref() right after creation, and export a stopPatreonRoleDedup() that clears it; then call that from the gracefulShutdown feature-cleanup section in src/startup/ready.ts alongside the other cleanups. Minimal fix if a stop hook is not wanted: append .unref() to the setInterval(...) call at line 178 (mirrors src/events/interactionCreate.ts:80 and src/features/modmail/routing.ts:144).

title: Remote migration wrapper exits 0 when the migration child is killed by a signal
detail: spawnSync runs scripts/migrate.ts and then `process.exit(result.status || 0)`. When the child process is terminated by a signal rather than a normal exit (OOM kill, SIGTERM during deploy), spawnSync sets `result.status` to null and `result.signal` to the signal name. `null || 0` evaluates to 0, so this wrapper reports SUCCESS even though the migration was killed mid-run. A deploy script keying off this exit code would proceed as if migrations completed. (A normal migration failure is fine: migrate.ts exits 1, status=1, 1||0=1.)
fix: Treat signal death and null status as failure: `if (result.status === null) process.exit(1); process.exit(result.status);` (or `process.exit(result.status ?? 1)` and also check result.signal/result.error).

title: Modmail context-menu defers and replies PUBLICLY, unlike the button path which keeps failures ephemeral
detail: handleModmailContextMenu calls interaction.deferReply() with no MessageFlags.Ephemeral (line 190) and then interaction.editReply({content: result.message}) (line 239), so both the 'Bot is thinking…' state and the final outcome message (including failure strings like 'Failed to create modmail thread. Check bot permissions.') are PUBLIC in whatever channel the staffer right-clicked a message in. The sibling button handler handleModmailOpenButton deliberately keeps the failure path ephemeral (followUp with flags:Ephemeral, lines 125-131) and only posts success publicly. The inline comment at line 188 ('Context menus don't support deferUpdate, so we use deferReply') justifies the deferReply but not the missing Ephemeral flag. Impact: a permission/setup failure when opening modmail from a context menu is broadcast to the channel rather than shown privately to the acting moderator, and the public 'thinking' bubble appears in a potentially user-visible channel.
fix: Pass flags: MessageFlags.Ephemeral to deferReply() in handleModmailContextMenu so the staffer's interaction matches the ephemeral semantics of the button path; post the public 'thread created' confirmation via interaction.channel.send (as the button path does) instead of via the public editReply.

title: review/index.ts is a fully unused duplicate barrel; the live back-compat barrel is review.ts
detail: There are two barrels for the review module: src/features/review.ts (128 lines) and src/features/review/index.ts (113 lines). Both headers claim to provide 'backwards compatibility with imports from ./features/review.js'. Only review.ts is actually imported (e.g. gateMain.ts:30 renderWelcomeTemplate, web/routes/review.ts:23 ensureReviewMessage). review/index.ts would only be reached via an import from '...features/review' with no further path segment, and grep for that exact pattern (from '<...>features/review') returns ZERO matches across src/web/scripts/tests. It contains only re-exports (no side effects), so it is pure dead source. Its re-exports of DEFAULT_WELCOME_TEMPLATE and buildWelcomeNotice are doubly dead -- those symbols are also re-exported by review.ts and used only internally inside review/welcome.ts.
fix: Delete src/features/review/index.ts. Keep src/features/review.ts (the one consumers actually import). If a directory-style barrel is desired long-term, consolidate to one and update review.ts importers, but do not keep both.

title: archiveMessageRowSync / archiveReactionRowsSync are dead; 'used by backfill' comment is false
detail: Both functions are exported with the comment 'Direct synchronous insert used by backfill (bypasses buffer).' But the only importer of messageArchive is src/events/guildEvents.ts via 'import * as archive', and that namespace only ever accesses archive.archiveMessage, markMessageDeleted, recordReaction, removeReaction (verified by listing archive.* member access). Neither *RowSync function is referenced anywhere in src/scripts/tests/web (verified by name grep, no dynamic/string refs). The backfill command (commands/backfill.ts) contains no 'archive' reference at all. So these are dead exports with a misleading comment that implies a live consumer that does not exist.
fix: Remove archiveMessageRowSync and archiveReactionRowsSync (and the ArchiveRow/ReactionRow plumbing if it becomes unused), or actually wire them into the backfill path the comment references. Confirm backfill genuinely does not need synchronous inserts first.

title: pruneOldMessages() exported but never called -> message_activity retention never enforced
detail: pruneOldMessages(guildId, daysToKeep=90) is exported but has zero references outside its own file (verified across src/tests/scripts/web, no dynamic refs). This is a retention/cleanup function for the message_activity table that nothing schedules or invokes, so old message-activity rows are never pruned. Low severity as dead code, but note the latent operational consequence: unbounded growth of message_activity (consistent with the 5GB data.db observed).
fix: Either schedule pruneOldMessages from a periodic task (e.g. the scheduler used for other maintenance) so retention actually happens, or delete it if retention is intentionally handled elsewhere. Do not leave it as an exported no-op.

title: getAllActiveMultipliers() exported but never used
detail: getAllActiveMultipliers (byteMultiplierStore.ts:231), backed by the getAllActiveMultipliersStmt prepared statement (line 99), is exported but referenced nowhere outside its own file (verified; no dynamic refs). Dead read-side API. The prepared statement is initialized at module load regardless, so it is wasted work, though negligible.

title: clearAllRulesCache() exported but never called
detail: clearAllRulesCache (rulesCache.ts:68) has no references outside its own file (verified across src/tests/scripts/web, no dynamic refs). It is a cache-invalidation helper that nothing triggers, so the rules cache is only ever invalidated by whatever per-entry mechanism exists (if any) and never globally. Dead export.

title: traceStore clearTraces() and stopAutoPrune() are dead (clearTraces comment claims 'for testing' but no test uses it)
detail: clearTraces (traceStore.ts:118, documented 'Clear all traces (for testing)') and stopAutoPrune (traceStore.ts:135) are exported but never imported anywhere, including tests (verified). startAutoPrune is auto-invoked at module load (line 143) and pruneExpired is used internally by it, so only the externally-facing teardown/test hooks are dead. Harmless but the 'for testing' comment is misleading since no test exercises it.
fix: Either add a test that uses clearTraces (justifying the comment) or remove clearTraces and stopAutoPrune. Keep startAutoPrune/pruneExpired (live).

title: getHeatmapData() is a dead wrapper superseded by getHeatmapDataForRange()
detail: getHeatmapData(guildId, weeks=1) at heatmap.ts:197 is a thin wrapper whose own docstring (line 195) says callers should 'use getHeatmapDataForRange directly.' The live route web/src/routes/dashboard/heatmap/+page.server.ts:3,21 imports and uses getHeatmapDataForRange, not getHeatmapData. getHeatmapData has no other references (verified). Dead superseded wrapper.

title: detectNsfwFlagSurge filters nsfw_flags.flagged_at via strftime(), bypassing the guild/reviewed index
detail: detectNsfwFlagSurge runs two counts of the form `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM nsfw_flags WHERE guild_id = ? AND strftime('%s', flagged_at) >= ? AND strftime('%s', flagged_at) < ?`. nsfw_flags.flagged_at is declared `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))` (migrations/032_nsfw_flags.ts:45) and the only indexes are idx_nsfw_flags_guild(guild_id) and idx_nsfw_flags_pending(guild_id, reviewed) (lines 53-54). Wrapping flagged_at in strftime() makes the time bound non-sargable, so after the guild_id prefix narrows the set SQLite still scans every flag row for that guild and recomputes strftime per row. Bounded in practice: nsfw_flags has UNIQUE(guild_id, user_id) so row count is capped near member count, and the Pulse bundle is cached. Real but low impact.
fix: Compare flagged_at as a raw ISO string against JS-computed ISO bounds (`flagged_at >= ?`) so an index on nsfw_flags(guild_id, flagged_at) can seek, or store flagged_at as unix-seconds INTEGER. Mirrors the modmail fix.

title: Live presence (Currently Online / In Voice Now) is bundled into the 60s range-keyed pulse cache
detail: getGuildSnapshot(guildId) (online_count, voice_users_now) is real-time presence that does not depend on the selected time window, but it is computed inside the same cached(guildKey, CACHE_TTL.medium=60_000, ...) object whose key is rangeCacheKeyParts(range,60). Consequences: (1) the UI labels these cards 'live from Discord' / 'connected to voice', yet they are stale by up to ~60s and only refresh when the minute bucket rolls or the user changes the window; (2) switching the time window pointlessly recomputes the snapshot since it shares the range-scoped key. This is a correctness/accuracy mismatch between the 'live' presentation and the caching.
fix: Pull getGuildSnapshot out of the range-keyed bundle and cache it under a window-independent key with a short TTL (e.g. CACHE_TTL.short or no cache), keyed only by guildId, so presence reflects near-real-time state regardless of the selected window.
